kjv.1:1: The proverbs of Solomon the son of David, king of Israel;
kjv.1:2: To know wisdom and instruction; to perceive the words of understanding;
kjv.1:3: To receive the instruction of wisdom, justice, and judgment, and equity;
kjv.1:4: To give subtilty to the simple, to the young man knowledge and discretion.
kjv.1:5: A wise [man] will hear, and will increase learning; and a man of understanding shall attain unto wise counsels:
kjv.1:6: To understand a proverb, and the interpretation; the words of the wise, and their dark sayings.
kjv.1:7: The fear of the LORD [is] the beginning of knowledge: [but] fools despise wisdom and instruction.
kjv.1:8: My son, hear the instruction of thy father, and forsake not the law of thy mother:
kjv.1:9: For they [shall be] an ornament of grace unto thy head, and chains about thy neck.
kjv.1:10: My son, if sinners entice thee, consent thou not.
kjv.1:11: If they say, Come with us, let us lay wait for blood, let us lurk privily for the innocent without cause:
kjv.1:12: Let us swallow them up alive as the grave; and whole, as those that go down into the pit:
kjv.1:13: We shall find all precious substance, we shall fill our houses with spoil:
kjv.1:14: Cast in thy lot among us; let us all have one purse:
kjv.1:15: My son, walk not thou in the way with them; refrain thy foot from their path:
kjv.1:16: For their feet run to evil, and make haste to shed blood.
kjv.1:17: Surely in vain the net is spread in the sight of any bird.
kjv.1:18: And they lay wait for their [own] blood; they lurk privily for their [own] lives.
kjv.1:19: So [are] the ways of every one that is greedy of gain; [which] taketh away the life of the owners thereof.
kjv.1:20: Wisdom crieth without; she uttereth her voice in the streets:
kjv.1:21: She crieth in the chief place of concourse, in the openings of the gates: in the city she uttereth her words, [saying],
kjv.1:22: How long, ye simple ones, will ye love simplicity? and the scorners delight in their scorning, and fools hate knowledge?
kjv.1:23: Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you.
kjv.1:24: Because I have called, and ye refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no man regarded;
kjv.1:25: But ye have set at nought all my counsel, and would none of my reproof:
kjv.1:26: I also will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when your fear cometh;
kjv.1:27: When your fear cometh as desolation, and your destruction cometh as a whirlwind; when distress and anguish cometh upon you.
kjv.1:28: Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me:
kjv.1:29: For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the LORD:
kjv.1:30: They would none of my counsel: they despised all my reproof.
kjv.1:31: Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own devices.
kjv.1:32: For the turning away of the simple shall slay them, and the prosperity of fools shall destroy them.
kjv.1:33: But whoso hearkeneth unto me shall dwell safely, and shall be quiet from fear of evil.
kjv.2:1: My son, if thou wilt receive my words, and hide my commandments with thee;
kjv.2:2: So that thou incline thine ear unto wisdom, [and] apply thine heart to understanding;
kjv.2:3: Yea, if thou criest after knowledge, [and] liftest up thy voice for understanding;
kjv.2:4: If thou seekest her as silver, and searchest for her as [for] hid treasures;
kjv.2:5: Then shalt thou understand the fear of the LORD, and find the knowledge of God.
kjv.2:6: For the LORD giveth wisdom: out of his mouth [cometh] knowledge and understanding.
kjv.2:7: He layeth up sound wisdom for the righteous: [he is] a buckler to them that walk uprightly.
kjv.2:8: He keepeth the paths of judgment, and preserveth the way of his saints.
kjv.2:9: Then shalt thou understand righteousness, and judgment, and equity; [yea], every good path.
kjv.2:10: When wisdom entereth into thine heart, and knowledge is pleasant unto thy soul;
kjv.2:11: Discretion shall preserve thee, understanding shall keep thee:
kjv.2:12: To deliver thee from the way of the evil [man], from the man that speaketh froward things;
kjv.2:13: Who leave the paths of uprightness, to walk in the ways of darkness;
kjv.2:14: Who rejoice to do evil, [and] delight in the frowardness of the wicked;
kjv.2:15: Whose ways [are] crooked, and [they] froward in their paths:
kjv.2:16: To deliver thee from the strange woman, [even] from the stranger [which] flattereth with her words;
kjv.2:17: Which forsaketh the guide of her youth, and forgetteth the covenant of her God.
kjv.2:18: For her house inclineth unto death, and her paths unto the dead.
kjv.2:19: None that go unto her return again, neither take they hold of the paths of life.
kjv.2:20: That thou mayest walk in the way of good [men], and keep the paths of the righteous.
kjv.2:21: For the upright shall dwell in the land, and the perfect shall remain in it.
kjv.2:22: But the wicked shall be cut off from the earth, and the transgressors shall be rooted out of it.
kjv.3:1: My son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments:
kjv.3:2: For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee.
kjv.3:3: Let not mercy and truth forsake thee: bind them about thy neck; write them upon the table of thine heart:
kjv.3:4: So shalt thou find favour and good understanding in the sight of God and man.
kjv.3:5: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.
kjv.3:6: In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
kjv.3:7: Be not wise in thine own eyes: fear the LORD, and depart from evil.
kjv.3:8: It shall be health to thy navel, and marrow to thy bones.
kjv.3:9: Honour the LORD with thy substance, and with the firstfruits of all thine increase:
kjv.3:10: So shall thy barns be filled with plenty, and thy presses shall burst out with new wine.
kjv.3:11: My son, despise not the chastening of the LORD; neither be weary of his correction:
kjv.3:12: For whom the LORD loveth he correcteth; even as a father the son [in whom] he delighteth.
kjv.3:13: Happy [is] the man [that] findeth wisdom, and the man [that] getteth understanding.
kjv.3:14: For the merchandise of it [is] better than the merchandise of silver, and the gain thereof than fine gold.
kjv.3:15: She [is] more precious than rubies: and all the things thou canst desire are not to be compared unto her.
kjv.3:16: Length of days [is] in her right hand; [and] in her left hand riches and honour.
kjv.3:17: Her ways [are] ways of pleasantness, and all her paths [are] peace.
kjv.3:18: She [is] a tree of life to them that lay hold upon her: and happy [is every one] that retaineth her.
kjv.3:19: The LORD by wisdom hath founded the earth; by understanding hath he established the heavens.
kjv.3:20: By his knowledge the depths are broken up, and the clouds drop down the dew.
kjv.3:21: My son, let not them depart from thine eyes: keep sound wisdom and discretion:
kjv.3:22: So shall they be life unto thy soul, and grace to thy neck.
kjv.3:23: Then shalt thou walk in thy way safely, and thy foot shall not stumble.
kjv.3:24: When thou liest down, thou shalt not be afraid: yea, thou shalt lie down, and thy sleep shall be sweet.
kjv.3:25: Be not afraid of sudden fear, neither of the desolation of the wicked, when it cometh.
kjv.3:26: For the LORD shall be thy confidence, and shall keep thy foot from being taken.
kjv.3:27: Withhold not good from them to whom it is due, when it is in the power of thine hand to do [it].
kjv.3:28: Say not unto thy neighbour, Go, and come again, and to morrow I will give; when thou hast it by thee.
kjv.3:29: Devise not evil against thy neighbour, seeing he dwelleth securely by thee.
kjv.3:30: Strive not with a man without cause, if he have done thee no harm.
kjv.3:31: Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.
kjv.3:32: For the froward [is] abomination to the LORD: but his secret [is] with the righteous.
kjv.3:33: The curse of the LORD [is] in the house of the wicked: but he blesseth the habitation of the just.
kjv.3:34: Surely he scorneth the scorners: but he giveth grace unto the lowly.
kjv.3:35: The wise shall inherit glory: but shame shall be the promotion of fools.
kjv.4:1: Hear, ye children, the instruction of a father, and attend to know understanding.
kjv.4:2: For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law.
kjv.4:3: For I was my father's son, tender and only [beloved] in the sight of my mother.
kjv.4:4: He taught me also, and said unto me, Let thine heart retain my words: keep my commandments, and live.
kjv.4:5: Get wisdom, get understanding: forget [it] not; neither decline from the words of my mouth.
kjv.4:6: Forsake her not, and she shall preserve thee: love her, and she shall keep thee.
kjv.4:7: Wisdom [is] the principal thing; [therefore] get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.
kjv.4:8: Exalt her, and she shall promote thee: she shall bring thee to honour, when thou dost embrace her.
kjv.4:9: She shall give to thine head an ornament of grace: a crown of glory shall she deliver to thee.
kjv.4:10: Hear, O my son, and receive my sayings; and the years of thy life shall be many.
kjv.4:11: I have taught thee in the way of wisdom; I have led thee in right paths.
kjv.4:12: When thou goest, thy steps shall not be straitened; and when thou runnest, thou shalt not stumble.
kjv.4:13: Take fast hold of instruction; let [her] not go: keep her; for she [is] thy life.
kjv.4:14: Enter not into the path of the wicked, and go not in the way of evil [men].
kjv.4:15: Avoid it, pass not by it, turn from it, and pass away.
kjv.4:16: For they sleep not, except they have done mischief; and their sleep is taken away, unless they cause [some] to fall.
kjv.4:17: For they eat the bread of wickedness, and drink the wine of violence.
kjv.4:18: But the path of the just [is] as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day.
kjv.4:19: The way of the wicked [is] as darkness: they know not at what they stumble.
kjv.4:20: My son, attend to my words; incline thine ear unto my sayings.
kjv.4:21: Let them not depart from thine eyes; keep them in the midst of thine heart.
kjv.4:22: For they [are] life unto those that find them, and health to all their flesh.
kjv.4:23: Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it [are] the issues of life.
kjv.4:24: Put away from thee a froward mouth, and perverse lips put far from thee.
kjv.4:25: Let thine eyes look right on, and let thine eyelids look straight before thee.
kjv.4:26: Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be established.
kjv.4:27: Turn not to the right hand nor to the left: remove thy foot from evil.
kjv.5:1: My son, attend unto my wisdom, [and] bow thine ear to my understanding:
kjv.5:2: That thou mayest regard discretion, and [that] thy lips may keep knowledge.
kjv.5:3: For the lips of a strange woman drop [as] an honeycomb, and her mouth [is] smoother than oil:
kjv.5:4: But her end is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a twoedged sword.
kjv.5:5: Her feet go down to death; her steps take hold on hell.
kjv.5:6: Lest thou shouldest ponder the path of life, her ways are moveable, [that] thou canst not know [them].
kjv.5:7: Hear me now therefore, O ye children, and depart not from the words of my mouth.
kjv.5:8: Remove thy way far from her, and come not nigh the door of her house:
kjv.5:9: Lest thou give thine honour unto others, and thy years unto the cruel:
kjv.5:10: Lest strangers be filled with thy wealth; and thy labours [be] in the house of a stranger;
kjv.5:11: And thou mourn at the last, when thy flesh and thy body are consumed,
kjv.5:12: And say, How have I hated instruction, and my heart despised reproof;
kjv.5:13: And have not obeyed the voice of my teachers, nor inclined mine ear to them that instructed me!
kjv.5:14: I was almost in all evil in the midst of the congregation and assembly.
kjv.5:15: Drink waters out of thine own cistern, and running waters out of thine own well.
kjv.5:16: Let thy fountains be dispersed abroad, [and] rivers of waters in the streets.
kjv.5:17: Let them be only thine own, and not strangers' with thee.
kjv.5:18: Let thy fountain be blessed: and rejoice with the wife of thy youth.
kjv.5:19: [Let her be as] the loving hind and pleasant roe; let her breasts satisfy thee at all times; and be thou ravished always with her love.
kjv.5:20: And why wilt thou, my son, be ravished with a strange woman, and embrace the bosom of a stranger?
kjv.5:21: For the ways of man [are] before the eyes of the LORD, and he pondereth all his goings.
kjv.5:22: His own iniquities shall take the wicked himself, and he shall be holden with the cords of his sins.
kjv.5:23: He shall die without instruction; and in the greatness of his folly he shall go astray.
kjv.6:1: My son, if thou be surety for thy friend, [if] thou hast stricken thy hand with a stranger,
kjv.6:2: Thou art snared with the words of thy mouth, thou art taken with the words of thy mouth.
kjv.6:3: Do this now, my son, and deliver thyself, when thou art come into the hand of thy friend; go, humble thyself, and make sure thy friend.
kjv.6:4: Give not sleep to thine eyes, nor slumber to thine eyelids.
kjv.6:5: Deliver thyself as a roe from the hand [of the hunter], and as a bird from the hand of the fowler.
kjv.6:6: Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise:
kjv.6:7: Which having no guide, overseer, or ruler,
kjv.6:8: Provideth her meat in the summer, [and] gathereth her food in the harvest.
kjv.6:9: How long wilt thou sleep, O sluggard? when wilt thou arise out of thy sleep?
kjv.6:10: [Yet] a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep:
kjv.6:11: So shall thy poverty come as one that travelleth, and thy want as an armed man.
kjv.6:12: A naughty person, a wicked man, walketh with a froward mouth.
kjv.6:13: He winketh with his eyes, he speaketh with his feet, he teacheth with his fingers;
kjv.6:14: Frowardness [is] in his heart, he deviseth mischief continually; he soweth discord.
kjv.6:15: Therefore shall his calamity come suddenly; suddenly shall he be broken without remedy.
kjv.6:16: These six [things] doth the LORD hate: yea, seven [are] an abomination unto him:
kjv.6:17: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood,
kjv.6:18: An heart that deviseth wicked imaginations, feet that be swift in running to mischief,
kjv.6:19: A false witness [that] speaketh lies, and he that soweth discord among brethren.
kjv.6:20: My son, keep thy father's commandment, and forsake not the law of thy mother:
kjv.6:21: Bind them continually upon thine heart, [and] tie them about thy neck.
kjv.6:22: When thou goest, it shall lead thee; when thou sleepest, it shall keep thee; and [when] thou awakest, it shall talk with thee.
kjv.6:23: For the commandment [is] a lamp; and the law [is] light; and reproofs of instruction [are] the way of life:
kjv.6:24: To keep thee from the evil woman, from the flattery of the tongue of a strange woman.
kjv.6:25: Lust not after her beauty in thine heart; neither let her take thee with her eyelids.
kjv.6:26: For by means of a whorish woman [a man is brought] to a piece of bread: and the adulteress will hunt for the precious life.
kjv.6:27: Can a man take fire in his bosom, and his clothes not be burned?
kjv.6:28: Can one go upon hot coals, and his feet not be burned?
kjv.6:29: So he that goeth in to his neighbour's wife; whosoever toucheth her shall not be innocent.
kjv.6:30: [Men] do not despise a thief, if he steal to satisfy his soul when he is hungry;
kjv.6:31: But [if] he be found, he shall restore sevenfold; he shall give all the substance of his house.
kjv.6:32: [But] whoso committeth adultery with a woman lacketh understanding: he [that] doeth it destroyeth his own soul.
kjv.6:33: A wound and dishonour shall he get; and his reproach shall not be wiped away.
kjv.6:34: For jealousy [is] the rage of a man: therefore he will not spare in the day of vengeance.
kjv.6:35: He will not regard any ransom; neither will he rest content, though thou givest many gifts.
kjv.7:1: My son, keep my words, and lay up my commandments with thee.
kjv.7:2: Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.
kjv.7:3: Bind them upon thy fingers, write them upon the table of thine heart.
kjv.7:4: Say unto wisdom, Thou [art] my sister; and call understanding [thy] kinswoman:
kjv.7:5: That they may keep thee from the strange woman, from the stranger [which] flattereth with her words.
kjv.7:6: For at the window of my house I looked through my casement,
kjv.7:7: And beheld among the simple ones, I discerned among the youths, a young man void of understanding,
kjv.7:8: Passing through the street near her corner; and he went the way to her house,
kjv.7:9: In the twilight, in the evening, in the black and dark night:
kjv.7:10: And, behold, there met him a woman [with] the attire of an harlot, and subtil of heart.
kjv.7:11: (She [is] loud and stubborn; her feet abide not in her house:
kjv.7:12: Now [is she] without, now in the streets, and lieth in wait at every corner.)
kjv.7:13: So she caught him, and kissed him, [and] with an impudent face said unto him,
kjv.7:14: [I have] peace offerings with me; this day have I payed my vows.
kjv.7:15: Therefore came I forth to meet thee, diligently to seek thy face, and I have found thee.
kjv.7:16: I have decked my bed with coverings of tapestry, with carved [works], with fine linen of Egypt.
kjv.7:17: I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.
kjv.7:18: Come, let us take our fill of love until the morning: let us solace ourselves with loves.
kjv.7:19: For the goodman [is] not at home, he is gone a long journey:
kjv.7:20: He hath taken a bag of money with him, [and] will come home at the day appointed.
kjv.7:21: With her much fair speech she caused him to yield, with the flattering of her lips she forced him.
kjv.7:22: He goeth after her straightway, as an ox goeth to the slaughter, or as a fool to the correction of the stocks;
kjv.7:23: Till a dart strike through his liver; as a bird hasteth to the snare, and knoweth not that it [is] for his life.
kjv.7:24: Hearken unto me now therefore, O ye children, and attend to the words of my mouth.
kjv.7:25: Let not thine heart decline to her ways, go not astray in her paths.
kjv.7:26: For she hath cast down many wounded: yea, many strong [men] have been slain by her.
kjv.7:27: Her house [is] the way to hell, going down to the chambers of death.
kjv.8:1: Doth not wisdom cry? and understanding put forth her voice?
kjv.8:2: She standeth in the top of high places, by the way in the places of the paths.
kjv.8:3: She crieth at the gates, at the entry of the city, at the coming in at the doors.
kjv.8:4: Unto you, O men, I call; and my voice [is] to the sons of man.
kjv.8:5: O ye simple, understand wisdom: and, ye fools, be ye of an understanding heart.
kjv.8:6: Hear; for I will speak of excellent things; and the opening of my lips [shall be] right things.
kjv.8:7: For my mouth shall speak truth; and wickedness [is] an abomination to my lips.
kjv.8:8: All the words of my mouth [are] in righteousness; [there is] nothing froward or perverse in them.
kjv.8:9: They [are] all plain to him that understandeth, and right to them that find knowledge.
kjv.8:10: Receive my instruction, and not silver; and knowledge rather than choice gold.
kjv.8:11: For wisdom [is] better than rubies; and all the things that may be desired are not to be compared to it.
kjv.8:12: I wisdom dwell with prudence, and find out knowledge of witty inventions.
kjv.8:13: The fear of the LORD [is] to hate evil: pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, and the froward mouth, do I hate.
kjv.8:14: Counsel [is] mine, and sound wisdom: I [am] understanding; I have strength.
kjv.8:15: By me kings reign, and princes decree justice.
kjv.8:16: By me princes rule, and nobles, [even] all the judges of the earth.
kjv.8:17: I love them that love me; and those that seek me early shall find me.
kjv.8:18: Riches and honour [are] with me; [yea], durable riches and righteousness.
kjv.8:19: My fruit [is] better than gold, yea, than fine gold; and my revenue than choice silver.
kjv.8:20: I lead in the way of righteousness, in the midst of the paths of judgment:
kjv.8:21: That I may cause those that love me to inherit substance; and I will fill their treasures.
kjv.8:22: The LORD possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old.
kjv.8:23: I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was.
kjv.8:24: When [there were] no depths, I was brought forth; when [there were] no fountains abounding with water.
kjv.8:25: Before the mountains were settled, before the hills was I brought forth:
kjv.8:26: While as yet he had not made the earth, nor the fields, nor the highest part of the dust of the world.
kjv.8:27: When he prepared the heavens, I [was] there: when he set a compass upon the face of the depth:
kjv.8:28: When he established the clouds above: when he strengthened the fountains of the deep:
kjv.8:29: When he gave to the sea his decree, that the waters should not pass his commandment: when he appointed the foundations of the earth:
kjv.8:30: Then I was by him, [as] one brought up [with him]: and I was daily [his] delight, rejoicing always before him;
kjv.8:31: Rejoicing in the habitable part of his earth; and my delights [were] with the sons of men.
kjv.8:32: Now therefore hearken unto me, O ye children: for blessed [are they that] keep my ways.
kjv.8:33: Hear instruction, and be wise, and refuse it not.
kjv.8:34: Blessed [is] the man that heareth me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at the posts of my doors.
kjv.8:35: For whoso findeth me findeth life, and shall obtain favour of the LORD.
kjv.8:36: But he that sinneth against me wrongeth his own soul: all they that hate me love death.
kjv.9:1: Wisdom hath builded her house, she hath hewn out her seven pillars:
kjv.9:2: She hath killed her beasts; she hath mingled her wine; she hath also furnished her table.
kjv.9:3: She hath sent forth her maidens: she crieth upon the highest places of the city,
kjv.9:4: Whoso [is] simple, let him turn in hither: [as for] him that wanteth understanding, she saith to him,
kjv.9:5: Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine [which] I have mingled.
kjv.9:6: Forsake the foolish, and live; and go in the way of understanding.
kjv.9:7: He that reproveth a scorner getteth to himself shame: and he that rebuketh a wicked [man getteth] himself a blot.
kjv.9:8: Reprove not a scorner, lest he hate thee: rebuke a wise man, and he will love thee.
kjv.9:9: Give [instruction] to a wise [man], and he will be yet wiser: teach a just [man], and he will increase in learning.
kjv.9:10: The fear of the LORD [is] the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy [is] understanding.
kjv.9:11: For by me thy days shall be multiplied, and the years of thy life shall be increased.
kjv.9:12: If thou be wise, thou shalt be wise for thyself: but [if] thou scornest, thou alone shalt bear [it].
kjv.9:13: A foolish woman [is] clamorous: [she is] simple, and knoweth nothing.
kjv.9:14: For she sitteth at the door of her house, on a seat in the high places of the city,
kjv.9:15: To call passengers who go right on their ways:
kjv.9:16: Whoso [is] simple, let him turn in hither: and [as for] him that wanteth understanding, she saith to him,
kjv.9:17: Stolen waters are sweet, and bread [eaten] in secret is pleasant.
kjv.9:18: But he knoweth not that the dead [are] there; [and that] her guests [are] in the depths of hell.
kjv.10:1: The proverbs of Solomon. A wise son maketh a glad father: but a foolish son [is] the heaviness of his mother.
kjv.10:2: Treasures of wickedness profit nothing: but righteousness delivereth from death.
kjv.10:3: The LORD will not suffer the soul of the righteous to famish: but he casteth away the substance of the wicked.
kjv.10:4: He becometh poor that dealeth [with] a slack hand: but the hand of the diligent maketh rich.
kjv.10:5: He that gathereth in summer [is] a wise son: [but] he that sleepeth in harvest [is] a son that causeth shame.
kjv.10:6: Blessings [are] upon the head of the just: but violence covereth the mouth of the wicked.
kjv.10:7: The memory of the just [is] blessed: but the name of the wicked shall rot.
kjv.10:8: The wise in heart will receive commandments: but a prating fool shall fall.
kjv.10:9: He that walketh uprightly walketh surely: but he that perverteth his ways shall be known.
kjv.10:10: He that winketh with the eye causeth sorrow: but a prating fool shall fall.
kjv.10:11: The mouth of a righteous [man is] a well of life: but violence covereth the mouth of the wicked.
kjv.10:12: Hatred stirreth up strifes: but love covereth all sins.
kjv.10:13: In the lips of him that hath understanding wisdom is found: but a rod [is] for the back of him that is void of understanding.
kjv.10:14: Wise [men] lay up knowledge: but the mouth of the foolish [is] near destruction.
kjv.10:15: The rich man's wealth [is] his strong city: the destruction of the poor [is] their poverty.
kjv.10:16: The labour of the righteous [tendeth] to life: the fruit of the wicked to sin.
kjv.10:17: He [is in] the way of life that keepeth instruction: but he that refuseth reproof erreth.
kjv.10:18: He that hideth hatred [with] lying lips, and he that uttereth a slander, [is] a fool.
kjv.10:19: In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips [is] wise.
kjv.10:20: The tongue of the just [is as] choice silver: the heart of the wicked [is] little worth.
kjv.10:21: The lips of the righteous feed many: but fools die for want of wisdom.
kjv.10:22: The blessing of the LORD, it maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow with it.
kjv.10:23: [It is] as sport to a fool to do mischief: but a man of understanding hath wisdom.
kjv.10:24: The fear of the wicked, it shall come upon him: but the desire of the righteous shall be granted.
kjv.10:25: As the whirlwind passeth, so [is] the wicked no [more]: but the righteous [is] an everlasting foundation.
kjv.10:26: As vinegar to the teeth, and as smoke to the eyes, so [is] the sluggard to them that send him.
kjv.10:27: The fear of the LORD prolongeth days: but the years of the wicked shall be shortened.
kjv.10:28: The hope of the righteous [shall be] gladness: but the expectation of the wicked shall perish.
kjv.10:29: The way of the LORD [is] strength to the upright: but destruction [shall be] to the workers of iniquity.
kjv.10:30: The righteous shall never be removed: but the wicked shall not inhabit the earth.
kjv.10:31: The mouth of the just bringeth forth wisdom: but the froward tongue shall be cut out.
kjv.10:32: The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable: but the mouth of the wicked [speaketh] frowardness.
kjv.11:1: A false balance [is] abomination to the LORD: but a just weight [is] his delight.
kjv.11:2: [When] pride cometh, then cometh shame: but with the lowly [is] wisdom.
kjv.11:3: The integrity of the upright shall guide them: but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them.
kjv.11:4: Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death.
kjv.11:5: The righteousness of the perfect shall direct his way: but the wicked shall fall by his own wickedness.
kjv.11:6: The righteousness of the upright shall deliver them: but transgressors shall be taken in [their own] naughtiness.
kjv.11:7: When a wicked man dieth, [his] expectation shall perish: and the hope of unjust [men] perisheth.
kjv.11:8: The righteous is delivered out of trouble, and the wicked cometh in his stead.
kjv.11:9: An hypocrite with [his] mouth destroyeth his neighbour: but through knowledge shall the just be delivered.
kjv.11:10: When it goeth well with the righteous, the city rejoiceth: and when the wicked perish, [there is] shouting.
kjv.11:11: By the blessing of the upright the city is exalted: but it is overthrown by the mouth of the wicked.
kjv.11:12: He that is void of wisdom despiseth his neighbour: but a man of understanding holdeth his peace.
kjv.11:13: A talebearer revealeth secrets: but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter.
kjv.11:14: Where no counsel [is], the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors [there is] safety.
kjv.11:15: He that is surety for a stranger shall smart [for it]: and he that hateth suretiship is sure.
kjv.11:16: A gracious woman retaineth honour: and strong [men] retain riches.
kjv.11:17: The merciful man doeth good to his own soul: but [he that is] cruel troubleth his own flesh.
kjv.11:18: The wicked worketh a deceitful work: but to him that soweth righteousness [shall be] a sure reward.
kjv.11:19: As righteousness [tendeth] to life: so he that pursueth evil [pursueth it] to his own death.
kjv.11:20: They that are of a froward heart [are] abomination to the LORD: but [such as are] upright in [their] way [are] his delight.
kjv.11:21: [Though] hand [join] in hand, the wicked shall not be unpunished: but the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.
kjv.11:22: [As] a jewel of gold in a swine's snout, [so is] a fair woman which is without discretion.
kjv.11:23: The desire of the righteous [is] only good: [but] the expectation of the wicked [is] wrath.
kjv.11:24: There is that scattereth, and yet increaseth; and [there is] that withholdeth more than is meet, but [it tendeth] to poverty.
kjv.11:25: The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.
kjv.11:26: He that withholdeth corn, the people shall curse him: but blessing [shall be] upon the head of him that selleth [it].
kjv.11:27: He that diligently seeketh good procureth favour: but he that seeketh mischief, it shall come unto him.
kjv.11:28: He that trusteth in his riches shall fall: but the righteous shall flourish as a branch.
kjv.11:29: He that troubleth his own house shall inherit the wind: and the fool [shall be] servant to the wise of heart.
kjv.11:30: The fruit of the righteous [is] a tree of life; and he that winneth souls [is] wise.
kjv.11:31: Behold, the righteous shall be recompensed in the earth: much more the wicked and the sinner.
kjv.12:1: Whoso loveth instruction loveth knowledge: but he that hateth reproof [is] brutish.
kjv.12:2: A good [man] obtaineth favour of the LORD: but a man of wicked devices will he condemn.
kjv.12:3: A man shall not be established by wickedness: but the root of the righteous shall not be moved.
kjv.12:4: A virtuous woman [is] a crown to her husband: but she that maketh ashamed [is] as rottenness in his bones.
kjv.12:5: The thoughts of the righteous [are] right: [but] the counsels of the wicked [are] deceit.
kjv.12:6: The words of the wicked [are] to lie in wait for blood: but the mouth of the upright shall deliver them.
kjv.12:7: The wicked are overthrown, and [are] not: but the house of the righteous shall stand.
kjv.12:8: A man shall be commended according to his wisdom: but he that is of a perverse heart shall be despised.
kjv.12:9: [He that is] despised, and hath a servant, [is] better than he that honoureth himself, and lacketh bread.
kjv.12:10: A righteous [man] regardeth the life of his beast: but the tender mercies of the wicked [are] cruel.
kjv.12:11: He that tilleth his land shall be satisfied with bread: but he that followeth vain [persons is] void of understanding.
kjv.12:12: The wicked desireth the net of evil [men]: but the root of the righteous yieldeth [fruit].
kjv.12:13: The wicked is snared by the transgression of [his] lips: but the just shall come out of trouble.
kjv.12:14: A man shall be satisfied with good by the fruit of [his] mouth: and the recompence of a man's hands shall be rendered unto him.
kjv.12:15: The way of a fool [is] right in his own eyes: but he that hearkeneth unto counsel [is] wise.
kjv.12:16: A fool's wrath is presently known: but a prudent [man] covereth shame.
kjv.12:17: [He that] speaketh truth sheweth forth righteousness: but a false witness deceit.
kjv.12:18: There is that speaketh like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise [is] health.
kjv.12:19: The lip of truth shall be established for ever: but a lying tongue [is] but for a moment.
kjv.12:20: Deceit [is] in the heart of them that imagine evil: but to the counsellors of peace [is] joy.
kjv.12:21: There shall no evil happen to the just: but the wicked shall be filled with mischief.
kjv.12:22: Lying lips [are] abomination to the LORD: but they that deal truly [are] his delight.
kjv.12:23: A prudent man concealeth knowledge: but the heart of fools proclaimeth foolishness.
kjv.12:24: The hand of the diligent shall bear rule: but the slothful shall be under tribute.
kjv.12:25: Heaviness in the heart of man maketh it stoop: but a good word maketh it glad.
kjv.12:26: The righteous [is] more excellent than his neighbour: but the way of the wicked seduceth them.
kjv.12:27: The slothful [man] roasteth not that which he took in hunting: but the substance of a diligent man [is] precious.
kjv.12:28: In the way of righteousness [is] life; and [in] the pathway [thereof there is] no death.
kjv.13:1: A wise son [heareth] his father's instruction: but a scorner heareth not rebuke.
kjv.13:2: A man shall eat good by the fruit of [his] mouth: but the soul of the transgressors [shall eat] violence.
kjv.13:3: He that keepeth his mouth keepeth his life: [but] he that openeth wide his lips shall have destruction.
kjv.13:4: The soul of the sluggard desireth, and [hath] nothing: but the soul of the diligent shall be made fat.
kjv.13:5: A righteous [man] hateth lying: but a wicked [man] is loathsome, and cometh to shame.
kjv.13:6: Righteousness keepeth [him that is] upright in the way: but wickedness overthroweth the sinner.
kjv.13:7: There is that maketh himself rich, yet [hath] nothing: [there is] that maketh himself poor, yet [hath] great riches.
kjv.13:8: The ransom of a man's life [are] his riches: but the poor heareth not rebuke.
kjv.13:9: The light of the righteous rejoiceth: but the lamp of the wicked shall be put out.
kjv.13:10: Only by pride cometh contention: but with the well advised [is] wisdom.
kjv.13:11: Wealth [gotten] by vanity shall be diminished: but he that gathereth by labour shall increase.
kjv.13:12: Hope deferred maketh the heart sick: but [when] the desire cometh, [it is] a tree of life.
kjv.13:13: Whoso despiseth the word shall be destroyed: but he that feareth the commandment shall be rewarded.
kjv.13:14: The law of the wise [is] a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death.
kjv.13:15: Good understanding giveth favour: but the way of transgressors [is] hard.
kjv.13:16: Every prudent [man] dealeth with knowledge: but a fool layeth open [his] folly.
kjv.13:17: A wicked messenger falleth into mischief: but a faithful ambassador [is] health.
kjv.13:18: Poverty and shame [shall be to] him that refuseth instruction: but he that regardeth reproof shall be honoured.
kjv.13:19: The desire accomplished is sweet to the soul: but [it is] abomination to fools to depart from evil.
kjv.13:20: He that walketh with wise [men] shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed.
kjv.13:21: Evil pursueth sinners: but to the righteous good shall be repayed.
kjv.13:22: A good [man] leaveth an inheritance to his children's children: and the wealth of the sinner [is] laid up for the just.
kjv.13:23: Much food [is in] the tillage of the poor: but there is [that is] destroyed for want of judgment.
kjv.13:24: He that spareth his rod hateth his son: but he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes.
kjv.13:25: The righteous eateth to the satisfying of his soul: but the belly of the wicked shall want.
kjv.14:1: Every wise woman buildeth her house: but the foolish plucketh it down with her hands.
kjv.14:2: He that walketh in his uprightness feareth the LORD: but [he that is] perverse in his ways despiseth him.
kjv.14:3: In the mouth of the foolish [is] a rod of pride: but the lips of the wise shall preserve them.
kjv.14:4: Where no oxen [are], the crib [is] clean: but much increase [is] by the strength of the ox.
kjv.14:5: A faithful witness will not lie: but a false witness will utter lies.
kjv.14:6: A scorner seeketh wisdom, and [findeth it] not: but knowledge [is] easy unto him that understandeth.
kjv.14:7: Go from the presence of a foolish man, when thou perceivest not [in him] the lips of knowledge.
kjv.14:8: The wisdom of the prudent [is] to understand his way: but the folly of fools [is] deceit.
kjv.14:9: Fools make a mock at sin: but among the righteous [there is] favour.
kjv.14:10: The heart knoweth his own bitterness; and a stranger doth not intermeddle with his joy.
kjv.14:11: The house of the wicked shall be overthrown: but the tabernacle of the upright shall flourish.
kjv.14:12: There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof [are] the ways of death.
kjv.14:13: Even in laughter the heart is sorrowful; and the end of that mirth [is] heaviness.
kjv.14:14: The backslider in heart shall be filled with his own ways: and a good man [shall be satisfied] from himself.
kjv.14:15: The simple believeth every word: but the prudent [man] looketh well to his going.
kjv.14:16: A wise [man] feareth, and departeth from evil: but the fool rageth, and is confident.
kjv.14:17: [He that is] soon angry dealeth foolishly: and a man of wicked devices is hated.
kjv.14:18: The simple inherit folly: but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
kjv.14:19: The evil bow before the good; and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
kjv.14:20: The poor is hated even of his own neighbour: but the rich [hath] many friends.
kjv.14:21: He that despiseth his neighbour sinneth: but he that hath mercy on the poor, happy [is] he.
kjv.14:22: Do they not err that devise evil? but mercy and truth [shall be] to them that devise good.
kjv.14:23: In all labour there is profit: but the talk of the lips [tendeth] only to penury.
kjv.14:24: The crown of the wise [is] their riches: [but] the foolishness of fools [is] folly.
kjv.14:25: A true witness delivereth souls: but a deceitful [witness] speaketh lies.
kjv.14:26: In the fear of the LORD [is] strong confidence: and his children shall have a place of refuge.
kjv.14:27: The fear of the LORD [is] a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death.
kjv.14:28: In the multitude of people [is] the king's honour: but in the want of people [is] the destruction of the prince.
kjv.14:29: [He that is] slow to wrath [is] of great understanding: but [he that is] hasty of spirit exalteth folly.
kjv.14:30: A sound heart [is] the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones.
kjv.14:31: He that oppresseth the poor reproacheth his Maker: but he that honoureth him hath mercy on the poor.
kjv.14:32: The wicked is driven away in his wickedness: but the righteous hath hope in his death.
kjv.14:33: Wisdom resteth in the heart of him that hath understanding: but [that which is] in the midst of fools is made known.
kjv.14:34: Righteousness exalteth a nation: but sin [is] a reproach to any people.
kjv.14:35: The king's favour [is] toward a wise servant: but his wrath is [against] him that causeth shame.
kjv.15:1: A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.
kjv.15:2: The tongue of the wise useth knowledge aright: but the mouth of fools poureth out foolishness.
kjv.15:3: The eyes of the LORD [are] in every place, beholding the evil and the good.
kjv.15:4: A wholesome tongue [is] a tree of life: but perverseness therein [is] a breach in the spirit.
kjv.15:5: A fool despiseth his father's instruction: but he that regardeth reproof is prudent.
kjv.15:6: In the house of the righteous [is] much treasure: but in the revenues of the wicked is trouble.
kjv.15:7: The lips of the wise disperse knowledge: but the heart of the foolish [doeth] not so.
kjv.15:8: The sacrifice of the wicked [is] an abomination to the LORD: but the prayer of the upright [is] his delight.
kjv.15:9: The way of the wicked [is] an abomination unto the LORD: but he loveth him that followeth after righteousness.
kjv.15:10: Correction [is] grievous unto him that forsaketh the way: [and] he that hateth reproof shall die.
kjv.15:11: Hell and destruction [are] before the LORD: how much more then the hearts of the children of men?
kjv.15:12: A scorner loveth not one that reproveth him: neither will he go unto the wise.
kjv.15:13: A merry heart maketh a cheerful countenance: but by sorrow of the heart the spirit is broken.
kjv.15:14: The heart of him that hath understanding seeketh knowledge: but the mouth of fools feedeth on foolishness.
kjv.15:15: All the days of the afflicted [are] evil: but he that is of a merry heart [hath] a continual feast.
kjv.15:16: Better [is] little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure and trouble therewith.
kjv.15:17: Better [is] a dinner of herbs where love is, than a stalled ox and hatred therewith.
kjv.15:18: A wrathful man stirreth up strife: but [he that is] slow to anger appeaseth strife.
kjv.15:19: The way of the slothful [man is] as an hedge of thorns: but the way of the righteous [is] made plain.
kjv.15:20: A wise son maketh a glad father: but a foolish man despiseth his mother.
kjv.15:21: Folly [is] joy to [him that is] destitute of wisdom: but a man of understanding walketh uprightly.
kjv.15:22: Without counsel purposes are disappointed: but in the multitude of counsellors they are established.
kjv.15:23: A man hath joy by the answer of his mouth: and a word [spoken] in due season, how good [is it]!
kjv.15:24: The way of life [is] above to the wise, that he may depart from hell beneath.
kjv.15:25: The LORD will destroy the house of the proud: but he will establish the border of the widow.
kjv.15:26: The thoughts of the wicked [are] an abomination to the LORD: but [the words] of the pure [are] pleasant words.
kjv.15:27: He that is greedy of gain troubleth his own house; but he that hateth gifts shall live.
kjv.15:28: The heart of the righteous studieth to answer: but the mouth of the wicked poureth out evil things.
kjv.15:29: The LORD [is] far from the wicked: but he heareth the prayer of the righteous.
kjv.15:30: The light of the eyes rejoiceth the heart: [and] a good report maketh the bones fat.
kjv.15:31: The ear that heareth the reproof of life abideth among the wise.
kjv.15:32: He that refuseth instruction despiseth his own soul: but he that heareth reproof getteth understanding.
kjv.15:33: The fear of the LORD [is] the instruction of wisdom; and before honour [is] humility.
kjv.16:1: The preparations of the heart in man, and the answer of the tongue, [is] from the LORD.
kjv.16:2: All the ways of a man [are] clean in his own eyes; but the LORD weigheth the spirits.
kjv.16:3: Commit thy works unto the LORD, and thy thoughts shall be established.
kjv.16:4: The LORD hath made all [things] for himself: yea, even the wicked for the day of evil.
kjv.16:5: Every one [that is] proud in heart [is] an abomination to the LORD: [though] hand [join] in hand, he shall not be unpunished.
kjv.16:6: By mercy and truth iniquity is purged: and by the fear of the LORD [men] depart from evil.
kjv.16:7: When a man's ways please the LORD, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.
kjv.16:8: Better [is] a little with righteousness than great revenues without right.
kjv.16:9: A man's heart deviseth his way: but the LORD directeth his steps.
kjv.16:10: A divine sentence [is] in the lips of the king: his mouth transgresseth not in judgment.
kjv.16:11: A just weight and balance [are] the LORD'S: all the weights of the bag [are] his work.
kjv.16:12: [It is] an abomination to kings to commit wickedness: for the throne is established by righteousness.
kjv.16:13: Righteous lips [are] the delight of kings; and they love him that speaketh right.
kjv.16:14: The wrath of a king [is as] messengers of death: but a wise man will pacify it.
kjv.16:15: In the light of the king's countenance [is] life; and his favour [is] as a cloud of the latter rain.
kjv.16:16: How much better [is it] to get wisdom than gold! and to get understanding rather to be chosen than silver!
kjv.16:17: The highway of the upright [is] to depart from evil: he that keepeth his way preserveth his soul.
kjv.16:18: Pride [goeth] before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.
kjv.16:19: Better [it is to be] of an humble spirit with the lowly, than to divide the spoil with the proud.
kjv.16:20: He that handleth a matter wisely shall find good: and whoso trusteth in the LORD, happy [is] he.
kjv.16:21: The wise in heart shall be called prudent: and the sweetness of the lips increaseth learning.
kjv.16:22: Understanding [is] a wellspring of life unto him that hath it: but the instruction of fools [is] folly.
kjv.16:23: The heart of the wise teacheth his mouth, and addeth learning to his lips.
kjv.16:24: Pleasant words [are as] an honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
kjv.16:25: There is a way that seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof [are] the ways of death.
kjv.16:26: He that laboureth laboureth for himself; for his mouth craveth it of him.
kjv.16:27: An ungodly man diggeth up evil: and in his lips [there is] as a burning fire.
kjv.16:28: A froward man soweth strife: and a whisperer separateth chief friends.
kjv.16:29: A violent man enticeth his neighbour, and leadeth him into the way [that is] not good.
kjv.16:30: He shutteth his eyes to devise froward things: moving his lips he bringeth evil to pass.
kjv.16:31: The hoary head [is] a crown of glory, [if] it be found in the way of righteousness.
kjv.16:32: [He that is] slow to anger [is] better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city.
kjv.16:33: The lot is cast into the lap; but the whole disposing thereof [is] of the LORD.
kjv.17:1: Better [is] a dry morsel, and quietness therewith, than an house full of sacrifices [with] strife.
kjv.17:2: A wise servant shall have rule over a son that causeth shame, and shall have part of the inheritance among the brethren.
kjv.17:3: The fining pot [is] for silver, and the furnace for gold: but the LORD trieth the hearts.
kjv.17:4: A wicked doer giveth heed to false lips; [and] a liar giveth ear to a naughty tongue.
kjv.17:5: Whoso mocketh the poor reproacheth his Maker: [and] he that is glad at calamities shall not be unpunished.
kjv.17:6: Children's children [are] the crown of old men; and the glory of children [are] their fathers.
kjv.17:7: Excellent speech becometh not a fool: much less do lying lips a prince.
kjv.17:8: A gift [is as] a precious stone in the eyes of him that hath it: whithersoever it turneth, it prospereth.
kjv.17:9: He that covereth a transgression seeketh love; but he that repeateth a matter separateth [very] friends.
kjv.17:10: A reproof entereth more into a wise man than an hundred stripes into a fool.
kjv.17:11: An evil [man] seeketh only rebellion: therefore a cruel messenger shall be sent against him.
kjv.17:12: Let a bear robbed of her whelps meet a man, rather than a fool in his folly.
kjv.17:13: Whoso rewardeth evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house.
kjv.17:14: The beginning of strife [is as] when one letteth out water: therefore leave off contention, before it be meddled with.
kjv.17:15: He that justifieth the wicked, and he that condemneth the just, even they both [are] abomination to the LORD.
kjv.17:16: Wherefore [is there] a price in the hand of a fool to get wisdom, seeing [he hath] no heart [to it]?
kjv.17:17: A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.
kjv.17:18: A man void of understanding striketh hands, [and] becometh surety in the presence of his friend.
kjv.17:19: He loveth transgression that loveth strife: [and] he that exalteth his gate seeketh destruction.
kjv.17:20: He that hath a froward heart findeth no good: and he that hath a perverse tongue falleth into mischief.
kjv.17:21: He that begetteth a fool [doeth it] to his sorrow: and the father of a fool hath no joy.
kjv.17:22: A merry heart doeth good [like] a medicine: but a broken spirit drieth the bones.
kjv.17:23: A wicked [man] taketh a gift out of the bosom to pervert the ways of judgment.
kjv.17:24: Wisdom [is] before him that hath understanding; but the eyes of a fool [are] in the ends of the earth.
kjv.17:25: A foolish son [is] a grief to his father, and bitterness to her that bare him.
kjv.17:26: Also to punish the just [is] not good, [nor] to strike princes for equity.
kjv.17:27: He that hath knowledge spareth his words: [and] a man of understanding is of an excellent spirit.
kjv.17:28: Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise: [and] he that shutteth his lips [is esteemed] a man of understanding.
kjv.18:1: Through desire a man, having separated himself, seeketh [and] intermeddleth with all wisdom.
kjv.18:2: A fool hath no delight in understanding, but that his heart may discover itself.
kjv.18:3: When the wicked cometh, [then] cometh also contempt, and with ignominy reproach.
kjv.18:4: The words of a man's mouth [are as] deep waters, [and] the wellspring of wisdom [as] a flowing brook.
kjv.18:5: [It is] not good to accept the person of the wicked, to overthrow the righteous in judgment.
kjv.18:6: A fool's lips enter into contention, and his mouth calleth for strokes.
kjv.18:7: A fool's mouth [is] his destruction, and his lips [are] the snare of his soul.
kjv.18:8: The words of a talebearer [are] as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.
kjv.18:9: He also that is slothful in his work is brother to him that is a great waster.
kjv.18:10: The name of the LORD [is] a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe.
kjv.18:11: The rich man's wealth [is] his strong city, and as an high wall in his own conceit.
kjv.18:12: Before destruction the heart of man is haughty, and before honour [is] humility.
kjv.18:13: He that answereth a matter before he heareth [it], it [is] folly and shame unto him.
kjv.18:14: The spirit of a man will sustain his infirmity; but a wounded spirit who can bear?
kjv.18:15: The heart of the prudent getteth knowledge; and the ear of the wise seeketh knowledge.
kjv.18:16: A man's gift maketh room for him, and bringeth him before great men.
kjv.18:17: [He that is] first in his own cause [seemeth] just; but his neighbour cometh and searcheth him.
kjv.18:18: The lot causeth contentions to cease, and parteth between the mighty.
kjv.18:19: A brother offended [is harder to be won] than a strong city: and [their] contentions [are] like the bars of a castle.
kjv.18:20: A man's belly shall be satisfied with the fruit of his mouth; [and] with the increase of his lips shall he be filled.
kjv.18:21: Death and life [are] in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.
kjv.18:22: [Whoso] findeth a wife findeth a good [thing], and obtaineth favour of the LORD.
kjv.18:23: The poor useth intreaties; but the rich answereth roughly.
kjv.18:24: A man [that hath] friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend [that] sticketh closer than a brother.
kjv.19:1: Better [is] the poor that walketh in his integrity, than [he that is] perverse in his lips, and is a fool.
kjv.19:2: Also, [that] the soul [be] without knowledge, [it is] not good; and he that hasteth with [his] feet sinneth.
kjv.19:3: The foolishness of man perverteth his way: and his heart fretteth against the LORD.
kjv.19:4: Wealth maketh many friends; but the poor is separated from his neighbour.
kjv.19:5: A false witness shall not be unpunished, and [he that] speaketh lies shall not escape.
kjv.19:6: Many will intreat the favour of the prince: and every man [is] a friend to him that giveth gifts.
kjv.19:7: All the brethren of the poor do hate him: how much more do his friends go far from him? he pursueth [them with] words, [yet] they [are] wanting [to him].
kjv.19:8: He that getteth wisdom loveth his own soul: he that keepeth understanding shall find good.
kjv.19:9: A false witness shall not be unpunished, and [he that] speaketh lies shall perish.
kjv.19:10: Delight is not seemly for a fool; much less for a servant to have rule over princes.
kjv.19:11: The discretion of a man deferreth his anger; and [it is] his glory to pass over a transgression.
kjv.19:12: The king's wrath [is] as the roaring of a lion; but his favour [is] as dew upon the grass.
kjv.19:13: A foolish son [is] the calamity of his father: and the contentions of a wife [are] a continual dropping.
kjv.19:14: House and riches [are] the inheritance of fathers: and a prudent wife [is] from the LORD.
kjv.19:15: Slothfulness casteth into a deep sleep; and an idle soul shall suffer hunger.
kjv.19:16: He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his own soul; [but] he that despiseth his ways shall die.
kjv.19:17: He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the LORD; and that which he hath given will he pay him again.
kjv.19:18: Chasten thy son while there is hope, and let not thy soul spare for his crying.
kjv.19:19: A man of great wrath shall suffer punishment: for if thou deliver [him], yet thou must do it again.
kjv.19:20: Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.
kjv.19:21: [There are] many devices in a man's heart; nevertheless the counsel of the LORD, that shall stand.
kjv.19:22: The desire of a man [is] his kindness: and a poor man [is] better than a liar.
kjv.19:23: The fear of the LORD [tendeth] to life: and [he that hath it] shall abide satisfied; he shall not be visited with evil.
kjv.19:24: A slothful [man] hideth his hand in [his] bosom, and will not so much as bring it to his mouth again.
kjv.19:25: Smite a scorner, and the simple will beware: and reprove one that hath understanding, [and] he will understand knowledge.
kjv.19:26: He that wasteth [his] father, [and] chaseth away [his] mother, [is] a son that causeth shame, and bringeth reproach.
kjv.19:27: Cease, my son, to hear the instruction [that causeth] to err from the words of knowledge.
kjv.19:28: An ungodly witness scorneth judgment: and the mouth of the wicked devoureth iniquity.
kjv.19:29: Judgments are prepared for scorners, and stripes for the back of fools.
kjv.20:1: Wine [is] a mocker, strong drink [is] raging: and whosoever is deceived thereby is not wise.
kjv.20:2: The fear of a king [is] as the roaring of a lion: [whoso] provoketh him to anger sinneth [against] his own soul.
kjv.20:3: [It is] an honour for a man to cease from strife: but every fool will be meddling.
kjv.20:4: The sluggard will not plow by reason of the cold; [therefore] shall he beg in harvest, and [have] nothing.
kjv.20:5: Counsel in the heart of man [is like] deep water; but a man of understanding will draw it out.
kjv.20:6: Most men will proclaim every one his own goodness: but a faithful man who can find?
kjv.20:7: The just [man] walketh in his integrity: his children [are] blessed after him.
kjv.20:8: A king that sitteth in the throne of judgment scattereth away all evil with his eyes.
kjv.20:9: Who can say, I have made my heart clean, I am pure from my sin?
kjv.20:10: Divers weights, [and] divers measures, both of them [are] alike abomination to the LORD.
kjv.20:11: Even a child is known by his doings, whether his work [be] pure, and whether [it be] right.
kjv.20:12: The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, the LORD hath made even both of them.
kjv.20:13: Love not sleep, lest thou come to poverty; open thine eyes, [and] thou shalt be satisfied with bread.
kjv.20:14: [It is] naught, [it is] naught, saith the buyer: but when he is gone his way, then he boasteth.
kjv.20:15: There is gold, and a multitude of rubies: but the lips of knowledge [are] a precious jewel.
kjv.20:16: Take his garment that is surety [for] a stranger: and take a pledge of him for a strange woman.
kjv.20:17: Bread of deceit [is] sweet to a man; but afterwards his mouth shall be filled with gravel.
kjv.20:18: [Every] purpose is established by counsel: and with good advice make war.
kjv.20:19: He that goeth about [as] a talebearer revealeth secrets: therefore meddle not with him that flattereth with his lips.
kjv.20:20: Whoso curseth his father or his mother, his lamp shall be put out in obscure darkness.
kjv.20:21: An inheritance [may be] gotten hastily at the beginning; but the end thereof shall not be blessed.
kjv.20:22: Say not thou, I will recompense evil; [but] wait on the LORD, and he shall save thee.
kjv.20:23: Divers weights [are] an abomination unto the LORD; and a false balance [is] not good.
kjv.20:24: Man's goings [are] of the LORD; how can a man then understand his own way?
kjv.20:25: [It is] a snare to the man [who] devoureth [that which is] holy, and after vows to make enquiry.
kjv.20:26: A wise king scattereth the wicked, and bringeth the wheel over them.
kjv.20:27: The spirit of man [is] the candle of the LORD, searching all the inward parts of the belly.
kjv.20:28: Mercy and truth preserve the king: and his throne is upholden by mercy.
kjv.20:29: The glory of young men [is] their strength: and the beauty of old men [is] the gray head.
kjv.20:30: The blueness of a wound cleanseth away evil: so [do] stripes the inward parts of the belly.
kjv.21:1: The king's heart [is] in the hand of the LORD, [as] the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.
kjv.21:2: Every way of a man [is] right in his own eyes: but the LORD pondereth the hearts.
kjv.21:3: To do justice and judgment [is] more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice.
kjv.21:4: An high look, and a proud heart, [and] the plowing of the wicked, [is] sin.
kjv.21:5: The thoughts of the diligent [tend] only to plenteousness; but of every one [that is] hasty only to want.
kjv.21:6: The getting of treasures by a lying tongue [is] a vanity tossed to and fro of them that seek death.
kjv.21:7: The robbery of the wicked shall destroy them; because they refuse to do judgment.
kjv.21:8: The way of man [is] froward and strange: but [as for] the pure, his work [is] right.
kjv.21:9: [It is] better to dwell in a corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman in a wide house.
kjv.21:10: The soul of the wicked desireth evil: his neighbour findeth no favour in his eyes.
kjv.21:11: When the scorner is punished, the simple is made wise: and when the wise is instructed, he receiveth knowledge.
kjv.21:12: The righteous [man] wisely considereth the house of the wicked: [but God] overthroweth the wicked for [their] wickedness.
kjv.21:13: Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, he also shall cry himself, but shall not be heard.
kjv.21:14: A gift in secret pacifieth anger: and a reward in the bosom strong wrath.
kjv.21:15: [It is] joy to the just to do judgment: but destruction [shall be] to the workers of iniquity.
kjv.21:16: The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.
kjv.21:17: He that loveth pleasure [shall be] a poor man: he that loveth wine and oil shall not be rich.
kjv.21:18: The wicked [shall be] a ransom for the righteous, and the transgressor for the upright.
kjv.21:19: [It is] better to dwell in the wilderness, than with a contentious and an angry woman.
kjv.21:20: [There is] treasure to be desired and oil in the dwelling of the wise; but a foolish man spendeth it up.
kjv.21:21: He that followeth after righteousness and mercy findeth life, righteousness, and honour.
kjv.21:22: A wise [man] scaleth the city of the mighty, and casteth down the strength of the confidence thereof.
kjv.21:23: Whoso keepeth his mouth and his tongue keepeth his soul from troubles.
kjv.21:24: Proud [and] haughty scorner [is] his name, who dealeth in proud wrath.
kjv.21:25: The desire of the slothful killeth him; for his hands refuse to labour.
kjv.21:26: He coveteth greedily all the day long: but the righteous giveth and spareth not.
kjv.21:27: The sacrifice of the wicked [is] abomination: how much more, [when] he bringeth it with a wicked mind?
kjv.21:28: A false witness shall perish: but the man that heareth speaketh constantly.
kjv.21:29: A wicked man hardeneth his face: but [as for] the upright, he directeth his way.
kjv.21:30: [There is] no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against the LORD.
kjv.21:31: The horse [is] prepared against the day of battle: but safety [is] of the LORD.
kjv.22:1: A [good] name [is] rather to be chosen than great riches, [and] loving favour rather than silver and gold.
kjv.22:2: The rich and poor meet together: the LORD [is] the maker of them all.
kjv.22:3: A prudent [man] foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.
kjv.22:4: By humility [and] the fear of the LORD [are] riches, and honour, and life.
kjv.22:5: Thorns [and] snares [are] in the way of the froward: he that doth keep his soul shall be far from them.
kjv.22:6: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
kjv.22:7: The rich ruleth over the poor, and the borrower [is] servant to the lender.
kjv.22:8: He that soweth iniquity shall reap vanity: and the rod of his anger shall fail.
kjv.22:9: He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; for he giveth of his bread to the poor.
kjv.22:10: Cast out the scorner, and contention shall go out; yea, strife and reproach shall cease.
kjv.22:11: He that loveth pureness of heart, [for] the grace of his lips the king [shall be] his friend.
kjv.22:12: The eyes of the LORD preserve knowledge, and he overthroweth the words of the transgressor.
kjv.22:13: The slothful [man] saith, [There is] a lion without, I shall be slain in the streets.
kjv.22:14: The mouth of strange women [is] a deep pit: he that is abhorred of the LORD shall fall therein.
kjv.22:15: Foolishness [is] bound in the heart of a child; [but] the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.
kjv.22:16: He that oppresseth the poor to increase his [riches, and] he that giveth to the rich, [shall] surely [come] to want.
kjv.22:17: Bow down thine ear, and hear the words of the wise, and apply thine heart unto my knowledge.
kjv.22:18: For [it is] a pleasant thing if thou keep them within thee; they shall withal be fitted in thy lips.
kjv.22:19: That thy trust may be in the LORD, I have made known to thee this day, even to thee.
kjv.22:20: Have not I written to thee excellent things in counsels and knowledge,
kjv.22:21: That I might make thee know the certainty of the words of truth; that thou mightest answer the words of truth to them that send unto thee?
kjv.22:22: Rob not the poor, because he [is] poor: neither oppress the afflicted in the gate:
kjv.22:23: For the LORD will plead their cause, and spoil the soul of those that spoiled them.
kjv.22:24: Make no friendship with an angry man; and with a furious man thou shalt not go:
kjv.22:25: Lest thou learn his ways, and get a snare to thy soul.
kjv.22:26: Be not thou [one] of them that strike hands, [or] of them that are sureties for debts.
kjv.22:27: If thou hast nothing to pay, why should he take away thy bed from under thee?
kjv.22:28: Remove not the ancient landmark, which thy fathers have set.
kjv.22:29: Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean [men].
kjv.23:1: When thou sittest to eat with a ruler, consider diligently what [is] before thee:
kjv.23:2: And put a knife to thy throat, if thou [be] a man given to appetite.
kjv.23:3: Be not desirous of his dainties: for they [are] deceitful meat.
kjv.23:4: Labour not to be rich: cease from thine own wisdom.
kjv.23:5: Wilt thou set thine eyes upon that which is not? for [riches] certainly make themselves wings; they fly away as an eagle toward heaven.
kjv.23:6: Eat thou not the bread of [him that hath] an evil eye, neither desire thou his dainty meats:
kjv.23:7: For as he thinketh in his heart, so [is] he: Eat and drink, saith he to thee; but his heart [is] not with thee.
kjv.23:8: The morsel [which] thou hast eaten shalt thou vomit up, and lose thy sweet words.
kjv.23:9: Speak not in the ears of a fool: for he will despise the wisdom of thy words.
kjv.23:10: Remove not the old landmark; and enter not into the fields of the fatherless:
kjv.23:11: For their redeemer [is] mighty; he shall plead their cause with thee.
kjv.23:12: Apply thine heart unto instruction, and thine ears to the words of knowledge.
kjv.23:13: Withhold not correction from the child: for [if] thou beatest him with the rod, he shall not die.
kjv.23:14: Thou shalt beat him with the rod, and shalt deliver his soul from hell.
kjv.23:15: My son, if thine heart be wise, my heart shall rejoice, even mine.
kjv.23:16: Yea, my reins shall rejoice, when thy lips speak right things.
kjv.23:17: Let not thine heart envy sinners: but [be thou] in the fear of the LORD all the day long.
kjv.23:18: For surely there is an end; and thine expectation shall not be cut off.
kjv.23:19: Hear thou, my son, and be wise, and guide thine heart in the way.
kjv.23:20: Be not among winebibbers; among riotous eaters of flesh:
kjv.23:21: For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty: and drowsiness shall clothe [a man] with rags.
kjv.23:22: Hearken unto thy father that begat thee, and despise not thy mother when she is old.
kjv.23:23: Buy the truth, and sell [it] not; [also] wisdom, and instruction, and understanding.
kjv.23:24: The father of the righteous shall greatly rejoice: and he that begetteth a wise [child] shall have joy of him.
kjv.23:25: Thy father and thy mother shall be glad, and she that bare thee shall rejoice.
kjv.23:26: My son, give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways.
kjv.23:27: For a whore [is] a deep ditch; and a strange woman [is] a narrow pit.
kjv.23:28: She also lieth in wait as [for] a prey, and increaseth the transgressors among men.
kjv.23:29: Who hath woe? who hath sorrow? who hath contentions? who hath babbling? who hath wounds without cause? who hath redness of eyes?
kjv.23:30: They that tarry long at the wine; they that go to seek mixed wine.
kjv.23:31: Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, when it giveth his colour in the cup, [when] it moveth itself aright.
kjv.23:32: At the last it biteth like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder.
kjv.23:33: Thine eyes shall behold strange women, and thine heart shall utter perverse things.
kjv.23:34: Yea, thou shalt be as he that lieth down in the midst of the sea, or as he that lieth upon the top of a mast.
kjv.23:35: They have stricken me, [shalt thou say, and] I was not sick; they have beaten me, [and] I felt [it] not: when shall I awake? I will seek it yet again.
kjv.24:1: Be not thou envious against evil men, neither desire to be with them.
kjv.24:2: For their heart studieth destruction, and their lips talk of mischief.
kjv.24:3: Through wisdom is an house builded; and by understanding it is established:
kjv.24:4: And by knowledge shall the chambers be filled with all precious and pleasant riches.
kjv.24:5: A wise man [is] strong; yea, a man of knowledge increaseth strength.
kjv.24:6: For by wise counsel thou shalt make thy war: and in multitude of counsellors [there is] safety.
kjv.24:7: Wisdom [is] too high for a fool: he openeth not his mouth in the gate.
kjv.24:8: He that deviseth to do evil shall be called a mischievous person.
kjv.24:9: The thought of foolishness [is] sin: and the scorner [is] an abomination to men.
kjv.24:10: [If] thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength [is] small.
kjv.24:11: If thou forbear to deliver [them that are] drawn unto death, and [those that are] ready to be slain;
kjv.24:12: If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider [it]? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth [not] he know [it]? and shall [not] he render to [every] man according to his works?
kjv.24:13: My son, eat thou honey, because [it is] good; and the honeycomb, [which is] sweet to thy taste:
kjv.24:14: So [shall] the knowledge of wisdom [be] unto thy soul: when thou hast found [it], then there shall be a reward, and thy expectation shall not be cut off.
kjv.24:15: Lay not wait, O wicked [man], against the dwelling of the righteous; spoil not his resting place:
kjv.24:16: For a just [man] falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.
kjv.24:17: Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, and let not thine heart be glad when he stumbleth:
kjv.24:18: Lest the LORD see [it], and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.
kjv.24:19: Fret not thyself because of evil [men], neither be thou envious at the wicked;
kjv.24:20: For there shall be no reward to the evil [man]; the candle of the wicked shall be put out.
kjv.24:21: My son, fear thou the LORD and the king: [and] meddle not with them that are given to change:
kjv.24:22: For their calamity shall rise suddenly; and who knoweth the ruin of them both?
kjv.24:23: These [things] also [belong] to the wise. [It is] not good to have respect of persons in judgment.
kjv.24:24: He that saith unto the wicked, Thou [art] righteous; him shall the people curse, nations shall abhor him:
kjv.24:25: But to them that rebuke [him] shall be delight, and a good blessing shall come upon them.
kjv.24:26: [Every man] shall kiss [his] lips that giveth a right answer.
kjv.24:27: Prepare thy work without, and make it fit for thyself in the field; and afterwards build thine house.
kjv.24:28: Be not a witness against thy neighbour without cause; and deceive [not] with thy lips.
kjv.24:29: Say not, I will do so to him as he hath done to me: I will render to the man according to his work.
kjv.24:30: I went by the field of the slothful, and by the vineyard of the man void of understanding;
kjv.24:31: And, lo, it was all grown over with thorns, [and] nettles had covered the face thereof, and the stone wall thereof was broken down.
kjv.24:32: Then I saw, [and] considered [it] well: I looked upon [it, and] received instruction.
kjv.24:33: [Yet] a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep:
kjv.24:34: So shall thy poverty come [as] one that travelleth; and thy want as an armed man.
kjv.25:1: These [are] also proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
kjv.25:2: [It is] the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings [is] to search out a matter.
kjv.25:3: The heaven for height, and the earth for depth, and the heart of kings [is] unsearchable.
kjv.25:4: Take away the dross from the silver, and there shall come forth a vessel for the finer.
kjv.25:5: Take away the wicked [from] before the king, and his throne shall be established in righteousness.
kjv.25:6: Put not forth thyself in the presence of the king, and stand not in the place of great [men]:
kjv.25:7: For better [it is] that it be said unto thee, Come up hither; than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince whom thine eyes have seen.
kjv.25:8: Go not forth hastily to strive, lest [thou know not] what to do in the end thereof, when thy neighbour hath put thee to shame.
kjv.25:9: Debate thy cause with thy neighbour [himself]; and discover not a secret to another:
kjv.25:10: Lest he that heareth [it] put thee to shame, and thine infamy turn not away.
kjv.25:11: A word fitly spoken [is like] apples of gold in pictures of silver.
kjv.25:12: [As] an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, [so is] a wise reprover upon an obedient ear.
kjv.25:13: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, [so is] a faithful messenger to them that send him: for he refresheth the soul of his masters.
kjv.25:14: Whoso boasteth himself of a false gift [is like] clouds and wind without rain.
kjv.25:15: By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone.
kjv.25:16: Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.
kjv.25:17: Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbour's house; lest he be weary of thee, and [so] hate thee.
kjv.25:18: A man that beareth false witness against his neighbour [is] a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.
kjv.25:19: Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble [is like] a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.
kjv.25:20: [As] he that taketh away a garment in cold weather, [and as] vinegar upon nitre, so [is] he that singeth songs to an heavy heart.
kjv.25:21: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:
kjv.25:22: For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the LORD shall reward thee.
kjv.25:23: The north wind driveth away rain: so [doth] an angry countenance a backbiting tongue.
kjv.25:24: [It is] better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman and in a wide house.
kjv.25:25: [As] cold waters to a thirsty soul, so [is] good news from a far country.
kjv.25:26: A righteous man falling down before the wicked [is as] a troubled fountain, and a corrupt spring.
kjv.25:27: [It is] not good to eat much honey: so [for men] to search their own glory [is not] glory.
kjv.25:28: He that [hath] no rule over his own spirit [is like] a city [that is] broken down, [and] without walls.
kjv.26:1: As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honour is not seemly for a fool.
kjv.26:2: As the bird by wandering, as the swallow by flying, so the curse causeless shall not come.
kjv.26:3: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fool's back.
kjv.26:4: Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest thou also be like unto him.
kjv.26:5: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own conceit.
kjv.26:6: He that sendeth a message by the hand of a fool cutteth off the feet, [and] drinketh damage.
kjv.26:7: The legs of the lame are not equal: so [is] a parable in the mouth of fools.
kjv.26:8: As he that bindeth a stone in a sling, so [is] he that giveth honour to a fool.
kjv.26:9: [As] a thorn goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, so [is] a parable in the mouth of fools.
kjv.26:10: The great [God] that formed all [things] both rewardeth the fool, and rewardeth transgressors.
kjv.26:11: As a dog returneth to his vomit, [so] a fool returneth to his folly.
kjv.26:12: Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit? [there is] more hope of a fool than of him.
kjv.26:13: The slothful [man] saith, [There is] a lion in the way; a lion [is] in the streets.
kjv.26:14: [As] the door turneth upon his hinges, so [doth] the slothful upon his bed.
kjv.26:15: The slothful hideth his hand in [his] bosom; it grieveth him to bring it again to his mouth.
kjv.26:16: The sluggard [is] wiser in his own conceit than seven men that can render a reason.
kjv.26:17: He that passeth by, [and] meddleth with strife [belonging] not to him, [is like] one that taketh a dog by the ears.
kjv.26:18: As a mad [man] who casteth firebrands, arrows, and death,
kjv.26:19: So [is] the man [that] deceiveth his neighbour, and saith, Am not I in sport?
kjv.26:20: Where no wood is, [there] the fire goeth out: so where [there is] no talebearer, the strife ceaseth.
kjv.26:21: [As] coals [are] to burning coals, and wood to fire; so [is] a contentious man to kindle strife.
kjv.26:22: The words of a talebearer [are] as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.
kjv.26:23: Burning lips and a wicked heart [are like] a potsherd covered with silver dross.
kjv.26:24: He that hateth dissembleth with his lips, and layeth up deceit within him;
kjv.26:25: When he speaketh fair, believe him not: for [there are] seven abominations in his heart.
kjv.26:26: [Whose] hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shewed before the [whole] congregation.
kjv.26:27: Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him.
kjv.26:28: A lying tongue hateth [those that are] afflicted by it; and a flattering mouth worketh ruin.
kjv.27:1: Boast not thyself of to morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.
kjv.27:2: Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; a stranger, and not thine own lips.
kjv.27:3: A stone [is] heavy, and the sand weighty; but a fool's wrath [is] heavier than them both.
kjv.27:4: Wrath [is] cruel, and anger [is] outrageous; but who [is] able to stand before envy?
kjv.27:5: Open rebuke [is] better than secret love.
kjv.27:6: Faithful [are] the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy [are] deceitful.
kjv.27:7: The full soul loatheth an honeycomb; but to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.
kjv.27:8: As a bird that wandereth from her nest, so [is] a man that wandereth from his place.
kjv.27:9: Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart: so [doth] the sweetness of a man's friend by hearty counsel.
kjv.27:10: Thine own friend, and thy father's friend, forsake not; neither go into thy brother's house in the day of thy calamity: [for] better [is] a neighbour [that is] near than a brother far off.
kjv.27:11: My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, that I may answer him that reproacheth me.
kjv.27:12: A prudent [man] foreseeth the evil, [and] hideth himself; [but] the simple pass on, [and] are punished.
kjv.27:13: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger, and take a pledge of him for a strange woman.
kjv.27:14: He that blesseth his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be counted a curse to him.
kjv.27:15: A continual dropping in a very rainy day and a contentious woman are alike.
kjv.27:16: Whosoever hideth her hideth the wind, and the ointment of his right hand, [which] bewrayeth [itself].
kjv.27:17: Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
kjv.27:18: Whoso keepeth the fig tree shall eat the fruit thereof: so he that waiteth on his master shall be honoured.
kjv.27:19: As in water face [answereth] to face, so the heart of man to man.
kjv.27:20: Hell and destruction are never full; so the eyes of man are never satisfied.
kjv.27:21: [As] the fining pot for silver, and the furnace for gold; so [is] a man to his praise.
kjv.27:22: Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar among wheat with a pestle, [yet] will not his foolishness depart from him.
kjv.27:23: Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, [and] look well to thy herds.
kjv.27:24: For riches [are] not for ever: and doth the crown [endure] to every generation?
kjv.27:25: The hay appeareth, and the tender grass sheweth itself, and herbs of the mountains are gathered.
kjv.27:26: The lambs [are] for thy clothing, and the goats [are] the price of the field.
kjv.27:27: And [thou shalt have] goats' milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, and [for] the maintenance for thy maidens.
kjv.28:1: The wicked flee when no man pursueth: but the righteous are bold as a lion.
kjv.28:2: For the transgression of a land many [are] the princes thereof: but by a man of understanding [and] knowledge the state [thereof] shall be prolonged.
kjv.28:3: A poor man that oppresseth the poor [is like] a sweeping rain which leaveth no food.
kjv.28:4: They that forsake the law praise the wicked: but such as keep the law contend with them.
kjv.28:5: Evil men understand not judgment: but they that seek the LORD understand all [things].
kjv.28:6: Better [is] the poor that walketh in his uprightness, than [he that is] perverse [in his] ways, though he [be] rich.
kjv.28:7: Whoso keepeth the law [is] a wise son: but he that is a companion of riotous [men] shameth his father.
kjv.28:8: He that by usury and unjust gain increaseth his substance, he shall gather it for him that will pity the poor.
kjv.28:9: He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer [shall be] abomination.
kjv.28:10: Whoso causeth the righteous to go astray in an evil way, he shall fall himself into his own pit: but the upright shall have good [things] in possession.
kjv.28:11: The rich man [is] wise in his own conceit; but the poor that hath understanding searcheth him out.
