bsb.26:14: As a door turns on its hinges, so the slacker turns on his bed.
bsb.26:15: The slacker buries his hand in the dish; it wearies him to bring it back to his mouth.
bsb.26:16: The slacker is wiser in his own eyes than seven men who answer discreetly.
bsb.26:17: Like one who grabs a dog by the ears is a passerby who meddles in a quarrel not his own.
bsb.26:18: Like a madman shooting firebrands and deadly arrows,
bsb.26:19: so is the man who deceives his neighbor and says, “I was only joking!”
bsb.26:20: Without wood, a fire goes out; without gossip, a conflict ceases.
bsb.26:21: Like charcoal for embers and wood for fire, so is a quarrelsome man for kindling strife.
bsb.26:22: The words of a gossip are like choice morsels that go down into the inmost being.
bsb.26:23: Like glaze covering an earthen vessel are burning lips and a wicked heart.
bsb.26:24: A hateful man disguises himself with his speech, but he lays up deceit in his heart.
bsb.26:25: When he speaks graciously, do not believe him, for seven abominations fill his heart.
bsb.26:26: Though his hatred is concealed by deception, his wickedness will be exposed in the assembly.
bsb.26:27: He who digs a pit will fall into it, and he who rolls a stone will have it roll back on him.
bsb.26:28: A lying tongue hates those it crushes, and a flattering mouth causes ruin.
bsb.27:1: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring.
bsb.27:2: Let another praise you, and not your own mouth— a stranger, and not your own lips.
bsb.27:3: A stone is heavy and sand is a burden, but aggravation from a fool outweighs them both.
bsb.27:4: Wrath is cruel and anger is like a flood, but who can withstand jealousy?
bsb.27:5: Better an open rebuke than love that is concealed.
bsb.27:6: The wounds of a friend are faithful, but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.
bsb.27:7: The soul that is full loathes honey, but to a hungry soul, any bitter thing is sweet.
bsb.27:8: Like a bird that strays from its nest is a man who wanders from his home.
bsb.27:9: Oil and incense bring joy to the heart, and the sweetness of a friend is counsel to the soul.
bsb.27:10: Do not forsake your friend or your father’s friend, and do not go to your brother’s house in the day of your calamity; better a neighbor nearby than a brother far away.
bsb.27:11: Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart, so that I can answer him who taunts me.
bsb.27:12: The prudent see danger and take cover; but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
bsb.27:13: Take the garment of him who posts security for a stranger; get collateral if it is for a foreigner.
bsb.27:14: If one blesses his neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning, it will be counted to him as a curse.
bsb.27:15: A constant dripping on a rainy day and a contentious woman are alike—
bsb.27:16: restraining her is like holding back the wind or grasping oil with one’s right hand.
bsb.27:17: As iron sharpens iron, so one man sharpens another.
bsb.27:18: Whoever tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, and he who looks after his master will be honored.
bsb.27:19: As water reflects the face, so the heart reflects the true man.
bsb.27:20: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; so the eyes of man are never satisfied.
bsb.27:21: A crucible for silver and a furnace for gold, but a man is tested by the praise accorded him.
bsb.27:22: Though you grind a fool like grain with mortar and a pestle, yet his folly will not depart from him.
bsb.27:23: Be sure to know the state of your flocks, and pay close attention to your herds;
bsb.27:24: for riches are not forever, nor does a crown endure to every generation.
bsb.27:25: When hay is removed and new growth appears and the grain from the hills is gathered,
bsb.27:26: the lambs will provide you with clothing, and the goats with the price of a field.
bsb.27:27: You will have plenty of goats’ milk to feed you— food for your household and nourishment for your maidservants.
bsb.28:1: The wicked flee when no one pursues, but the righteous are as bold as a lion.
bsb.28:2: A land in rebellion has many rulers, but a man of understanding and knowledge maintains order.
bsb.28:3: A destitute leader who oppresses the poor is like a driving rain that leaves no food.
bsb.28:4: Those who forsake the law praise the wicked, but those who keep the law resist them.
bsb.28:5: Evil men do not understand justice, but those who seek the LORD comprehend fully.
bsb.28:6: Better a poor man who walks with integrity than a rich man whose ways are perverse.
bsb.28:7: A discerning son keeps the law, but a companion of gluttons disgraces his father.
bsb.28:8: He who increases his wealth by interest and usury lays it up for one who is kind to the poor.
bsb.28:9: Whoever turns his ear away from hearing the law, even his prayer is detestable.
bsb.28:10: He who leads the upright along the path of evil will fall into his own pit, but the blameless will inherit what is good.
bsb.28:11: A rich man is wise in his own eyes, but a poor man with discernment sees through him.
bsb.28:12: When the righteous triumph, there is great glory, but when the wicked rise, men hide themselves.
bsb.28:13: He who conceals his sins will not prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them will find mercy.
bsb.28:14: Blessed is the man who is always reverent, but he who hardens his heart falls into trouble.
bsb.28:15: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.
bsb.28:16: A leader who lacks judgment is also a great oppressor, but he who hates dishonest profit will prolong his days.
bsb.28:17: A man burdened by bloodguilt will flee into the Pit; let no one support him.
bsb.28:18: He who walks with integrity will be kept safe, but whoever is perverse in his ways will suddenly fall.
bsb.28:19: The one who works his land will have plenty of food, but whoever chases fantasies will have his fill of poverty.
bsb.28:20: A faithful man will abound with blessings, but one eager to be rich will not go unpunished.
bsb.28:21: To show partiality is not good, yet a man will do wrong for a piece of bread.
bsb.28:22: A stingy man hastens after wealth and does not know that poverty awaits him.
bsb.28:23: He who rebukes a man will later find more favor than one who flatters with his tongue.
bsb.28:24: He who robs his father or mother, saying, “It is not wrong,” is a companion to the man who destroys.
bsb.28:25: A greedy man stirs up strife, but he who trusts in the LORD will prosper.
bsb.28:26: He who trusts in himself is a fool, but one who walks in wisdom will be safe.
bsb.28:27: Whoever gives to the poor will not be in need, but he who hides his eyes will receive many curses.
bsb.28:28: When the wicked come to power, people hide themselves; but when they perish, the righteous flourish.
bsb.29:1: A man who remains stiff-necked after much reproof will suddenly be shattered beyond recovery.
bsb.29:2: When the righteous flourish, the people rejoice, but when the wicked rule, the people groan.
bsb.29:3: A man who loves wisdom brings joy to his father, but a companion of prostitutes squanders his wealth.
bsb.29:4: By justice a king brings stability to the land, but a man who exacts tribute demolishes it.
bsb.29:5: A man who flatters his neighbor spreads a net for his feet.
bsb.29:6: An evil man is caught by his own sin, but a righteous one sings and rejoices.
bsb.29:7: The righteous consider the cause of the poor, but the wicked have no regard for such concerns.
bsb.29:8: Mockers inflame a city, but the wise turn away anger.
bsb.29:9: If a wise man goes to court with a fool, there will be raving and laughing with no resolution.
bsb.29:10: Men of bloodshed hate a blameless man, but the upright care for his life.
bsb.29:11: A fool vents all his anger, but a wise man holds it back.
bsb.29:12: If a ruler listens to lies, all his officials will be wicked.
bsb.29:13: The poor man and the oppressor have this in common: The LORD gives light to the eyes of both.
bsb.29:14: A king who judges the poor with fairness— his throne will be established forever.
bsb.29:15: A rod of correction imparts wisdom, but a child left to himself disgraces his mother.
bsb.29:16: When the wicked thrive, rebellion increases; but the righteous will see their downfall.
bsb.29:17: Discipline your son, and he will give you rest; he will bring delight to your soul.
bsb.29:18: Where there is no vision, the people cast off restraint; but blessed is he who keeps the Law.
bsb.29:19: A servant cannot be corrected by words alone; though he understands, he will not respond.
bsb.29:20: Do you see a man who speaks in haste? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
bsb.29:21: A servant pampered from his youth will bring grief in the end.
bsb.29:22: An angry man stirs up dissension, and a hot-tempered man abounds in transgression.
bsb.29:23: A man’s pride will bring him low, but a humble spirit will obtain honor.
bsb.29:24: A partner to a thief hates his own soul; he receives the oath, but does not testify.
bsb.29:25: The fear of man is a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is set securely on high.
bsb.29:26: Many seek the ruler’s favor, but a man receives justice from the LORD.
bsb.29:27: An unjust man is detestable to the righteous, and one whose way is upright is detestable to the wicked.
bsb.30:1: These are the words of Agur son of Jakeh—the burden that this man declared to Ithiel: “I am weary, O God, and worn out.
bsb.30:2: Surely I am the most ignorant of men, and I lack the understanding of a man.
bsb.30:3: I have not learned wisdom, and I have no knowledge of the Holy One.
bsb.30:4: Who has ascended to heaven and come down? Who has gathered the wind in His hands? Who has bound up the waters in His cloak? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is His name, and what is the name of His Son— surely you know!
bsb.30:5: Every word of God is flawless; He is a shield to those who take refuge in Him.
bsb.30:6: Do not add to His words, lest He rebuke you and prove you a liar.
bsb.30:7: Two things I ask of You— do not refuse me before I die:
bsb.30:8: Keep falsehood and deceitful words far from me. Give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with the bread that is my portion.
bsb.30:9: Otherwise, I may have too much and deny You, saying, ‘Who is the LORD?’ Or I may become poor and steal, profaning the name of my God.
bsb.30:10: Do not slander a servant to his master, or he will curse you, and you will bear the guilt.
bsb.30:11: There is a generation of those who curse their fathers and do not bless their mothers.
bsb.30:12: There is a generation of those who are pure in their own eyes and yet unwashed of their filth.
bsb.30:13: There is a generation—how haughty are their eyes and pretentious are their glances—
bsb.30:14: there is a generation whose teeth are swords and whose jaws are knives, devouring the oppressed from the earth and the needy from among men.
bsb.30:15: The leech has two daughters: Give and Give. There are three things that are never satisfied, four that never say, ‘Enough!’:
bsb.30:16: Sheol, the barren womb, land never satisfied with water, and fire that never says, ‘Enough!’
bsb.30:17: As for the eye that mocks a father and scorns obedience to a mother, may the ravens of the valley pluck it out and young vultures devour it.
bsb.30:18: There are three things too wonderful for me, four that I cannot understand:
bsb.30:19: the way of an eagle in the sky, the way of a snake on a rock, the way of a ship at sea, and the way of a man with a maiden.
bsb.30:20: This is the way of an adulteress: She eats and wipes her mouth and says, ‘I have done nothing wrong.’
bsb.30:21: Under three things the earth trembles, under four it cannot bear up:
bsb.30:22: a servant who becomes king, a fool who is filled with food,
bsb.30:23: an unloved woman who marries, and a maidservant who supplants her mistress.
bsb.30:24: Four things on earth are small, yet they are exceedingly wise:
bsb.30:25: The ants are creatures of little strength, yet they store up their food in the summer;
bsb.30:26: the rock badgers are creatures of little power, yet they make their homes in the rocks;
bsb.30:27: the locusts have no king, yet they all advance in formation;
bsb.30:28: and the lizard can be caught in one’s hands, yet it is found in the palaces of kings.
bsb.30:29: There are three things that are stately in their stride, and four that are impressive in their walk:
bsb.30:30: a lion, mighty among beasts, refusing to retreat before anything;
bsb.30:31: a strutting rooster; a he-goat; and a king with his army around him.
bsb.30:32: If you have foolishly exalted yourself or if you have plotted evil, put your hand over your mouth.
bsb.30:33: For as the churning of milk yields butter, and the twisting of the nose draws blood, so the stirring of anger brings forth strife.”
bsb.31:1: These are the words of King Lemuel—the burden that his mother taught him:
bsb.31:2: What shall I say, O my son? What, O son of my womb? What, O son of my vows?
bsb.31:3: Do not spend your strength on women or your vigor on those who ruin kings.
bsb.31:4: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine, or for rulers to crave strong drink,
bsb.31:5: lest they drink and forget what is decreed, depriving all the oppressed of justice.
bsb.31:6: Give strong drink to one who is perishing, and wine to the bitter in soul.
bsb.31:7: Let him drink and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.
bsb.31:8: Open your mouth for those with no voice, for the cause of all the dispossessed.
bsb.31:9: Open your mouth, judge righteously, and defend the cause of the poor and needy.
bsb.31:10: A wife of noble character, who can find? She is far more precious than rubies.
bsb.31:11: The heart of her husband trusts in her, and he lacks nothing of value.
bsb.31:12: She brings him good and not harm all the days of her life.
bsb.31:13: She selects wool and flax and works with eager hands.
bsb.31:14: She is like the merchant ships, bringing her food from afar.
bsb.31:15: She rises while it is still night to provide food for her household and portions for her maidservants.
bsb.31:16: She appraises a field and buys it; from her earnings she plants a vineyard.
bsb.31:17: She girds herself with strength and shows that her arms are strong.
bsb.31:18: She sees that her gain is good, and her lamp is not extinguished at night.
bsb.31:19: She stretches out her hands to the distaff and grasps the spindle with her fingers.
bsb.31:20: She opens her arms to the poor and reaches out her hands to the needy.
bsb.31:21: When it snows, she has no fear for her household, for they are all clothed in scarlet.
bsb.31:22: She makes coverings for her bed; her clothing is fine linen and purple.
bsb.31:23: Her husband is known at the city gate, where he sits among the elders of the land.
bsb.31:24: She makes linen garments and sells them; she delivers sashes to the merchants.
bsb.31:25: Strength and honor are her clothing, and she can laugh at the days to come.
bsb.31:26: She opens her mouth with wisdom, and faithful instruction is on her tongue.
bsb.31:27: She watches over the affairs of her household and does not eat the bread of idleness.
bsb.31:28: Her children rise up and call her blessed; her husband praises her as well:
bsb.31:29: “Many daughters have done noble things, but you surpass them all!”
bsb.31:30: Charm is deceptive and beauty is fleeting, but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.
bsb.31:31: Give her the fruit of her hands, and let her works praise her at the gates.

asv.1:1: The proverbs of Solomon the son of David, king of Israel:
asv.1:2: To know wisdom and instruction; To discern the words of understanding;
asv.1:3: To receive instruction in wise dealing, In righteousness and justice and equity;
asv.1:4: To give prudence to the simple, To the young man knowledge and discretion:
asv.1:5: That the wise man may hear, and increase in learning; And that the man of understanding may attain unto sound counsels:
asv.1:6: To understand a proverb, and a figure, The words of the wise, and their dark sayings.
asv.1:7: The fear of Jehovah is the beginning of knowledge; But the foolish despise wisdom and instruction.
asv.1:8: My son, hear the instruction of thy father, And forsake not the law of thy mother:
asv.1:9: For they shall be a chaplet of grace unto thy head, And chains about thy neck.
asv.1:10: My son, if sinners entice thee, Consent thou not.
asv.1:11: If they say, Come with us, Let us lay wait for blood; Let us lurk privily for the innocent without cause;
asv.1:12: Let us swallow them up alive as Sheol, And whole, as those that go down into the pit;
asv.1:13: We shall find all precious substance; We shall fill our houses with spoil;
asv.1:14: Thou shalt cast thy lot among us; We will all have one purse:
asv.1:15: My son, walk not thou in the way with them; Refrain thy foot from their path:
asv.1:16: For their feet run to evil, And they make haste to shed blood.
asv.1:17: For in vain is the net spread In the sight of any bird:
asv.1:18: And these lay wait for their own blood; They lurk privily for their own lives.
asv.1:19: So are the ways of every one that is greedy of gain; It taketh away the life of the owners thereof.
asv.1:20: Wisdom crieth aloud in the street; She uttereth her voice in the broad places;
asv.1:21: She crieth in the chief place of concourse; At the entrance of the gates, In the city, she uttereth her words:
asv.1:22: How long, ye simple ones, will ye love simplicity? And scoffers delight them in scoffing, And fools hate knowledge?
asv.1:23: Turn you at my reproof: Behold, I will pour out my spirit upon you; I will make known my words unto you.
asv.1:24: Because I have called, and ye have refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no man hath regarded;
asv.1:25: But ye have set at nought all my counsel, And would none of my reproof:
asv.1:26: I also will laugh in the day of your calamity; I will mock when your fear cometh;
asv.1:27: When your fear cometh as a storm, And your calamity cometh on as a whirlwind; When distress and anguish come upon you.
asv.1:28: Then will they call upon me, but I will not answer; They will seek me diligently, but they shall not find me:
asv.1:29: For that they hated knowledge, And did not choose the fear of Jehovah,
asv.1:30: They would none of my counsel, They despised all my reproof.
asv.1:31: Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way, And be filled with their own devices.
asv.1:32: For the backsliding of the simple shall slay them, And the careless ease of fools shall destroy them.
asv.1:33: But whoso hearkeneth unto me shall dwell securely, And shall be quiet without fear of evil.
asv.2:1: My son, if thou wilt receive my words, And lay up my commandments with thee;
asv.2:2: So as to incline thine ear unto wisdom, And apply thy heart to understanding;
asv.2:3: Yea, if thou cry after discernment, And lift up thy voice for understanding;
asv.2:4: If thou seek her as silver, And search for her as for hid treasures:
asv.2:5: Then shalt thou understand the fear of Jehovah, And find the knowledge of God.
asv.2:6: For Jehovah giveth wisdom; Out of his mouth cometh knowledge and understanding:
asv.2:7: He layeth up sound wisdom for the upright; He is a shield to them that walk in integrity;
asv.2:8: That he may guard the paths of justice, And preserve the way of his saints.
asv.2:9: Then shalt thou understand righteousness and justice, And equity, yea, every good path.
asv.2:10: For wisdom shall enter into thy heart, And knowledge shall be pleasant unto thy soul;
asv.2:11: Discretion shall watch over thee; Understanding shall keep thee:
asv.2:12: To deliver thee from the way of evil, From the men that speak perverse things;
asv.2:13: Who forsake the paths of uprightness, To walk in the ways of darkness;
asv.2:14: Who rejoice to do evil, And delight in the perverseness of evil;
asv.2:15: Who are crooked in their ways, And wayward in their paths:
asv.2:16: To deliver thee from the strange woman, Even from the foreigner that flattereth with her words;
asv.2:17: That forsaketh the friend of her youth, And forgetteth the covenant of her God:
asv.2:18: For her house inclineth unto death, And her paths unto the dead;
asv.2:19: None that go unto her return again, Neither do they attain unto the paths of life:
asv.2:20: That thou mayest walk in the way of good men, And keep the paths of the righteous.
asv.2:21: For the upright shall dwell in the land, And the perfect shall remain in it.
asv.2:22: But the wicked shall be cut off from the land, And the treacherous shall be rooted out of it.
asv.3:1: My son, forget not my law; But let thy heart keep my commandments:
asv.3:2: For length of days, and years of life, And peace, will they add to thee.
asv.3:3: Let not kindness and truth forsake thee: Bind them about thy neck; Write them upon the tablet of thy heart:
asv.3:4: So shalt thou find favor and good understanding In the sight of God and man.
asv.3:5: Trust in Jehovah with all thy heart, And lean not upon thine own understanding:
asv.3:6: In all thy ways acknowledge him, And he will direct thy paths.
asv.3:7: Be not wise in thine own eyes; Fear Jehovah, and depart from evil:
asv.3:8: It will be health to thy navel, And marrow to thy bones.
asv.3:9: Honor Jehovah with thy substance, And with the first-fruits of all thine increase:
asv.3:10: So shall thy barns be filled with plenty, And thy vats shall overflow with new wine.
asv.3:11: My son, despise not the chastening of Jehovah; Neither be weary of his reproof:
asv.3:12: For whom Jehovah loveth he reproveth, Even as a father the son in whom he delighteth.
asv.3:13: Happy is the man that findeth wisdom, And the man that getteth understanding.
asv.3:14: For the gaining of it is better than the gaining of silver, And the profit thereof than fine gold.
asv.3:15: She is more precious than rubies: And none of the things thou canst desire are to be compared unto her.
asv.3:16: Length of days is in her right hand; In her left hand are riches and honor.
asv.3:17: Her ways are ways of pleasantness, And all her paths are peace.
asv.3:18: She is a tree of life to them that lay hold upon her: And happy is every one that retaineth her.
asv.3:19: Jehovah by wisdom founded the earth; By understanding he established the heavens.
asv.3:20: By his knowledge the depths were broken up, And the skies drop down the dew.
asv.3:21: My son, let them not depart from thine eyes; Keep sound wisdom and discretion:
asv.3:22: So shall they be life unto thy soul, And grace to thy neck.
asv.3:23: Then shalt thou walk in thy way securely, And thy foot shall not stumble.
asv.3:24: When thou liest down, thou shalt not be afraid: Yea, thou shalt lie down, and thy sleep shall be sweet.
asv.3:25: Be not afraid of sudden fear, Neither of the desolation of the wicked, when it cometh:
asv.3:26: For Jehovah will be thy confidence, And will keep thy foot from being taken.
asv.3:27: Withhold not good from them to whom it is due, When it is in the power of thy hand to do it.
asv.3:28: Say not unto thy neighbor, Go, and come again, And to-morrow I will give; When thou hast it by thee.
asv.3:29: Devise not evil against thy neighbor, Seeing he dwelleth securely by thee.
asv.3:30: Strive not with a man without cause, If he have done thee no harm.
asv.3:31: Envy thou not the man of violence, And choose none of his ways.
asv.3:32: For the perverse is an abomination to Jehovah; But his friendship is with the upright.
asv.3:33: The curse of Jehovah is in the house of the wicked; But he blesseth the habitation of the righteous.
asv.3:34: Surely he scoffeth at the scoffers; But he giveth grace unto the lowly.
asv.3:35: The wise shall inherit glory; But shame shall be the promotion of fools.
asv.4:1: Hear, my sons, the instruction of a father, And attend to know understanding:
asv.4:2: For I give you good doctrine; Forsake ye not my law.
asv.4:3: For I was a son unto my father, Tender and only beloved in the sight of my mother.
asv.4:4: And he taught me, and said unto me: Let thy heart retain my words; Keep my commandments, and live;
asv.4:5: Get wisdom, get understanding; Forget not, neither decline from the words of my mouth;
asv.4:6: Forsake her not, and she will preserve thee; Love her, and she will keep thee.
asv.4:7: Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom; Yea, with all thy getting get understanding.
asv.4:8: Exalt her, and she will promote thee; She will bring thee to honor, when thou dost embrace her.
asv.4:9: She will give to thy head a chaplet of grace; A crown of beauty will she deliver to thee.
asv.4:10: Hear, O my son, and receive my sayings; And the years of thy life shall be many.
asv.4:11: I have taught thee in the way of wisdom; I have led thee in paths of uprightness.
asv.4:12: When thou goest, thy steps shall not be straitened; And if thou runnest, thou shalt not stumble.
asv.4:13: Take fast hold of instruction; let her not go: Keep her; for she is thy life.
asv.4:14: Enter not into the path of the wicked, And walk not in the way of evil men.
asv.4:15: Avoid it, pass not by it; Turn from it, and pass on.
asv.4:16: For they sleep not, except they do evil; And their sleep is taken away, unless they cause some to fall.
asv.4:17: For they eat the bread of wickedness, And drink the wine of violence.
asv.4:18: But the path of the righteous is as the dawning light, That shineth more and more unto the perfect day.
asv.4:19: The way of the wicked is as darkness: They know not at what they stumble.
asv.4:20: My son, attend to my words; Incline thine ear unto my sayings.
asv.4:21: Let them not depart from thine eyes; Keep them in the midst of thy heart.
asv.4:22: For they are life unto those that find them, And health to all their flesh.
asv.4:23: Keep thy heart with all diligence; For out of it are the issues of life.
asv.4:24: Put away from thee a wayward mouth, And perverse lips put far from thee.
asv.4:25: Let thine eyes look right on, And let thine eyelids look straight before thee.
asv.4:26: Make level the path of thy feet, And let all thy ways be established.
asv.4:27: Turn not to the right hand nor to the left: Remove thy foot from evil.
asv.5:1: My son, attend unto my wisdom; Incline thine ear to my understanding:
asv.5:2: That thou mayest preserve discretion, And that thy lips may keep knowledge.
asv.5:3: For the lips of a strange woman drop honey, And her mouth is smoother than oil:
asv.5:4: But in the end she is bitter as wormwood, Sharp as a two-edged sword.
asv.5:5: Her feet go down to death; Her steps take hold on Sheol;
asv.5:6: So that she findeth not the level path of life: Her ways are unstable, and she knoweth it not.
asv.5:7: Now therefore, my sons, hearken unto me, And depart not from the words of my mouth.
asv.5:8: Remove thy way far from her, And come not nigh the door of her house;
asv.5:9: Lest thou give thine honor unto others, And thy years unto the cruel;
asv.5:10: Lest strangers be filled with thy strength, And thy labors be in the house of an alien,
asv.5:11: And thou mourn at thy latter end, When thy flesh and thy body are consumed,
asv.5:12: And say, How have I hated instruction, And my heart despised reproof;
asv.5:13: Neither have I obeyed the voice of my teachers, Nor inclined mine ear to them that instructed me!
asv.5:14: I was well-nigh in all evil In the midst of the assembly and congregation.
asv.5:15: Drink waters out of thine own cistern, And running waters out of thine own well.
asv.5:16: Should thy springs be dispersed abroad, And streams of water in the streets?
asv.5:17: Let them be for thyself alone, And not for strangers with thee.
asv.5:18: Let thy fountain be blessed; And rejoice in the wife of thy youth.
asv.5:19: As a loving hind and a pleasant doe, Let her breasts satisfy thee at all times; And be thou ravished always with her love.
asv.5:20: For why shouldest thou, my son, be ravished with a strange woman, And embrace the bosom of a foreigner?
asv.5:21: For the ways of man are before the eyes of Jehovah; And he maketh level all his paths.
asv.5:22: His own iniquities shall take the wicked, And he shall be holden with the cords of his sin.
asv.5:23: He shall die for lack of instruction; And in the greatness of his folly he shall go astray.
asv.6:1: My son, if thou art become surety for thy neighbor, If thou hast stricken thy hands for a stranger;
asv.6:2: Thou art snared with the words of thy mouth, Thou art taken with the words of thy mouth.
asv.6:3: Do this now, my son, and deliver thyself, Seeing thou art come into the hand of thy neighbor: Go, humble thyself, and importune thy neighbor;
asv.6:4: Give not sleep to thine eyes, Nor slumber to thine eyelids;
asv.6:5: Deliver thyself as a roe from the hand of the hunter, And as a bird from the hand of the fowler.
asv.6:6: Go to the ant, thou sluggard; Consider her ways, and be wise:
asv.6:7: Which having no chief, Overseer, or ruler,
asv.6:8: Provideth her bread in the summer, And gathereth her food in the harvest.
asv.6:9: How long wilt thou sleep, O sluggard? When wilt thou arise out of thy sleep?
asv.6:10: Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, A little folding of the hands to sleep:
asv.6:11: So shall thy poverty come as a robber, And thy want as an armed man.
asv.6:12: A worthless person, a man of iniquity, Is he that walketh with a perverse mouth;
asv.6:13: That winketh with his eyes, that speaketh with his feet, That maketh signs with his fingers;
asv.6:14: In whose heart is perverseness, Who deviseth evil continually, Who soweth discord.
asv.6:15: Therefore shall his calamity come suddenly; On a sudden shall he be broken, and that without remedy.
asv.6:16: There are six things which Jehovah hateth; Yea, seven which are an abomination unto him:
asv.6:17: Haughty eyes, a lying tongue, And hands that shed innocent blood;
asv.6:18: A heart that deviseth wicked purposes, Feet that are swift in running to mischief,
asv.6:19: A false witness that uttereth lies, And he that soweth discord among brethren.
asv.6:20: My son, keep the commandment of thy father, And forsake not the law of thy mother:
asv.6:21: Bind them continually upon thy heart; Tie them about thy neck.
asv.6:22: When thou walkest, it shall lead thee; When thou sleepest, it shall watch over thee; And when thou awakest, it shall talk with thee.
asv.6:23: For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; And reproofs of instruction are the way of life:
asv.6:24: To keep thee from the evil woman, From the flattery of the foreigner’s tongue.
asv.6:25: Lust not after her beauty in thy heart; Neither let her take thee with her eyelids.
asv.6:26: For on account of a harlot a man is brought to a piece of bread; And the adulteress hunteth for the precious life.
asv.6:27: Can a man take fire in his bosom, And his clothes not be burned?
asv.6:28: Or can one walk upon hot coals, And his feet not be scorched?
asv.6:29: So he that goeth in to his neighbor’s wife; Whosoever toucheth her shall not be unpunished.
asv.6:30: Men do not despise a thief, if he steal To satisfy himself when he is hungry:
asv.6:31: But if he be found, he shall restore sevenfold; He shall give all the substance of his house.
asv.6:32: He that committeth adultery with a woman is void of understanding: He doeth it who would destroy his own soul.
asv.6:33: Wounds and dishonor shall he get; And his reproach shall not be wiped away.
asv.6:34: For jealousy is the rage of a man; And he will not spare in the day of vengeance.
asv.6:35: He will not regard any ransom; Neither will he rest content, though thou givest many gifts.
asv.7:1: My son, keep my words, And lay up my commandments with thee.
asv.7:2: Keep my commandments and live; And my law as the apple of thine eye.
asv.7:3: Bind them upon thy fingers; Write them upon the tablet of thy heart.
asv.7:4: Say unto wisdom, Thou art my sister; And call understanding thy kinswoman:
asv.7:5: That they may keep thee from the strange woman, From the foreigner that flattereth with her words.
asv.7:6: For at the window of my house I looked forth through my lattice;
asv.7:7: And I beheld among the simple ones, I discerned among the youths, A young man void of understanding,
asv.7:8: Passing through the street near her corner; And he went the way to her house,
asv.7:9: In the twilight, in the evening of the day, In the middle of the night and in the darkness.
asv.7:10: And, behold, there met him a woman With the attire of a harlot, and wily of heart.
asv.7:11: (She is clamorous and wilful; Her feet abide not in her house:
asv.7:12: Now she is in the streets, now in the broad places, And lieth in wait at every corner.)
asv.7:13: So she caught him, and kissed him, And with an impudent face she said unto him:
asv.7:14: Sacrifices of peace-offerings are with me; This day have I paid my vows.
asv.7:15: Therefore came I forth to meet thee, Diligently to seek thy face, and I have found thee.
asv.7:16: I have spread my couch with carpets of tapestry, With striped cloths of the yarn of Egypt.
asv.7:17: I have perfumed my bed With myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.
asv.7:18: Come, let us take our fill of love until the morning; Let us solace ourselves with loves.
asv.7:19: For the man is not at home; He is gone a long journey:
asv.7:20: He hath taken a bag of money with him; He will come home at the full moon.
asv.7:21: With her much fair speech she causeth him to yield; With the flattering of her lips she forceth him along.
asv.7:22: He goeth after her straightway, As an ox goeth to the slaughter, Or as one in fetters to the correction of the fool;
asv.7:23: Till an arrow strike through his liver; As a bird hasteth to the snare, And knoweth not that it is for his life.
asv.7:24: Now therefore, my sons, hearken unto me, And attend to the words of my mouth.
asv.7:25: Let not thy heart decline to her ways; Go not astray in her paths.
asv.7:26: For she hath cast down many wounded: Yea, all her slain are a mighty host.
asv.7:27: Her house is the way to Sheol, Going down to the chambers of death.
asv.8:1: Doth not wisdom cry, And understanding put forth her voice?
asv.8:2: On the top of high places by the way, Where the paths meet, she standeth;
asv.8:3: Beside the gates, at the entry of the city, At the coming in at the doors, she crieth aloud:
asv.8:4: Unto you, O men, I call; And my voice is to the sons of men.
asv.8:5: O ye simple, understand prudence; And, ye fools, be of an understanding heart.
asv.8:6: Hear, for I will speak excellent things; And the opening of my lips shall be right things.
asv.8:7: For my mouth shall utter truth; And wickedness is an abomination to my lips.
asv.8:8: All the words of my mouth are in righteousness; There is nothing crooked or perverse in them.
asv.8:9: They are all plain to him that understandeth, And right to them that find knowledge.
asv.8:10: Receive my instruction, and not silver; And knowledge rather than choice gold.
asv.8:11: For wisdom is better than rubies; And all the things that may be desired are not to be compared unto it.
asv.8:12: I wisdom have made prudence my dwelling, And find out knowledge and discretion.
asv.8:13: The fear of Jehovah is to hate evil: Pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, And the perverse mouth, do I hate.
asv.8:14: Counsel is mine, and sound knowledge: I am understanding; I have might.
asv.8:15: By me kings reign, And princes decree justice.
asv.8:16: By me princes rule, And nobles, even all the judges of the earth.
asv.8:17: I love them that love me; And those that seek me diligently shall find me.
asv.8:18: Riches and honor are with me; Yea, durable wealth and righteousness.
asv.8:19: My fruit is better than gold, yea, than fine gold; And my revenue than choice silver.
asv.8:20: I walk in the way of righteousness, In the midst of the paths of justice;
asv.8:21: That I may cause those that love me to inherit substance, And that I may fill their treasuries.
asv.8:22: Jehovah possessed me in the beginning of his way, Before his works of old.
asv.8:23: I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, Before the earth was.
asv.8:24: When there were no depths, I was brought forth, When there were no fountains abounding with water.
asv.8:25: Before the mountains were settled, Before the hills was I brought forth;
asv.8:26: While as yet he had not made the earth, nor the fields, Nor the beginning of the dust of the world.
asv.8:27: When he established the heavens, I was there: When he set a circle upon the face of the deep,
asv.8:28: When he made firm the skies above, When the fountains of the deep became strong,
asv.8:29: When he gave to the sea its bound, That the waters should not transgress his commandment, When he marked out the foundations of the earth;
asv.8:30: Then I was by him, as a master workman; And I was daily his delight, Rejoicing always before him,
asv.8:31: Rejoicing in his habitable earth; And my delight was with the sons of men.
asv.8:32: Now therefore, my sons, hearken unto me; For blessed are they that keep my ways.
asv.8:33: Hear instruction, and be wise, And refuse it not.
asv.8:34: Blessed is the man that heareth me, Watching daily at my gates, Waiting at the posts of my doors.
asv.8:35: For whoso findeth me findeth life, And shall obtain favor of Jehovah.
asv.8:36: But he that sinneth against me wrongeth his own soul: All they that hate me love death.
asv.9:1: Wisdom hath builded her house; She hath hewn out her seven pillars:
asv.9:2: She hath killed her beasts; she hath mingled her wine; She hath also furnished her table:
asv.9:3: She hath sent forth her maidens; She crieth upon the highest places of the city:
asv.9:4: Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither: As for him that is void of understanding, she saith to him,
asv.9:5: Come, eat ye of my bread, And drink of the wine which I have mingled.
asv.9:6: Leave off, ye simple ones, and live; And walk in the way of understanding.
asv.9:7: He that correcteth a scoffer getteth to himself reviling; And he that reproveth a wicked man getteth himself a blot.
asv.9:8: Reprove not a scoffer, lest he hate thee: Reprove a wise man, and he will love thee.
asv.9:9: Give instruction to a wise man, and he will be yet wiser: Teach a righteous man, and he will increase in learning.
asv.9:10: The fear of Jehovah is the beginning of wisdom; And the knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.
asv.9:11: For by me thy days shall be multiplied, And the years of thy life shall be increased.
asv.9:12: If thou art wise, thou art wise for thyself; And if thou scoffest, thou alone shalt bear it.
asv.9:13: The foolish woman is clamorous; She is simple, and knoweth nothing.
asv.9:14: And she sitteth at the door of her house, On a seat in the high places of the city,
asv.9:15: To call to them that pass by, Who go right on their ways:
asv.9:16: Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither; And as for him that is void of understanding, she saith to him,
asv.9:17: Stolen waters are sweet, And bread eaten in secret is pleasant.
asv.9:18: But he knoweth not that the dead are there; That her guests are in the depths of Sheol.
asv.10:1: The proverbs of Solomon. A wise son maketh a glad father; But a foolish son is the heaviness of his mother.
asv.10:2: Treasures of wickedness profit nothing; But righteousness delivereth from death.
asv.10:3: Jehovah will not suffer the soul of the righteous to famish; But he thrusteth away the desire of the wicked.
asv.10:4: He becometh poor that worketh with a slack hand; But the hand of the diligent maketh rich.
asv.10:5: He that gathereth in summer is a wise son; But he that sleepeth in harvest is a son that causeth shame.
asv.10:6: Blessings are upon the head of the righteous; But violence covereth the mouth of the wicked.
asv.10:7: The memory of the righteous is blessed; But the name of the wicked shall rot.
asv.10:8: The wise in heart will receive commandments; But a prating fool shall fall.
asv.10:9: He that walketh uprightly walketh surely; But he that perverteth his ways shall be known.
asv.10:10: He that winketh with the eye causeth sorrow; But a prating fool shall fall.
asv.10:11: The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life; But violence covereth the mouth of the wicked.
asv.10:12: Hatred stirreth up strifes; But love covereth all transgressions.
asv.10:13: In the lips of him that hath discernment wisdom is found; But a rod is for the back of him that is void of understanding.
asv.10:14: Wise men lay up knowledge; But the mouth of the foolish is a present destruction.
asv.10:15: The rich man’s wealth is his strong city: The destruction of the poor is their poverty.
asv.10:16: The labor of the righteous tendeth to life; The increase of the wicked, to sin.
asv.10:17: He is in the way of life that heedeth correction; But he that forsaketh reproof erreth.
asv.10:18: He that hideth hatred is of lying lips; And he that uttereth a slander is a fool.
asv.10:19: In the multitude of words there wanteth not transgression; But he that refraineth his lips doeth wisely.
asv.10:20: The tongue of the righteous is as choice silver: The heart of the wicked is little worth.
asv.10:21: The lips of the righteous feed many; But the foolish die for lack of understanding.
asv.10:22: The blessing of Jehovah, it maketh rich; And he addeth no sorrow therewith.
asv.10:23: It is as sport to a fool to do wickedness; And so is wisdom to a man of understanding.
asv.10:24: The fear of the wicked, it shall come upon him; And the desire of the righteous shall be granted.
asv.10:25: When the whirlwind passeth, the wicked is no more; But the righteous is an everlasting foundation.
asv.10:26: As vinegar to the teeth, and as smoke to the eyes, So is the sluggard to them that send him.
asv.10:27: The fear of Jehovah prolongeth days; But the years of the wicked shall be shortened.
asv.10:28: The hope of the righteous shall be gladness; But the expectation of the wicked shall perish.
asv.10:29: The way of Jehovah is a stronghold to the upright; But it is a destruction to the workers of iniquity.
asv.10:30: The righteous shall never be removed; But the wicked shall not dwell in the land.
asv.10:31: The mouth of the righteous bringeth forth wisdom; But the perverse tongue shall be cut off.
asv.10:32: The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable; But the mouth of the wicked speaketh perverseness.
asv.11:1: A false balance is an abomination to Jehovah; But a just weight is his delight.
asv.11:2: When pride cometh, then cometh shame; But with the lowly is wisdom.
asv.11:3: The integrity of the upright shall guide them; But the perverseness of the treacherous shall destroy them.
asv.11:4: Riches profit not in the day of wrath; But righteousness delivereth from death.
asv.11:5: The righteousness of the perfect shall direct his way; But the wicked shall fall by his own wickedness.
asv.11:6: The righteousness of the upright shall deliver them; But the treacherous shall be taken in their own iniquity.
asv.11:7: When a wicked man dieth, his expectation shall perish; And the hope of iniquity perisheth.
asv.11:8: The righteous is delivered out of trouble; And the wicked cometh in his stead.
asv.11:9: With his mouth the godless man destroyeth his neighbor; But through knowledge shall the righteous be delivered.
asv.11:10: When it goeth well with the righteous, the city rejoiceth; And when the wicked perish, there is shouting.
asv.11:11: By the blessing of the upright the city is exalted; But it is overthrown by the mouth of the wicked.
asv.11:12: He that despiseth his neighbor is void of wisdom; But a man of understanding holdeth his peace.
asv.11:13: He that goeth about as a tale-bearer revealeth secrets; But he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth a matter.
asv.11:14: Where no wise guidance is, the people falleth; But in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.
asv.11:15: He that is surety for a stranger shall smart for it; But he that hateth suretyship is secure.
asv.11:16: A gracious woman obtaineth honor; And violent men obtain riches.
asv.11:17: The merciful man doeth good to his own soul; But he that is cruel troubleth his own flesh.
asv.11:18: The wicked earneth deceitful wages; But he that soweth righteousness hath a sure reward.
asv.11:19: He that is stedfast in righteousness shall attain unto life; And he that pursueth evil doeth it to his own death.
asv.11:20: They that are perverse in heart are an abomination to Jehovah; But such as are perfect in their way are his delight.
asv.11:21: Though hand join in hand, the evil man shall not be unpunished; But the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.
asv.11:22: As a ring of gold in a swine’s snout, So is a fair woman that is without discretion.
asv.11:23: The desire of the righteous is only good; But the expectation of the wicked is wrath.
asv.11:24: There is that scattereth, and increaseth yet more; And there is that withholdeth more than is meet, but it tendeth only to want.
asv.11:25: The liberal soul shall be made fat; And he that watereth shall be watered also himself.
asv.11:26: He that withholdeth grain, the people shall curse him; But blessing shall be upon the head of him that selleth it.
asv.11:27: He that diligently seeketh good seeketh favor; But he that searcheth after evil, it shall come unto him.
asv.11:28: He that trusteth in his riches shall fall; But the righteous shall flourish as the green leaf.
asv.11:29: He that troubleth his own house shall inherit the wind; And the foolish shall be servant to the wise of heart.
asv.11:30: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life; And he that is wise winneth souls.
asv.11:31: Behold, the righteous shall be recompensed in the earth; How much more the wicked and the sinner!
asv.12:1: Whoso loveth correction loveth knowledge; But he that hateth reproof is brutish.
asv.12:2: A good man shall obtain favor of Jehovah; But a man of wicked devices will he condemn.
asv.12:3: A man shall not be established by wickedness; But the root of the righteous shall not be moved.
asv.12:4: A worthy woman is the crown of her husband; But she that maketh ashamed is as rottenness in his bones.
asv.12:5: The thoughts of the righteous are just; But the counsels of the wicked are deceit.
asv.12:6: The words of the wicked are of lying in wait for blood; But the mouth of the upright shall deliver them.
asv.12:7: The wicked are overthrown, and are not; But the house of the righteous shall stand.
asv.12:8: A man shall be commended according to his wisdom; But he that is of a perverse heart shall be despised.
asv.12:9: Better is he that is lightly esteemed, and hath a servant, Than he that honoreth himself, and lacketh bread.
asv.12:10: A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast; But the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel.
asv.12:11: He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread; But he that followeth after vain persons is void of understanding.
asv.12:12: The wicked desireth the net of evil men; But the root of the righteous yieldeth fruit.
asv.12:13: In the transgression of the lips is a snare to the evil man; But the righteous shall come out of trouble.
asv.12:14: A man shall be satisfied with good by the fruit of his mouth; And the doings of a man’s hands shall be rendered unto him.
asv.12:15: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes; But he that is wise hearkeneth unto counsel.
asv.12:16: A fool’s vexation is presently known; But a prudent man concealeth shame.
asv.12:17: He that uttereth truth showeth forth righteousness; But a false witness, deceit.
asv.12:18: There is that speaketh rashly like the piercings of a sword; But the tongue of the wise is health.
asv.12:19: The lip of truth shall be established for ever; But a lying tongue is but for a moment.
asv.12:20: Deceit is in the heart of them that devise evil; But to the counsellors of peace is joy.
asv.12:21: There shall no mischief happen to the righteous; But the wicked shall be filled with evil.
asv.12:22: Lying lips are an abomination to Jehovah; But they that deal truly are his delight.
asv.12:23: A prudent man concealeth knowledge; But the heart of fools proclaimeth foolishness.
asv.12:24: The hand of the diligent shall bear rule; But the slothful shall be put under taskwork.
asv.12:25: Heaviness in the heart of a man maketh it stoop; But a good word maketh it glad.
asv.12:26: The righteous is a guide to his neighbor; But the way of the wicked causeth them to err.
asv.12:27: The slothful man roasteth not that which he took in hunting; But the precious substance of men is to the diligent.
asv.12:28: In the way of righteousness is life; And in the pathway thereof there is no death.
asv.13:1: A wise son heareth his father’s instruction; But a scoffer heareth not rebuke.
asv.13:2: A man shall eat good by the fruit of his mouth; But the soul of the treacherous shall eat violence.
asv.13:3: He that guardeth his mouth keepeth his life; But he that openeth wide his lips shall have destruction.
asv.13:4: The soul of the sluggard desireth, and hath nothing; But the soul of the diligent shall be made fat.
asv.13:5: A righteous man hateth lying; But a wicked man is loathsome, and cometh to shame.
asv.13:6: Righteousness guardeth him that is upright in the way; But wickedness overthroweth the sinner.
asv.13:7: There is that maketh himself rich, yet hath nothing: There is that maketh himself poor, yet hath great wealth.
asv.13:8: The ransom of a man’s life is his riches; But the poor heareth no threatening.
asv.13:9: The light of the righteous rejoiceth; But the lamp of the wicked shall be put out.
asv.13:10: By pride cometh only contention; But with the well-advised is wisdom.
asv.13:11: Wealth gotten by vanity shall be diminished; But he that gathereth by labor shall have increase.
asv.13:12: Hope deferred maketh the heart sick; But when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life.
asv.13:13: Whoso despiseth the word bringeth destruction on himself; But he that feareth the commandment shall be rewarded.
asv.13:14: The law of the wise is a fountain of life, That one may depart from the snares of death.
asv.13:15: Good understanding giveth favor; But the way of the transgressor is hard.
asv.13:16: Every prudent man worketh with knowledge; But a fool flaunteth his folly.
asv.13:17: A wicked messenger falleth into evil; But a faithful ambassador is health.
asv.13:18: Poverty and shame shall be to him that refuseth correction; But he that regardeth reproof shall be honored.
asv.13:19: The desire accomplished is sweet to the soul; But it is an abomination to fools to depart from evil.
asv.13:20: Walk with wise men, and thou shalt be wise; But the companion of fools shall smart for it.
asv.13:21: Evil pursueth sinners; But the righteous shall be recompensed with good.
asv.13:22: A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children’s children; And the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the righteous.
asv.13:23: Much food is in the tillage of the poor; But there is that is destroyed by reason of injustice.
asv.13:24: He that spareth his rod hateth his son; But he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes.
asv.13:25: The righteous eateth to the satisfying of his soul; But the belly of the wicked shall want.
asv.14:1: Every wise woman buildeth her house; But the foolish plucketh it down with her own hands.
asv.14:2: He that walketh in his uprightness feareth Jehovah; But he that is perverse in his ways despiseth him.
asv.14:3: In the mouth of the foolish is a rod for his pride; But the lips of the wise shall preserve them.
asv.14:4: Where no oxen are, the crib is clean; But much increase is by the strength of the ox.
asv.14:5: A faithful witness will not lie; But a false witness uttereth lies.
asv.14:6: A scoffer seeketh wisdom, and findeth it not; But knowledge is easy unto him that hath understanding.
asv.14:7: Go into the presence of a foolish man, And thou shalt not perceive in him the lips of knowledge.
asv.14:8: The wisdom of the prudent is to understand his way; But the folly of fools is deceit.
asv.14:9: A trespass-offering mocketh fools; But among the upright there is good will.
asv.14:10: The heart knoweth its own bitterness; And a stranger doth not intermeddle with its joy.
asv.14:11: The house of the wicked shall be overthrown; But the tent of the upright shall flourish.
asv.14:12: There is a way which seemeth right unto a man; But the end thereof are the ways of death.
asv.14:13: Even in laughter the heart is sorrowful; And the end of mirth is heaviness.
asv.14:14: The backslider in heart shall be filled with his own ways; And a good man shall be satisfied from himself.
asv.14:15: The simple believeth every word; But the prudent man looketh well to his going.
asv.14:16: A wise man feareth, and departeth from evil; But the fool beareth himself insolently, and is confident.
asv.14:17: He that is soon angry will deal foolishly; And a man of wicked devices is hated.
asv.14:18: The simple inherit folly; But the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
asv.14:19: The evil bow down before the good; And the wicked, at the gates of the righteous.
asv.14:20: The poor is hated even of his own neighbor; But the rich hath many friends.
asv.14:21: He that despiseth his neighbor sinneth; But he that hath pity on the poor, happy is he.
asv.14:22: Do they not err that devise evil? But mercy and truth shall be to them that devise good.
asv.14:23: In all labor there is profit; But the talk of the lips tendeth only to penury.
asv.14:24: The crown of the wise is their riches; But the folly of fools is only folly.
asv.14:25: A true witness delivereth souls; But he that uttereth lies causeth deceit.
asv.14:26: In the fear of Jehovah is strong confidence; And his children shall have a place of refuge.
asv.14:27: The fear of Jehovah is a fountain of life, That one may depart from the snares of death.
asv.14:28: In the multitude of people is the king’s glory; But in the want of people is the destruction of the prince.
asv.14:29: He that is slow to anger is of great understanding; But he that is hasty of spirit exalteth folly.
asv.14:30: A tranquil heart is the life of the flesh; But envy is the rottenness of the bones.
asv.14:31: He that oppresseth the poor reproacheth his Maker; But he that hath mercy on the needy honoreth him.
asv.14:32: The wicked is thrust down in his evil-doing; But the righteous hath a refuge in his death.
asv.14:33: Wisdom resteth in the heart of him that hath understanding; But that which is in the inward part of fools is made known.
asv.14:34: Righteousness exalteth a nation; But sin is a reproach to any people.
asv.14:35: The king’s favor is toward a servant that dealeth wisely; But his wrath will be against him that causeth shame.
asv.15:1: A soft answer turneth away wrath; But a grievous word stirreth up anger.
asv.15:2: The tongue of the wise uttereth knowledge aright; But the mouth of fools poureth out folly.
asv.15:3: The eyes of Jehovah are in every place, Keeping watch upon the evil and the good.
asv.15:4: A gentle tongue is a tree of life; But perverseness therein is a breaking of the spirit.
asv.15:5: A fool despiseth his father’s correction; But he that regardeth reproof getteth prudence.
asv.15:6: In the house of the righteous is much treasure; But in the revenues of the wicked is trouble.
asv.15:7: The lips of the wise disperse knowledge; But the heart of the foolish doeth not so.
asv.15:8: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to Jehovah; But the prayer of the upright is his delight.
asv.15:9: The way of the wicked is an abomination to Jehovah; But he loveth him that followeth after righteousness.
asv.15:10: There is grievous correction for him that forsaketh the way; And he that hateth reproof shall die.
asv.15:11: Sheol and Abaddon are before Jehovah; How much more then the hearts of the children of men!
asv.15:12: A scoffer loveth not to be reproved; He will not go unto the wise.
asv.15:13: A glad heart maketh a cheerful countenance; But by sorrow of heart the spirit is broken.
asv.15:14: The heart of him that hath understanding seeketh knowledge; But the mouth of fools feedeth on folly.
asv.15:15: All the days of the afflicted are evil; But he that is of a cheerful heart hath a continual feast.
asv.15:16: Better is little, with the fear of Jehovah, Than great treasure and trouble therewith.
asv.15:17: Better is a dinner of herbs, where love is, Than a stalled ox and hatred therewith.
asv.15:18: A wrathful man stirreth up contention; But he that is slow to anger appeaseth strife.
asv.15:19: The way of the sluggard is as a hedge of thorns; But the path of the upright is made a highway.
asv.15:20: A wise son maketh a glad father; But a foolish man despiseth his mother.
asv.15:21: Folly is joy to him that is void of wisdom; But a man of understanding maketh straight his going.
asv.15:22: Where there is no counsel, purposes are disappointed; But in the multitude of counsellors they are established.
asv.15:23: A man hath joy in the answer of his mouth; And a word in due season, how good is it!
asv.15:24: To the wise the way of life goeth upward, That he may depart from Sheol beneath.
asv.15:25: Jehovah will root up the house of the proud; But he will establish the border of the widow.
asv.15:26: Evil devices are an abomination to Jehovah; But pleasant words are pure.
asv.15:27: He that is greedy of gain troubleth his own house; But he that hateth bribes shall live.
asv.15:28: The heart of the righteous studieth to answer; But the mouth of the wicked poureth out evil things.
asv.15:29: Jehovah is far from the wicked; But he heareth the prayer of the righteous.
asv.15:30: The light of the eyes rejoiceth the heart; And good tidings make the bones fat.
asv.15:31: The ear that hearkeneth to the reproof of life Shall abide among the wise.
asv.15:32: He that refuseth correction despiseth his own soul; But he that hearkeneth to reproof getteth understanding.
asv.15:33: The fear of Jehovah is the instruction of wisdom; And before honor goeth humility.
asv.16:1: The plans of the heart belong to man; But the answer of the tongue is from Jehovah.
asv.16:2: All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes; But Jehovah weigheth the spirits.
asv.16:3: Commit thy works unto Jehovah, And thy purposes shall be established.
asv.16:4: Jehovah hath made everything for its own end; Yea, even the wicked for the day of evil.
asv.16:5: Every one that is proud in heart is an abomination to Jehovah: Though hand join in hand, he shall not be unpunished.
asv.16:6: By mercy and truth iniquity is atoned for; And by the fear of Jehovah men depart from evil.
asv.16:7: When a man’s ways please Jehovah, He maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.
asv.16:8: Better is a little, with righteousness, Than great revenues with injustice.
asv.16:9: A man’s heart deviseth his way; But Jehovah directeth his steps.
asv.16:10: A divine sentence is in the lips of the king; His mouth shall not transgress in judgment.
asv.16:11: A just balance and scales are Jehovah’s; All the weights of the bag are his work.
asv.16:12: It is an abomination to kings to commit wickedness; For the throne is established by righteousness.
asv.16:13: Righteous lips are the delight of kings; And they love him that speaketh right.
asv.16:14: The wrath of a king is as messengers of death; But a wise man will pacify it.
asv.16:15: In the light of the king’s countenance is life; And his favor is as a cloud of the latter rain.
asv.16:16: How much better is it to get wisdom than gold! Yea, to get understanding is rather to be chosen than silver.
asv.16:17: The highway of the upright is to depart from evil: He that keepeth his way preserveth his soul.
asv.16:18: Pride goeth before destruction, And a haughty spirit before a fall.
asv.16:19: Better it is to be of a lowly spirit with the poor, Than to divide the spoil with the proud.
asv.16:20: He that giveth heed unto the word shall find good; And whoso trusteth in Jehovah, happy is he.
asv.16:21: The wise in heart shall be called prudent; And the sweetness of the lips increaseth learning.
asv.16:22: Understanding is a well-spring of life unto him that hath it; But the correction of fools is their folly.
asv.16:23: The heart of the wise instructeth his mouth, And addeth learning to his lips.
asv.16:24: Pleasant words are as a honeycomb, Sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
asv.16:25: There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, But the end thereof are the ways of death.
asv.16:26: The appetite of the laboring man laboreth for him; For his mouth urgeth him thereto.
asv.16:27: A worthless man deviseth mischief; And in his lips there is as a scorching fire.
asv.16:28: A perverse man scattereth abroad strife; And a whisperer separateth chief friends.
asv.16:29: A man of violence enticeth his neighbor, And leadeth him in a way that is not good.
asv.16:30: He that shutteth his eyes, it is to devise perverse things: He that compresseth his lips bringeth evil to pass.
asv.16:31: The hoary head is a crown of glory; It shall be found in the way of righteousness.
asv.16:32: He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; And he that ruleth his spirit, than he that taketh a city.
asv.16:33: The lot is cast into the lap; But the whole disposing thereof is of Jehovah.
asv.17:1: Better is a dry morsel, and quietness therewith, Than a house full of feasting with strife.
asv.17:2: A servant that dealeth wisely shall have rule over a son that causeth shame, And shall have part in the inheritance among the brethren.
asv.17:3: The refining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold; But Jehovah trieth the hearts.
asv.17:4: An evil-doer giveth heed to wicked lips; And a liar giveth ear to a mischievous tongue.
asv.17:5: Whoso mocketh the poor reproacheth his Maker; And he that is glad at calamity shall not be unpunished.
asv.17:6: Children’s children are the crown of old men; And the glory of children are their fathers.
asv.17:7: Excellent speech becometh not a fool; Much less do lying lips a prince.
asv.17:8: A bribe is as a precious stone in the eyes of him that hath it; Whithersoever it turneth, it prospereth.
asv.17:9: He that covereth a transgression seeketh love; But he that harpeth on a matter separateth chief friends.
asv.17:10: A rebuke entereth deeper into one that hath understanding Than a hundred stripes into a fool.
asv.17:11: An evil man seeketh only rebellion; Therefore a cruel messenger shall be sent against him.
asv.17:12: Let a bear robbed of her whelps meet a man, Rather than a fool in his folly.
asv.17:13: Whoso rewardeth evil for good, Evil shall not depart from his house.
asv.17:14: The beginning of strife is as when one letteth out water: Therefore leave off contention, before there is quarrelling.
asv.17:15: He that justifieth the wicked, and he that condemneth the righteous, Both of them alike are an abomination to Jehovah.
asv.17:16: Wherefore is there a price in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom, Seeing he hath no understanding?
asv.17:17: A friend loveth at all times; And a brother is born for adversity.
asv.17:18: A man void of understanding striketh hands, And becometh surety in the presence of his neighbor.
asv.17:19: He loveth transgression that loveth strife: He that raiseth high his gate seeketh destruction.
asv.17:20: He that hath a wayward heart findeth no good; And he that hath a perverse tongue falleth into mischief.
asv.17:21: He that begetteth a fool doeth it to his sorrow; And the father of a fool hath no joy.
asv.17:22: A cheerful heart is a good medicine; But a broken spirit drieth up the bones.
asv.17:23: A wicked man receiveth a bribe out of the bosom, To pervert the ways of justice.
asv.17:24: Wisdom is before the face of him that hath understanding; But the eyes of a fool are in the ends of the earth.
asv.17:25: A foolish son is a grief to his father, And bitterness to her that bare him.
asv.17:26: Also to punish the righteous is not good, Nor to smite the noble for their uprightness.
asv.17:27: He that spareth his words hath knowledge; And he that is of a cool spirit is a man of understanding.
asv.17:28: Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise; When he shutteth his lips, he is esteemed as prudent.
asv.18:1: He that separateth himself seeketh his own desire, And rageth against all sound wisdom.
asv.18:2: A fool hath no delight in understanding, But only that his heart may reveal itself.
asv.18:3: When the wicked cometh, there cometh also contempt, And with ignominy cometh reproach.
asv.18:4: The words of a man’s mouth are as deep waters; The wellspring of wisdom is as a flowing brook.
asv.18:5: To respect the person of the wicked is not good, Nor to turn aside the righteous in judgment.
asv.18:6: A fool’s lips enter into contention, And his mouth calleth for stripes.
asv.18:7: A fool’s mouth is his destruction, And his lips are the snare of his soul.
asv.18:8: The words of a whisperer are as dainty morsels, And they go down into the innermost parts.
asv.18:9: He also that is slack in his work Is brother to him that is a destroyer.
asv.18:10: The name of Jehovah is a strong tower; The righteous runneth into it, and is safe.
asv.18:11: The rich man’s wealth is his strong city, And as a high wall in his own imagination.
asv.18:12: Before destruction the heart of man is haughty; And before honor goeth humility.
asv.18:13: He that giveth answer before he heareth, It is folly and shame unto him.
asv.18:14: The spirit of a man will sustain his infirmity; But a broken spirit who can bear?
asv.18:15: The heart of the prudent getteth knowledge; And the ear of the wise seeketh knowledge.
asv.18:16: A man’s gift maketh room for him, And bringeth him before great men.
asv.18:17: He that pleadeth his cause first seemeth just; But his neighbor cometh and searcheth him out.
asv.18:18: The lot causeth contentions to cease, And parteth between the mighty.
asv.18:19: A brother offended is harder to be won than a strong city; And such contentions are like the bars of a castle.
asv.18:20: A man’s belly shall be filled with the fruit of his mouth; With the increase of his lips shall he be satisfied.
asv.18:21: Death and life are in the power of the tongue; And they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.
asv.18:22: Whoso findeth a wife findeth a good thing, And obtaineth favor of Jehovah.
asv.18:23: The poor useth entreaties; But the rich answereth roughly.
asv.18:24: He that maketh many friends doeth it to his own destruction; But there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.
asv.19:1: Better is the poor that walketh in his integrity Than he that is perverse in his lips and is a fool.
asv.19:2: Also, that the soul be without knowledge is not good; And he that hasteth with his feet sinneth.
asv.19:3: The foolishness of man subverteth his way; And his heart fretteth against Jehovah.
asv.19:4: Wealth addeth many friends; But the poor is separated from his friend.
asv.19:5: A false witness shall not be unpunished; And he that uttereth lies shall not escape.
asv.19:6: Many will entreat the favor of the liberal man; And every man is a friend to him that giveth gifts.
asv.19:7: All the brethren of the poor do hate him: How much more do his friends go far from him! He pursueth them with words, but they are gone.
asv.19:8: He that getteth wisdom loveth his own soul: He that keepeth understanding shall find good.
asv.19:9: A false witness shall not be unpunished; And he that uttereth lies shall perish.
asv.19:10: Delicate living is not seemly for a fool; Much less for a servant to have rule over princes.
asv.19:11: The discretion of a man maketh him slow to anger; And it is his glory to pass over a transgression.
asv.19:12: The king’s wrath is as the roaring of a lion; But his favor is as dew upon the grass.
asv.19:13: A foolish son is the calamity of his father; And the contentions of a wife are a continual dropping.
asv.19:14: House and riches are an inheritance from fathers; But a prudent wife is from Jehovah.
asv.19:15: Slothfulness casteth into a deep sleep; And the idle soul shall suffer hunger.
asv.19:16: He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his soul; But he that is careless of his ways shall die.
asv.19:17: He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto Jehovah, And his good deed will he pay him again.
asv.19:18: Chasten thy son, seeing there is hope; And set not thy heart on his destruction.
asv.19:19: A man of great wrath shall bear the penalty; For if thou deliver him, thou must do it yet again.
asv.19:20: Hear counsel, and receive instruction, That thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.
asv.19:21: There are many devices in a man’s heart; But the counsel of Jehovah, that shall stand.
asv.19:22: That which maketh a man to be desired is his kindness; And a poor man is better than a liar.
asv.19:23: The fear of Jehovah tendeth to life; And he that hath it shall abide satisfied; He shall not be visited with evil.
asv.19:24: The sluggard burieth his hand in the dish, And will not so much as bring it to his mouth again.
asv.19:25: Smite a scoffer, and the simple will learn prudence; And reprove one that hath understanding, and he will understand knowledge.
asv.19:26: He that doeth violence to his father, and chaseth away his mother, Is a son that causeth shame and bringeth reproach.
asv.19:27: Cease, my son, to hear instruction Only to err from the words of knowledge.
asv.19:28: A worthless witness mocketh at justice; And the mouth of the wicked swalloweth iniquity.
asv.19:29: Judgments are prepared for scoffers, And stripes for the back of fools.
asv.20:1: Wine is a mocker, strong drink a brawler; And whosoever erreth thereby is not wise.
asv.20:2: The terror of a king is as the roaring of a lion: He that provoketh him to anger sinneth against his own life.
asv.20:3: It is an honor for a man to keep aloof from strife; But every fool will be quarrelling.
asv.20:4: The sluggard will not plow by reason of the winter; Therefore he shall beg in harvest, and have nothing.
asv.20:5: Counsel in the heart of man is like deep water; But a man of understanding will draw it out.
asv.20:6: Most men will proclaim every one his own kindness; But a faithful man who can find?
asv.20:7: A righteous man that walketh in his integrity, Blessed are his children after him.
asv.20:8: A king that sitteth on the throne of judgment Scattereth away all evil with his eyes.
asv.20:9: Who can say, I have made my heart clean, I am pure from my sin?
asv.20:10: Diverse weights, and diverse measures, Both of them alike are an abomination to Jehovah.
asv.20:11: Even a child maketh himself known by his doings, Whether his work be pure, and whether it be right.
asv.20:12: The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, Jehovah hath made even both of them.
asv.20:13: Love not sleep, lest thou come to poverty; Open thine eyes, and thou shalt be satisfied with bread.
asv.20:14: It is bad, it is bad, saith the buyer; But when he is gone his way, then he boasteth.
asv.20:15: There is gold, and abundance of rubies; But the lips of knowledge are a precious jewel.
asv.20:16: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger; And hold him in pledge that is surety for foreigners.
asv.20:17: Bread of falsehood is sweet to a man; But afterwards his mouth shall be filled with gravel.
asv.20:18: Every purpose is established by counsel; And by wise guidance make thou war.
asv.20:19: He that goeth about as a tale-bearer revealeth secrets; Therefore company not with him that openeth wide his lips.
asv.20:20: Whoso curseth his father or his mother, His lamp shall be put out in blackness of darkness.
asv.20:21: An inheritance may be gotten hastily at the beginning; But the end thereof shall not be blessed.
asv.20:22: Say not thou, I will recompense evil: Wait for Jehovah, and he will save thee.
asv.20:23: Diverse weights are an abomination to Jehovah; And a false balance is not good.
asv.20:24: A man’s goings are of Jehovah; How then can man understand his way?
asv.20:25: It is a snare to a man rashly to say, It is holy, And after vows to make inquiry.
asv.20:26: A wise king winnoweth the wicked, And bringeth the threshing -wheel over them.
asv.20:27: The spirit of man is the lamp of Jehovah, Searching all his innermost parts.
asv.20:28: Kindness and truth preserve the king; And his throne is upholden by kindness.
asv.20:29: The glory of young men is their strength; And the beauty of old men is the hoary head.
asv.20:30: Stripes that wound cleanse away evil; And strokes reach the innermost parts.
asv.21:1: The king’s heart is in the hand of Jehovah as the watercourses: He turneth it whithersoever he will.
asv.21:2: Every way of a man is right in his own eyes; But Jehovah weigheth the hearts.
asv.21:3: To do righteousness and justice Is more acceptable to Jehovah than sacrifice.
asv.21:4: A high look, and a proud heart, Even the lamp of the wicked, is sin.
asv.21:5: The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness; But every one that is hasty hasteth only to want.
asv.21:6: The getting of treasures by a lying tongue Is a vapor driven to and fro by them that seek death.
asv.21:7: The violence of the wicked shall sweep them away, Because they refuse to do justice.
asv.21:8: The way of him that is laden with guilt is exceeding crooked; But as for the pure, his work is right.
asv.21:9: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, Than with a contentious woman in a wide house.
asv.21:10: The soul of the wicked desireth evil: His neighbor findeth no favor in his eyes.
asv.21:11: When the scoffer is punished, the simple is made wise; And when the wise is instructed, he receiveth knowledge.
asv.21:12: The righteous man considereth the house of the wicked, How the wicked are overthrown to their ruin.
asv.21:13: Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, He also shall cry, but shall not be heard.
asv.21:14: A gift in secret pacifieth anger; And a present in the bosom, strong wrath.
asv.21:15: It is joy to the righteous to do justice; But it is a destruction to the workers of iniquity.
asv.21:16: The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding Shall rest in the assembly of the dead.
asv.21:17: He that loveth pleasure shall be a poor man: He that loveth wine and oil shall not be rich.
asv.21:18: The wicked is a ransom for the righteous; And the treacherous cometh in the stead of the upright.
asv.21:19: It is better to dwell in a desert land, Than with a contentious and fretful woman.
asv.21:20: There is precious treasure and oil in the dwelling of the wise; But a foolish man swalloweth it up.
asv.21:21: He that followeth after righteousness and kindness Findeth life, righteousness, and honor.
asv.21:22: A wise man scaleth the city of the mighty, And bringeth down the strength of the confidence thereof.
asv.21:23: Whoso keepeth his mouth and his tongue Keepeth his soul from troubles.
asv.21:24: The proud and haughty man, scoffer is his name; He worketh in the arrogance of pride.
asv.21:25: The desire of the sluggard killeth him; For his hands refuse to labor.
asv.21:26: There is that coveteth greedily all the day long; But the righteous giveth and withholdeth not.
asv.21:27: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination; How much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind!
asv.21:28: A false witness shall perish; But the man that heareth shall speak so as to endure.
asv.21:29: A wicked man hardeneth his face; But as for the upright, he establisheth his ways.
asv.21:30: There is no wisdom nor understanding Nor counsel against Jehovah.
asv.21:31: The horse is prepared against the day of battle; But victory is of Jehovah.
asv.22:1: A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, And loving favor rather than silver and gold.
asv.22:2: The rich and the poor meet together: Jehovah is the maker of them all.
asv.22:3: A prudent man seeth the evil, and hideth himself; But the simple pass on, and suffer for it.
asv.22:4: The reward of humility and the fear of Jehovah Is riches, and honor, and life.
asv.22:5: Thorns and snares are in the way of the perverse: He that keepeth his soul shall be far from them.
asv.22:6: Train up a child in the way he should go, And even when he is old he will not depart from it.
asv.22:7: The rich ruleth over the poor; And the borrower is servant to the lender.
asv.22:8: He that soweth iniquity shall reap calamity; And the rod of his wrath shall fail.
asv.22:9: He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; For he giveth of his bread to the poor.
asv.22:10: Cast out the scoffer, and contention will go out; Yea, strife and ignominy will cease.
asv.22:11: He that loveth pureness of heart, For the grace of his lips the king will be his friend.
asv.22:12: The eyes of Jehovah preserve him that hath knowledge; But he overthroweth the words of the treacherous man.
asv.22:13: The sluggard saith, There is a lion without; I shall be slain in the streets.
asv.22:14: The mouth of strange women is a deep pit; He that is abhorred of Jehovah shall fall therein.
asv.22:15: Foolishness is bound up in the heart of a child; But the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.
asv.22:16: He that oppresseth the poor to increase his gain, And he that giveth to the rich, shall come only to want.
asv.22:17: Incline thine ear, and hear the words of the wise, And apply thy heart unto my knowledge.
asv.22:18: For it is a pleasant thing if thou keep them within thee, If they be established together upon thy lips.
asv.22:19: That thy trust may be in Jehovah, I have made them known to thee this day, even to thee.
asv.22:20: Have not I written unto thee excellent things Of counsels and knowledge,
asv.22:21: To make thee know the certainty of the words of truth, That thou mayest carry back words of truth to them that send thee?
asv.22:22: Rob not the poor, because he is poor; Neither oppress the afflicted in the gate:
asv.22:23: For Jehovah will plead their cause, And despoil of life those that despoil them.
asv.22:24: Make no friendship with a man that is given to anger; And with a wrathful man thou shalt not go:
asv.22:25: Lest thou learn his ways, And get a snare to thy soul.
asv.22:26: Be thou not one of them that strike hands, Or of them that are sureties for debts.
asv.22:27: If thou hast not wherewith to pay, Why should he take away thy bed from under thee?
asv.22:28: Remove not the ancient landmark, Which thy fathers have set.
asv.22:29: Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; He shall not stand before mean men.
asv.23:1: When thou sittest to eat with a ruler, Consider diligently him that is before thee;
asv.23:2: And put a knife to thy throat, If thou be a man given to appetite.
asv.23:3: Be not desirous of his dainties; Seeing they are deceitful food.
asv.23:4: Weary not thyself to be rich; Cease from thine own wisdom.
asv.23:5: Wilt thou set thine eyes upon that which is not? For riches certainly make themselves wings, Like an eagle that flieth toward heaven.
asv.23:6: Eat thou not the bread of him that hath an evil eye, Neither desire thou his dainties:
asv.23:7: For as he thinketh within himself, so is he: Eat and drink, saith he to thee; But his heart is not with thee.
asv.23:8: The morsel which thou hast eaten shalt thou vomit up, And lose thy sweet words.
asv.23:9: Speak not in the hearing of a fool; For he will despise the wisdom of thy words.
asv.23:10: Remove not the ancient landmark; And enter not into the fields of the fatherless:
asv.23:11: For their Redeemer is strong; He will plead their cause against thee.
asv.23:12: Apply thy heart unto instruction, And thine ears to the words of knowledge.
asv.23:13: Withhold not correction from the child; For if thou beat him with the rod, he will not die.
asv.23:14: Thou shalt beat him with the rod, And shalt deliver his soul from Sheol.
asv.23:15: My son, if thy heart be wise, My heart will be glad, even mine:
asv.23:16: Yea, my heart will rejoice, When thy lips speak right things.
asv.23:17: Let not thy heart envy sinners; But be thou in the fear of Jehovah all the day long:
