asv.23:18: For surely there is a reward; And thy hope shall not be cut off.
asv.23:19: Hear thou, my son, and be wise, And guide thy heart in the way.
asv.23:20: Be not among winebibbers, Among gluttonous eaters of flesh:
asv.23:21: For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty; And drowsiness will clothe a man with rags.
asv.23:22: Hearken unto thy father that begat thee, And despise not thy mother when she is old.
asv.23:23: Buy the truth, and sell it not; Yea, wisdom, and instruction, and understanding.
asv.23:24: The father of the righteous will greatly rejoice; And he that begetteth a wise child will have joy of him.
asv.23:25: Let thy father and thy mother be glad, And let her that bare thee rejoice.
asv.23:26: My son, give me thy heart; And let thine eyes delight in my ways.
asv.23:27: For a harlot is a deep ditch; And a foreign woman is a narrow pit.
asv.23:28: Yea, she lieth in wait as a robber, And increaseth the treacherous among men.
asv.23:29: Who hath woe? who hath sorrow? who hath contentions? Who hath complaining? who hath wounds without cause? Who hath redness of eyes?
asv.23:30: They that tarry long at the wine; They that go to seek out mixed wine.
asv.23:31: Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, When it sparkleth in the cup, When it goeth down smoothly:
asv.23:32: At the last it biteth like a serpent, And stingeth like an adder.
asv.23:33: Thine eyes shall behold strange things, And thy heart shall utter perverse things.
asv.23:34: Yea, thou shalt be as he that lieth down in the midst of the sea, Or as he that lieth upon the top of a mast.
asv.23:35: They have stricken me, shalt thou say, and I was not hurt; They have beaten me, and I felt it not: When shall I awake? I will seek it yet again.
asv.24:1: Be not thou envious against evil men; Neither desire to be with them:
asv.24:2: For their heart studieth oppression, And their lips talk of mischief.
asv.24:3: Through wisdom is a house builded; And by understanding it is established;
asv.24:4: And by knowledge are the chambers filled With all precious and pleasant riches.
asv.24:5: A wise man is strong; Yea, a man of knowledge increaseth might.
asv.24:6: For by wise guidance thou shalt make thy war; And in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.
asv.24:7: Wisdom is too high for a fool: He openeth not his mouth in the gate.
asv.24:8: He that deviseth to do evil, Men shall call him a mischief-maker.
asv.24:9: The thought of foolishness is sin; And the scoffer is an abomination to men.
asv.24:10: If thou faint in the day of adversity, Thy strength is small.
asv.24:11: Deliver them that are carried away unto death, And those that are ready to be slain see that thou hold back.
asv.24:12: If thou sayest, Behold, we knew not this; Doth not he that weigheth the hearts consider it? And he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? And shall not he render to every man according to his work?
asv.24:13: My son, eat thou honey, for it is good; And the droppings of the honeycomb, which are sweet to thy taste:
asv.24:14: So shalt thou know wisdom to be unto thy soul; If thou hast found it, then shall there be a reward, And thy hope shall not be cut off.
asv.24:15: Lay not wait, O wicked man, against the habitation of the righteous; Destroy not his resting-place:
asv.24:16: For a righteous man falleth seven times, and riseth up again; But the wicked are overthrown by calamity.
asv.24:17: Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, And let not thy heart be glad when he is overthrown;
asv.24:18: Lest Jehovah see it, and it displease him, And he turn away his wrath from him.
asv.24:19: Fret not thyself because of evil-doers; Neither be thou envious at the wicked:
asv.24:20: For there shall be no reward to the evil man; The lamp of the wicked shall be put out.
asv.24:21: My son, fear thou Jehovah and the king; And company not with them that are given to change:
asv.24:22: For their calamity shall rise suddenly; And the destruction from them both, who knoweth it?
asv.24:23: These also are sayings of the wise. To have respect of persons in judgment is not good.
asv.24:24: He that saith unto the wicked, Thou art righteous, Peoples shall curse him, nations shall abhor him;
asv.24:25: But to them that rebuke him shall be delight, And a good blessing shall come upon them.
asv.24:26: He kisseth the lips Who giveth a right answer.
asv.24:27: Prepare thy work without, And make it ready for thee in the field; And afterwards build thy house.
asv.24:28: Be not a witness against thy neighbor without cause; And deceive not with thy lips.
asv.24:29: Say not, I will do so to him as he hath done to me; I will render to the man according to his work.
asv.24:30: I went by the field of the sluggard, And by the vineyard of the man void of understanding;
asv.24:31: And, lo, it was all grown over with thorns, The face thereof was covered with nettles, And the stone wall thereof was broken down.
asv.24:32: Then I beheld, and considered well; I saw, and received instruction:
asv.24:33: Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, A little folding of the hands to sleep;
asv.24:34: So shall thy poverty come as a robber, And thy want as an armed man.
asv.25:1: These also are proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
asv.25:2: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing; But the glory of kings is to search out a matter.
asv.25:3: As the heavens for height, and the earth for depth, So the heart of kings is unsearchable.
asv.25:4: Take away the dross from the silver, And there cometh forth a vessel for the refiner:
asv.25:5: Take away the wicked from before the king, And his throne shall be established in righteousness.
asv.25:6: Put not thyself forward in the presence of the king, And stand not in the place of great men:
asv.25:7: For better is it that it be said unto thee, Come up hither, Than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince, Whom thine eyes have seen.
asv.25:8: Go not forth hastily to strive, Lest thou know not what to do in the end thereof, When thy neighbor hath put thee to shame.
asv.25:9: Debate thy cause with thy neighbor himself, And disclose not the secret of another;
asv.25:10: Lest he that heareth it revile thee, And thine infamy turn not away.
asv.25:11: A word fitly spoken Is like apples of gold in network of silver.
asv.25:12: As an ear-ring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, So is a wise reprover upon an obedient ear.
asv.25:13: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, So is a faithful messenger to them that send him; For he refresheth the soul of his masters.
asv.25:14: As clouds and wind without rain, So is he that boasteth himself of his gifts falsely.
asv.25:15: By long forbearing is a ruler persuaded, And a soft tongue breaketh the bone.
asv.25:16: Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, Lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.
asv.25:17: Let thy foot be seldom in thy neighbor’s house, Lest he be weary of thee, and hate thee.
asv.25:18: A man that beareth false witness against his neighbor Is a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.
asv.25:19: Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble Is like a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.
asv.25:20: As one that taketh off a garment in cold weather, and as vinegar upon soda, So is he that singeth songs to a heavy heart.
asv.25:21: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; And if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:
asv.25:22: For thou wilt heap coals of fire upon his head, And Jehovah will reward thee.
asv.25:23: The north wind bringeth forth rain; So doth a backbiting tongue an angry countenance.
asv.25:24: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, Than with a contentious woman in a wide house.
asv.25:25: As cold waters to a thirsty soul, So is good news from a far country.
asv.25:26: As a troubled fountain, and a corrupted spring, So is a righteous man that giveth way before the wicked.
asv.25:27: It is not good to eat much honey; So for men to search out their own glory is grievous.
asv.25:28: He whose spirit is without restraint Is like a city that is broken down and without walls.
asv.26:1: As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, So honor is not seemly for a fool.
asv.26:2: As the sparrow in her wandering, as the swallow in her flying, So the curse that is causeless alighteth not.
asv.26:3: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, And a rod for the back of fools.
asv.26:4: Answer not a fool according to his folly, Lest thou also be like unto him.
asv.26:5: Answer a fool according to his folly, Lest he be wise in his own conceit.
asv.26:6: He that sendeth a message by the hand of a fool Cutteth off his own feet, and drinketh in damage.
asv.26:7: The legs of the lame hang loose; So is a parable in the mouth of fools.
asv.26:8: As one that bindeth a stone in a sling, So is he that giveth honor to a fool.
asv.26:9: As a thorn that goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, So is a parable in the mouth of fools.
asv.26:10: As an archer that woundeth all, So is he that hireth a fool and he that hireth them that pass by.
asv.26:11: As a dog that returneth to his vomit, So is a fool that repeateth his folly.
asv.26:12: Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit? There is more hope of a fool than of him.
asv.26:13: The sluggard saith, There is a lion in the way; A lion is in the streets.
asv.26:14: As the door turneth upon its hinges, So doth the sluggard upon his bed.
asv.26:15: The sluggard burieth his hand in the dish; It wearieth him to bring it again to his mouth.
asv.26:16: The sluggard is wiser in his own conceit Than seven men that can render a reason.
asv.26:17: He that passeth by, and vexeth himself with strife belonging not to him, Is like one that taketh a dog by the ears.
asv.26:18: As a madman who casteth firebrands, Arrows, and death,
asv.26:19: So is the man that deceiveth his neighbor, And saith, Am not I in sport?
asv.26:20: For lack of wood the fire goeth out; And where there is no whisperer, contention ceaseth.
asv.26:21: As coals are to hot embers, and wood to fire, So is a contentious man to inflame strife.
asv.26:22: The words of a whisperer are as dainty morsels, And they go down into the innermost parts.
asv.26:23: Fervent lips and a wicked heart Are like an earthen vessel overlaid with silver dross.
asv.26:24: He that hateth dissembleth with his lips; But he layeth up deceit within him:
asv.26:25: When he speaketh fair, believe him not; For there are seven abominations in his heart:
asv.26:26: Though his hatred cover itself with guile, His wickedness shall be openly showed before the assembly.
asv.26:27: Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein; And he that rolleth a stone, it shall return upon him.
asv.26:28: A lying tongue hateth those whom it hath wounded; And a flattering mouth worketh ruin.
asv.27:1: Boast not thyself of to-morrow; For thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.
asv.27:2: Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; A stranger, and not thine own lips.
asv.27:3: A stone is heavy, and the sand weighty; But a fool’s vexation is heavier than they both.
asv.27:4: Wrath is cruel, and anger is overwhelming; But who is able to stand before jealousy?
asv.27:5: Better is open rebuke Than love that is hidden.
asv.27:6: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; But the kisses of an enemy are profuse.
asv.27:7: The full soul loatheth a honeycomb; But to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.
asv.27:8: As a bird that wandereth from her nest, So is a man that wandereth from his place.
asv.27:9: Oil and perfume rejoice the heart; So doth the sweetness of a man’s friend that cometh of hearty counsel.
asv.27:10: Thine own friend, and thy father’s friend, forsake not; And go not to thy brother’s house in the day of thy calamity: Better is a neighbor that is near than a brother far off.
asv.27:11: My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, That I may answer him that reproacheth me.
asv.27:12: A prudent man seeth the evil, and hideth himself; But the simple pass on, and suffer for it.
asv.27:13: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger; And hold him in pledge that is surety for a foreign woman.
asv.27:14: He that blesseth his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, It shall be counted a curse to him.
asv.27:15: A continual dropping in a very rainy day And a contentious woman are alike:
asv.27:16: He that would restrain her restraineth the wind; And his right hand encountereth oil.
asv.27:17: Iron sharpeneth iron; So a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
asv.27:18: Whoso keepeth the fig-tree shall eat the fruit thereof; And he that regardeth his master shall be honored.
asv.27:19: As in water face answereth to face, So the heart of man to man.
asv.27:20: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; And the eyes of man are never satisfied.
asv.27:21: The refining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold; And a man is tried by his praise.
asv.27:22: Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with bruised grain, Yet will not his foolishness depart from him.
asv.27:23: Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, And look well to thy herds:
asv.27:24: For riches are not for ever; And doth the crown endure unto all generations?
asv.27:25: The hay is carried, and the tender grass showeth itself, And the herbs of the mountains are gathered in.
asv.27:26: The lambs are for thy clothing, And the goats are the price of the field;
asv.27:27: And there will be goats’ milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, And maintenance for thy maidens.
asv.28:1: The wicked flee when no man pursueth; But the righteous are bold as a lion.
asv.28:2: For the transgression of a land many are the princes thereof; But by men of understanding and knowledge the state thereof shall be prolonged.
asv.28:3: A needy man that oppresseth the poor Is like a sweeping rain which leaveth no food.
asv.28:4: They that forsake the law praise the wicked; But such as keep the law contend with them.
asv.28:5: Evil men understand not justice; But they that seek Jehovah understand all things.
asv.28:6: Better is the poor that walketh in his integrity, Than he that is perverse in his ways, though he be rich.
asv.28:7: Whoso keepeth the law is a wise son; But he that is a companion of gluttons shameth his father.
asv.28:8: He that augmenteth his substance by interest and increase, Gathereth it for him that hath pity on the poor.
asv.28:9: He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, Even his prayer is an abomination.
asv.28:10: Whoso causeth the upright to go astray in an evil way, He shall fall himself into his own pit; But the perfect shall inherit good.
asv.28:11: The rich man is wise in his own conceit; But the poor that hath understanding searcheth him out.
asv.28:12: When the righteous triumph, there is great glory; But when the wicked rise, men hide themselves.
asv.28:13: He that covereth his transgressions shall not prosper; But whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall obtain mercy.
asv.28:14: Happy is the man that feareth alway; But he that hardeneth his heart shall fall into mischief.
asv.28:15: As a roaring lion, and a ranging bear, So is a wicked ruler over a poor people.
asv.28:16: The prince that lacketh understanding is also a great oppressor; But he that hateth covetousness shall prolong his days.
asv.28:17: A man that is laden with the blood of any person Shall flee unto the pit; let no man stay him.
asv.28:18: Whoso walketh uprightly shall be delivered; But he that is perverse in his ways shall fall at once.
asv.28:19: He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread; But he that followeth after vain persons shall have poverty enough.
asv.28:20: A faithful man shall abound with blessings; But he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be unpunished.
asv.28:21: To have respect of persons is not good; Neither that a man should transgress for a piece of bread.
asv.28:22: He that hath an evil eye hasteth after riches, And knoweth not that want shall come upon him.
asv.28:23: He that rebuketh a man shall afterward find more favor Than he that flattereth with the tongue.
asv.28:24: Whoso robbeth his father or his mother, and saith, It is no transgression, The same is the companion of a destroyer.
asv.28:25: He that is of a greedy spirit stirreth up strife; But he that putteth his trust in Jehovah shall be made fat.
asv.28:26: He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool; But whoso walketh wisely, he shall be delivered.
asv.28:27: He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack; But he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse.
asv.28:28: When the wicked rise, men hide themselves; But when they perish, the righteous increase.
asv.29:1: He that being often reproved hardeneth his neck Shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.
asv.29:2: When the righteous are increased, the people rejoice; But when a wicked man beareth rule, the people sigh.
asv.29:3: Whoso loveth wisdom rejoiceth his father; But he that keepeth company with harlots wasteth his substance.
asv.29:4: The king by justice establisheth the land; But he that exacteth gifts overthroweth it.
asv.29:5: A man that flattereth his neighbor Spreadeth a net for his steps.
asv.29:6: In the transgression of an evil man there is a snare; But the righteous doth sing and rejoice.
asv.29:7: The righteous taketh knowledge of the cause of the poor; The wicked hath not understanding to know it.
asv.29:8: Scoffers set a city in a flame; But wise men turn away wrath.
asv.29:9: If a wise man hath a controversy with a foolish man, Whether he be angry or laugh, there will be no rest.
asv.29:10: The bloodthirsty hate him that is perfect; And as for the upright, they seek his life.
asv.29:11: A fool uttereth all his anger; But a wise man keepeth it back and stilleth it.
asv.29:12: If a ruler hearkeneth to falsehood, All his servants are wicked.
asv.29:13: The poor man and the oppressor meet together; Jehovah lighteneth the eyes of them both.
asv.29:14: The king that faithfully judgeth the poor, His throne shall be established for ever.
asv.29:15: The rod and reproof give wisdom; But a child left to himself causeth shame to his mother.
asv.29:16: When the wicked are increased, transgression increaseth; But the righteous shall look upon their fall.
asv.29:17: Correct thy son, and he will give thee rest; Yea, he will give delight unto thy soul.
asv.29:18: Where there is no vision, the people cast off restraint; But he that keepeth the law, happy is he.
asv.29:19: A servant will not be corrected by words; For though he understand, he will not give heed.
asv.29:20: Seest thou a man that is hasty in his words? There is more hope of a fool than of him.
asv.29:21: He that delicately bringeth up his servant from a child Shall have him become a son at the last.
asv.29:22: An angry man stirreth up strife, And a wrathful man aboundeth in transgression.
asv.29:23: A man’s pride shall bring him low; But he that is of a lowly spirit shall obtain honor.
asv.29:24: Whoso is partner with a thief hateth his own soul; He heareth the adjuration and uttereth nothing.
asv.29:25: The fear of man bringeth a snare; But whoso putteth his trust in Jehovah shall be safe.
asv.29:26: Many seek the ruler’s favor; But a man’s judgment cometh from Jehovah.
asv.29:27: An unjust man is an abomination to the righteous; And he that is upright in the way is an abomination to the wicked.
asv.30:1: The words of Agur the son of Jakeh; the oracle. The man saith unto Ithiel, unto Ithiel and Ucal:
asv.30:2: Surely I am more brutish than any man, And have not the understanding of a man;
asv.30:3: And I have not learned wisdom, Neither have I the knowledge of the Holy One.
asv.30:4: Who hath ascended up into heaven, and descended? Who hath gathered the wind in his fists? Who hath bound the waters in his garment? Who hath established all the ends of the earth? What is his name, and what is his son’s name, if thou knowest?
asv.30:5: Every word of God is tried: He is a shield unto them that take refuge in him.
asv.30:6: Add thou not unto his words, Lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar.
asv.30:7: Two things have I asked of thee; Deny me them not before I die:
asv.30:8: Remove far from me falsehood and lies; Give me neither poverty nor riches; Feed me with the food that is needful for me:
asv.30:9: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is Jehovah? Or lest I be poor, and steal, And use profanely the name of my God.
asv.30:10: Slander not a servant unto his master, Lest he curse thee, and thou be held guilty.
asv.30:11: There is a generation that curse their father, And bless not their mother.
asv.30:12: There is a generation that are pure in their own eyes, And yet are not washed from their filthiness.
asv.30:13: There is a generation, oh how lofty are their eyes! And their eyelids are lifted up.
asv.30:14: There is a generation whose teeth are as swords, and their jaw teeth as knives, To devour the poor from off the earth, and the needy from among men.
asv.30:15: The horseleach hath two daughters, crying, Give, give. There are three things that are never satisfied, Yea, four that say not, Enough:
asv.30:16: Sheol; and the barren womb; The earth that is not satisfied with water; And the fire that saith not, Enough.
asv.30:17: The eye that mocketh at his father, And despiseth to obey his mother, The ravens of the valley shall pick it out, And the young eagles shall eat it.
asv.30:18: There are three things which are too wonderful for me, Yea, four which I know not:
asv.30:19: The way of an eagle in the air; The way of a serpent upon a rock; The way of a ship in the midst of the sea; And the way of a man with a maiden.
asv.30:20: So is the way of an adulterous woman; She eateth, and wipeth her mouth, And saith, I have done no wickedness.
asv.30:21: For three things the earth doth tremble, And for four, which it cannot bear:
asv.30:22: For a servant when he is king; And a fool when he is filled with food;
asv.30:23: For an odious woman when she is married; And a handmaid that is heir to her mistress.
asv.30:24: There are four things which are little upon the earth, But they are exceeding wise:
asv.30:25: The ants are a people not strong, Yet they provide their food in the summer;
asv.30:26: The conies are but a feeble folk, Yet make they their houses in the rocks;
asv.30:27: The locusts have no king, Yet go they forth all of them by bands;
asv.30:28: The lizard taketh hold with her hands, Yet is she in kings’ palaces.
asv.30:29: There are three things which are stately in their march, Yea, four which are stately in going:
asv.30:30: The lion, which is mightiest among beasts, And turneth not away for any;
asv.30:31: The greyhound; the he-goat also; And the king against whom there is no rising up.
asv.30:32: If thou hast done foolishly in lifting up thyself, Or if thou hast thought evil, Lay thy hand upon thy mouth.
asv.30:33: For the churning of milk bringeth forth butter, And the wringing of the nose bringeth forth blood; So the forcing of wrath bringeth forth strife.
asv.31:1: The words of king Lemuel; the oracle which his mother taught him.
asv.31:2: What, my son? and what, O son of my womb? And what, O son of my vows?
asv.31:3: Give not thy strength unto women, Nor thy ways to that which destroyeth kings.
asv.31:4: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine; Nor for princes to say, Where is strong drink?
asv.31:5: Lest they drink, and forget the law, And pervert the justice due to any that is afflicted.
asv.31:6: Give strong drink unto him that is ready to perish, And wine unto the bitter in soul:
asv.31:7: Let him drink, and forget his poverty, And remember his misery no more.
asv.31:8: Open thy mouth for the dumb, In the cause of all such as are left desolate.
asv.31:9: Open thy mouth, judge righteously, And minister justice to the poor and needy.
asv.31:10: A worthy woman who can find? For her price is far above rubies.
asv.31:11: The heart of her husband trusteth in her, And he shall have no lack of gain.
asv.31:12: She doeth him good and not evil All the days of her life.
asv.31:13: She seeketh wool and flax, And worketh willingly with her hands.
asv.31:14: She is like the merchant-ships; She bringeth her bread from afar.
asv.31:15: She riseth also while it is yet night, And giveth food to her household, And their task to her maidens.
asv.31:16: She considereth a field, and buyeth it; With the fruit of her hands she planteth a vineyard.
asv.31:17: She girdeth her loins with strength, And maketh strong her arms.
asv.31:18: She perceiveth that her merchandise is profitable; Her lamp goeth not out by night.
asv.31:19: She layeth her hands to the distaff, And her hands hold the spindle.
asv.31:20: She stretcheth out her hand to the poor; Yea, she reacheth forth her hands to the needy.
asv.31:21: She is not afraid of the snow for her household; For all her household are clothed with scarlet.
asv.31:22: She maketh for herself carpets of tapestry; Her clothing is fine linen and purple.
asv.31:23: Her husband is known in the gates, When he sitteth among the elders of the land.
asv.31:24: She maketh linen garments and selleth them, And delivereth girdles unto the merchant.
asv.31:25: Strength and dignity are her clothing; And she laugheth at the time to come.
asv.31:26: She openeth her mouth with wisdom; And the law of kindness is on her tongue.
asv.31:27: She looketh well to the ways of her household, And eateth not the bread of idleness.
asv.31:28: Her children rise up, and call her blessed; Her husband also, and he praiseth her, saying:
asv.31:29: Many daughters have done worthily, But thou excellest them all.
asv.31:30: Grace is deceitful, and beauty is vain; But a woman that feareth Jehovah, she shall be praised.
asv.31:31: Give her of the fruit of her hands; And let her works praise her in the gates.

ylt.1:1: Proverbs of Solomon, son of David, king of Israel:
ylt.1:2: For knowing wisdom and instruction, For understanding sayings of intelligence,
ylt.1:3: For receiving the instruction of wisdom, Righteousness, judgment, and uprightness,
ylt.1:4: For giving to simple ones--prudence, To a youth--knowledge and discretion.
ylt.1:5: (The wise doth hear and increaseth learning, And the intelligent doth obtain counsels.)
ylt.1:6: For understanding a proverb and its sweetness, Words of the wise and their acute sayings.
ylt.1:7: Fear of Jehovah is a beginning of knowledge, Wisdom and instruction fools have despised!
ylt.1:8: Hear, my son, the instruction of thy father, And leave not the law of thy mother,
ylt.1:9: For a graceful wreath are they to thy head, And chains to thy neck.
ylt.1:10: My son, if sinners entice thee be not willing.
ylt.1:11: If they say, `Come with us, we lay wait for blood, We watch secretly for the innocent without cause,
ylt.1:12: We swallow them as Sheol--alive, And whole--as those going down to the pit,
ylt.1:13: Every precious substance we find, We fill our houses with spoil,
ylt.1:14: Thy lot thou dost cast among us, One purse is--to all of us.'
ylt.1:15: My son! go not in the way with them, Withhold thy foot from their path,
ylt.1:16: For their feet to evil do run, And they haste to shed blood.
ylt.1:17: Surely in vain is the net spread out before the eyes of any bird.
ylt.1:18: And they for their own blood lay wait, They watch secretly for their own lives.
ylt.1:19: So are the paths of every gainer of dishonest gain, The life of its owners it taketh.
ylt.1:20: Wisdom in an out-place crieth aloud, In broad places she giveth forth her voice,
ylt.1:21: At the head of the multitudes she calleth, In the openings of the gates, In the city her sayings she saith:
ylt.1:22: `Till when, ye simple, do ye love simplicity? And have scorners their scorning desired? And do fools hate knowledge?
ylt.1:23: Turn back at my reproof, lo, I pour forth to you my spirit, I make known my words with you.
ylt.1:24: Because I have called, and ye refuse, I stretched out my hand, and none is attending,
ylt.1:25: And ye slight all my counsel, And my reproof ye have not desired.
ylt.1:26: I also in your calamity do laugh, I deride when your fear cometh,
ylt.1:27: When your fear cometh as destruction, And your calamity as a hurricane doth come, When on you come adversity and distress.
ylt.1:28: Then they call me, and I do not answer, They seek me earnestly, and find me not.
ylt.1:29: Because that they have hated knowledge, And the fear of Jehovah have not chosen.
ylt.1:30: They have not consented to my counsel, They have despised all my reproof,
ylt.1:31: And they eat of the fruit of their way, And from their own counsels they are filled.
ylt.1:32: For the turning of the simple slayeth them, And the security of the foolish destroyeth them.
ylt.1:33: And whoso is hearkening to me dwelleth confidently, And is quiet from fear of evil!'
ylt.2:1: My son, if thou dost accept my sayings, And my commands dost lay up with thee,
ylt.2:2: To cause thine ear to attend to wisdom, Thou inclinest thy heart to understanding,
ylt.2:3: For, if for intelligence thou callest, For understanding givest forth thy voice,
ylt.2:4: If thou dost seek her as silver, And as hid treasures searchest for her,
ylt.2:5: Then understandest thou fear of Jehovah, And knowledge of God thou findest.
ylt.2:6: For Jehovah giveth wisdom, From His mouth knowledge and understanding.
ylt.2:7: Even to lay up for the upright substance, A shield for those walking uprightly.
ylt.2:8: To keep the paths of judgment, And the way of His saints He preserveth.
ylt.2:9: Then understandest thou righteousness, And judgment, and uprightness--every good path.
ylt.2:10: For wisdom cometh into thy heart, And knowledge to thy soul is pleasant,
ylt.2:11: Thoughtfulness doth watch over thee, Understanding doth keep thee,
ylt.2:12: To deliver thee from an evil way, From any speaking froward things,
ylt.2:13: Who are forsaking paths of uprightness, To walk in ways of darkness,
ylt.2:14: Who are rejoicing to do evil, They delight in frowardness of the wicked,
ylt.2:15: Whose paths are crooked, Yea, they are perverted in their ways.
ylt.2:16: To deliver thee from the strange woman, From the stranger who hath made smooth her sayings,
ylt.2:17: Who is forsaking the guide of her youth, And the covenant of her God hath forgotten.
ylt.2:18: For her house hath inclined unto death, And unto Rephaim her paths.
ylt.2:19: None going in unto her turn back, Nor do they reach the paths of life.
ylt.2:20: That thou dost go in the way of the good, And the paths of the righteous dost keep.
ylt.2:21: For the upright do inhabit the earth, And the perfect are left in it,
ylt.2:22: And the wicked from the earth are cut off, And treacherous dealers plucked out of it!
ylt.3:1: My son! my law forget not, And my commands let thy heart keep,
ylt.3:2: For length of days and years, Life and peace they do add to thee.
ylt.3:3: Let not kindness and truth forsake thee, Bind them on thy neck, Write them on the tablet of thy heart,
ylt.3:4: And find grace and good understanding In the eyes of God and man.
ylt.3:5: Trust unto Jehovah with all thy heart, And unto thine own understanding lean not.
ylt.3:6: In all thy ways know thou Him, And He doth make straight thy paths.
ylt.3:7: Be not wise in thine own eyes, Fear Jehovah, and turn aside from evil.
ylt.3:8: Healing it is to thy navel, And moistening to thy bones.
ylt.3:9: Honour Jehovah from thy substance, And from the beginning of all thine increase;
ylt.3:10: And filled are thy barns with plenty, And with new wine thy presses break forth.
ylt.3:11: Chastisement of Jehovah, my son, despise not, And be not vexed with His reproof,
ylt.3:12: For whom Jehovah loveth He reproveth, Even as a father the son He is pleased with.
ylt.3:13: O the happiness of a man who hath found wisdom, And of a man who bringeth forth understanding.
ylt.3:14: For better is her merchandise Than the merchandise of silver, And than gold--her increase.
ylt.3:15: Precious she is above rubies, And all thy pleasures are not comparable to her.
ylt.3:16: Length of days is in her right hand, In her left are wealth and honour.
ylt.3:17: Her ways are ways of pleasantness, And all her paths are peace.
ylt.3:18: A tree of life she is to those laying hold on her, And whoso is retaining her is happy.
ylt.3:19: Jehovah by wisdom did found the earth, He prepared the heavens by understanding.
ylt.3:20: By His knowledge depths have been rent, And clouds do drop dew.
ylt.3:21: My son! let them not turn from thine eyes, Keep thou wisdom and thoughtfulness,
ylt.3:22: And they are life to thy soul, and grace to thy neck.
ylt.3:23: Then thou goest thy way confidently, And thy foot doth not stumble.
ylt.3:24: If thou liest down, thou art not afraid, Yea, thou hast lain down, And sweet hath been thy sleep.
ylt.3:25: Be not afraid of sudden fear, And of the desolation of the wicked when it cometh.
ylt.3:26: For Jehovah is at thy side, And He hath kept thy foot from capture.
ylt.3:27: Withhold not good from its owners, When thy hand is toward God to do it.
ylt.3:28: Say not thou to thy friend, `Go, and return, and to-morrow I give,' And substance with thee.
ylt.3:29: Devise not against thy neighbour evil, And he sitting confidently with thee.
ylt.3:30: Strive not with a man without cause, If he have not done thee evil.
ylt.3:31: Be not envious of a man of violence, Nor fix thou on any of his ways.
ylt.3:32: For an abomination to Jehovah is the perverted, And with the upright is His secret counsel.
ylt.3:33: The curse of Jehovah is in the house of the wicked. And the habitation of the righteous He blesseth.
ylt.3:34: If the scorners He doth scorn, Yet to the humble He doth give grace.
ylt.3:35: Honour do the wise inherit, And fools are bearing away shame!
ylt.4:1: Hear, ye sons, the instruction of a father, And give attention to know understanding.
ylt.4:2: For good learning I have given to you, My law forsake not.
ylt.4:3: For, a son I have been to my father--tender, And an only one before my mother.
ylt.4:4: And he directeth me, and he saith to me: `Let thy heart retain my words, Keep my commands, and live.
ylt.4:5: Get wisdom, get understanding, Do not forget, nor turn away From the sayings of my mouth.
ylt.4:6: Forsake her not, and she doth preserve thee, Love her, and she doth keep thee.
ylt.4:7: The first thing is wisdom--get wisdom, And with all thy getting get understanding.
ylt.4:8: Exalt her, and she doth lift thee up, She honoureth thee, when thou dost embrace her.
ylt.4:9: She giveth to thy head a wreath of grace, A crown of beauty she doth give thee freely.
ylt.4:10: Hear, my son, and receive my sayings, And years of life are multiplied to thee.
ylt.4:11: In a way of wisdom I have directed thee, I have caused thee to tread in paths of uprightness.
ylt.4:12: In thy walking thy step is not straitened, And if thou runnest, thou stumblest not.
ylt.4:13: Lay hold on instruction, do not desist, Keep her, for she is thy life.
ylt.4:14: Into the path of the wicked enter not, And be not happy in a way of evil doers.
ylt.4:15: Avoid it, pass not over into it, Turn aside from it, and pass on.
ylt.4:16: For they sleep not if they do not evil, And their sleep hath been taken violently away, If they cause not some to stumble.
ylt.4:17: For they have eaten bread of wickedness, And wine of violence they drink.
ylt.4:18: And the path of the righteous is as a shining light, Going and brightening till the day is established,
ylt.4:19: The way of the wicked is as darkness, They have not known at what they stumble.
ylt.4:20: My son, to my words give attention, To my sayings incline thine ear,
ylt.4:21: Let them not turn aside from thine eyes, Preserve them in the midst of thy heart.
ylt.4:22: For life they are to those finding them, And to all their flesh healing.
ylt.4:23: Above every charge keep thy heart, For out of it are the outgoings of life.
ylt.4:24: Turn aside from thee a froward mouth, And perverse lips put far from thee,
ylt.4:25: Thine eyes do look straightforward, And thine eyelids look straight before thee.
ylt.4:26: Ponder thou the path of thy feet, And all thy ways are established.
ylt.4:27: Incline not to the right or to the left, Turn aside thy foot from evil!
ylt.5:1: My son! to my wisdom give attention, To mine understanding incline thine ear,
ylt.5:2: To observe thoughtfulness, And knowledge do thy lips keep.
ylt.5:3: For the lips of a strange woman drop honey, And smoother than oil is her mouth,
ylt.5:4: And her latter end is bitter as wormwood, Sharp as a sword with mouths.
ylt.5:5: Her feet are going down to death, Sheol do her steps take hold of.
ylt.5:6: The path of life--lest thou ponder, Moved have her paths--thou knowest not.
ylt.5:7: And now, ye sons, hearken to me, And turn not from sayings of my mouth.
ylt.5:8: Keep far from off her thy way, And come not near unto the opening of her house,
ylt.5:9: Lest thou give to others thy honour, And thy years to the fierce,
ylt.5:10: Lest strangers be filled with thy power, And thy labours in the house of a stranger,
ylt.5:11: And thou hast howled in thy latter end, In the consumption of thy flesh and thy food,
ylt.5:12: And hast said, `How have I hated instruction, And reproof hath my heart despised,
ylt.5:13: And I have not hearkened to the voice of my directors, And to my teachers have not inclined mine ear.
ylt.5:14: As a little thing I have been all evil, In the midst of an assembly and a company.
ylt.5:15: Drink waters out of thine own cistern, Even flowing ones out of thine own well.
ylt.5:16: Let thy fountains be scattered abroad, In broad places rivulets of waters.
ylt.5:17: Let them be to thee for thyself, And not to strangers with thee.
ylt.5:18: Let thy fountain be blessed, And rejoice because of the wife of thy youth,
ylt.5:19: A hind of loves, and a roe of grace! Let her loves satisfy thee at all times, In her love magnify thyself continually.
ylt.5:20: And why dost thou magnify thyself, My son, with a stranger? And embrace the bosom of a strange woman?
ylt.5:21: For over-against the eyes of Jehovah are the ways of each, And all his paths He is pondering.
ylt.5:22: His own iniquities do capture the wicked, And with the ropes of his sin he is holden.
ylt.5:23: He dieth without instruction, And in the abundance of his folly magnifieth himself!
ylt.6:1: My son! if thou hast been surety for thy friend, Hast stricken for a stranger thy hand,
ylt.6:2: Hast been snared with sayings of thy mouth, Hast been captured with sayings of thy mouth,
ylt.6:3: Do this now, my son, and be delivered, For thou hast come into the hand of thy friend. Go, trample on thyself, and strengthen thy friend,
ylt.6:4: Give not sleep to thine eyes, And slumber to thine eyelids,
ylt.6:5: Be delivered as a roe from the hand, And as a bird from the hand of a fowler.
ylt.6:6: Go unto the ant, O slothful one, See her ways and be wise;
ylt.6:7: Which hath not captain, overseer, and ruler,
ylt.6:8: She doth prepare in summer her bread, She hath gathered in harvest her food.
ylt.6:9: Till when, O slothful one, dost thou lie? When dost thou arise from thy sleep?
ylt.6:10: A little sleep, a little slumber, A little clasping of the hands to rest,
ylt.6:11: And thy poverty hath come as a traveller, And thy want as an armed man.
ylt.6:12: A man of worthlessness, a man of iniquity, Walking with perverseness of mouth,
ylt.6:13: Winking with his eyes, speaking with his feet, Directing with his fingers,
ylt.6:14: Frowardness is in his heart, devising evil at all times, Contentions he sendeth forth.
ylt.6:15: Therefore suddenly cometh his calamity, Instantly he is broken--and no healing.
ylt.6:16: These six hath Jehovah hated, Yea, seven are abominations to His soul.
ylt.6:17: Eyes high--tongues false--And hands shedding innocent blood--
ylt.6:18: A heart devising thoughts of vanity--Feet hasting to run to evil--
ylt.6:19: A false witness who doth breathe out lies--And one sending forth contentions between brethren.
ylt.6:20: Keep, my son, the command of thy father, And leave not the law of thy mother.
ylt.6:21: Bind them on thy heart continually, Tie them on thy neck.
ylt.6:22: In thy going up and down, it leadeth thee, In thy lying down, it watcheth over thee, And thou hast awaked--it talketh with thee.
ylt.6:23: For a lamp is the command, And the law a light, And a way of life are reproofs of instruction,
ylt.6:24: To preserve thee from an evil woman, From the flattery of the tongue of a strange woman.
ylt.6:25: Desire not her beauty in thy heart, And let her not take thee with her eyelids.
ylt.6:26: For a harlot consumeth unto a cake of bread, And an adulteress the precious soul hunteth.
ylt.6:27: Doth a man take fire into his bosom, And are his garments not burnt?
ylt.6:28: Doth a man walk on the hot coals, And are his feet not scorched?
ylt.6:29: So is he who hath gone in unto the wife of his neighbour, None who doth touch her is innocent.
ylt.6:30: They do not despise the thief, When he stealeth to fill his soul when he is hungry,
ylt.6:31: And being found he repayeth sevenfold, All the substance of his house he giveth.
ylt.6:32: He who committeth adultery with a woman lacketh heart, He is destroying his soul who doth it.
ylt.6:33: A stroke and shame he doth find, And his reproach is not wiped away,
ylt.6:34: For jealousy is the fury of a man, And he doth not spare in a day of vengeance.
ylt.6:35: He accepteth not the appearance of any atonement, Yea, he doth not consent, Though thou dost multiply bribes!
ylt.7:1: My son! keep my sayings, And my commands lay up with thee.
ylt.7:2: Keep my commands, and live, And my law as the pupil of thine eye.
ylt.7:3: Bind them on thy fingers, Write them on the tablet of thy heart.
ylt.7:4: Say to wisdom, `My sister Thou art.' And cry to understanding, `Kinswoman!'
ylt.7:5: To preserve thee from a strange woman, From a stranger who hath made smooth her sayings.
ylt.7:6: For, at a window of my house, Through my casement I have looked out,
ylt.7:7: And I do see among the simple ones, I discern among the sons, A young man lacking understanding,
ylt.7:8: Passing on in the street, near her corner, And the way to her house he doth step,
ylt.7:9: In the twilight--in the evening of day, In the darkness of night and blackness.
ylt.7:10: And, lo, a woman to meet him--(A harlot's dress, and watchful of heart,
ylt.7:11: Noisy she is, and stubborn, In her house her feet rest not.
ylt.7:12: Now in an out-place, now in broad places, And near every corner she lieth in wait) --
ylt.7:13: And she laid hold on him, and kissed him, She hath hardened her face, and saith to him,
ylt.7:14: `Sacrifices of peace-offerings are by me, To-day I have completed my vows.
ylt.7:15: Therefore I have come forth to meet thee, To seek earnestly thy face, and I find thee.
ylt.7:16: With ornamental coverings I decked my couch, Carved works--cotton of Egypt.
ylt.7:17: I sprinkled my bed--myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.
ylt.7:18: Come, we are filled with loves till the morning, We delight ourselves in loves.
ylt.7:19: For the man is not in his house, He hath gone on a long journey.
ylt.7:20: A bag of money he hath taken in his hand, At the day of the new moon he cometh to his house.'
ylt.7:21: She turneth him aside with the abundance of her speech, With the flattery of her lips she forceth him.
ylt.7:22: He is going after her straightway, As an ox unto the slaughter he cometh, And as a fetter unto the chastisement of a fool,
ylt.7:23: Till an arrow doth split his liver, As a bird hath hastened unto a snare, And hath not known that it is for its life.
ylt.7:24: And now, ye sons, hearken to me, And give attention to sayings of my mouth.
ylt.7:25: Let not thy heart turn unto her ways, Do not wander in her paths,
ylt.7:26: For many are the wounded she caused to fall, And mighty are all her slain ones.
ylt.7:27: The ways of Sheol--her house, Going down unto inner chambers of death!
ylt.8:1: Doth not wisdom call? And understanding give forth her voice?
ylt.8:2: At the head of high places by the way, Between the paths she hath stood,
ylt.8:3: At the side of the gates, at the mouth of the city, The entrance of the openings, she crieth aloud,
ylt.8:4: `Unto you, O men, I call, And my voice is unto the sons of men.
ylt.8:5: Understand, ye simple ones, prudence, And ye fools, understand the heart,
ylt.8:6: Hearken, for noble things I speak, And the opening of my lips is uprightness.
ylt.8:7: For truth doth my mouth utter, And an abomination to my lips is wickedness.
ylt.8:8: In righteousness are all the sayings of my mouth, Nothing in them is froward and perverse.
ylt.8:9: All of them are plain to the intelligent, And upright to those finding knowledge.
ylt.8:10: Receive my instruction, and not silver, And knowledge rather than choice gold.
ylt.8:11: For better is wisdom than rubies, Yea, all delights are not comparable with it.
ylt.8:12: I, wisdom, have dwelt with prudence, And a knowledge of devices I find out.
ylt.8:13: The fear of Jehovah is to hate evil; Pride, and arrogance, and an evil way, And a froward mouth, I have hated.
ylt.8:14: Mine is counsel and substance, I am understanding, I have might.
ylt.8:15: By me kings reign, and princes decree righteousness,
ylt.8:16: By me do chiefs rule, and nobles, All judges of the earth.
ylt.8:17: I love those loving me, And those seeking me earnestly do find me.
ylt.8:18: Wealth and honour are with me, Lasting substance and righteousness.
ylt.8:19: Better is my fruit than gold, even fine gold, And mine increase than choice silver.
ylt.8:20: In a path of righteousness I cause to walk, In midst of paths of judgment,
ylt.8:21: To cause my lovers to inherit substance, Yea, their treasures I fill.
ylt.8:22: Jehovah possessed me--the beginning of His way, Before His works since then.
ylt.8:23: From the age I was anointed, from the first, From former states of the earth.
ylt.8:24: In there being no depths, I was brought forth, In there being no fountains heavy with waters,
ylt.8:25: Before mountains were sunk, Before heights, I was brought forth.
ylt.8:26: While He had not made the earth, and out-places, And the top of the dusts of the world.
ylt.8:27: In His preparing the heavens I am there, In His decreeing a circle on the face of the deep,
ylt.8:28: In His strengthening clouds above, In His making strong fountains of the deep,
ylt.8:29: In His setting for the sea its limit, And the waters transgress not His command, In His decreeing the foundations of earth,
ylt.8:30: Then I am near Him, a workman, And I am a delight--day by day. Rejoicing before Him at all times,
ylt.8:31: Rejoicing in the habitable part of His earth, And my delights are with the sons of men.
ylt.8:32: And now, ye sons, hearken to me, Yea, happy are they who keep my ways.
ylt.8:33: Hear instruction, and be wise, and slight not.
ylt.8:34: O the happiness of the man hearkening to me, To watch at my doors day by day, To watch at the door-posts of my entrance.
ylt.8:35: For whoso is finding me, hath found life, And bringeth out good-will from Jehovah.
ylt.8:36: And whoso is missing me, is wronging his soul, All hating me have loved death!
ylt.9:1: Wisdom hath builded her house, She hath hewn out her pillars--seven.
ylt.9:2: She hath slaughtered her slaughter, She hath mingled her wine, Yea, she hath arranged her table.
ylt.9:3: She hath sent forth her damsels, She crieth on the tops of the high places of the city:
ylt.9:4: `Who is simple? let him turn aside hither.' Whoso lacketh heart: she hath said to him,
ylt.9:5: `Come, eat of my bread, And drink of the wine I have mingled.
ylt.9:6: Forsake ye, the simple, and live, And be happy in the way of understanding.
ylt.9:7: The instructor of a scorner Is receiving for it--shame, And a reprover of the wicked--his blemish.
ylt.9:8: Reprove not a scorner, lest he hate thee, Give reproof to the wise, and he loveth thee.
ylt.9:9: Give to the wise, and he is wiser still, Make known to the righteous, And he increaseth learning.
ylt.9:10: The commencement of wisdom is the fear of Jehovah, And a knowledge of the Holy Ones is understanding.
ylt.9:11: For by me do thy days multiply, And added to thee are years of life.
ylt.9:12: If thou hast been wise, thou hast been wise for thyself, And thou hast scorned--thyself bearest it.
ylt.9:13: A foolish woman is noisy, Simple, and hath not known what.
ylt.9:14: And she hath sat at the opening of her house, On a throne--the high places of the city,
ylt.9:15: To call to those passing by the way, Who are going straight on their paths.
ylt.9:16: `Who is simple? let him turn aside hither.' And whoso lacketh heart--she said to him,
ylt.9:17: `Stolen waters are sweet, And hidden bread is pleasant.'
ylt.9:18: And he hath not known that Rephaim are there, In deep places of Sheol her invited ones!
ylt.10:1: Proverbs of Solomon. A wise son causeth a father to rejoice, And a foolish son is an affliction to his mother.
ylt.10:2: Treasures of wickedness profit not, And righteousness delivereth from death.
ylt.10:3: Jehovah causeth not the soul of the righteous to hunger, And the desire of the wicked He thrusteth away.
ylt.10:4: Poor is he who is working--a slothful hand, And the hand of the diligent maketh rich.
ylt.10:5: Whoso is gathering in summer is a wise son, Whoso is sleeping in harvest is a son causing shame.
ylt.10:6: Blessings are for the head of the righteous, And the mouth of the wicked cover doth violence.
ylt.10:7: The remembrance of the righteous is for a blessing, And the name of the wicked doth rot.
ylt.10:8: The wise in heart accepteth commands, And a talkative fool kicketh.
ylt.10:9: Whoso is walking in integrity walketh confidently, And whoso is perverting his ways is known.
ylt.10:10: Whoso is winking the eye giveth grief, And a talkative fool kicketh.
ylt.10:11: A fountain of life is the mouth of the righteous, And the mouth of the wicked cover doth violence.
ylt.10:12: Hatred awaketh contentions, And over all transgressions love covereth.
ylt.10:13: In the lips of the intelligent is wisdom found, And a rod is for the back of him who is lacking understanding.
ylt.10:14: The wise lay up knowledge, and the mouth of a fool is near ruin.
ylt.10:15: The wealth of the rich is his strong city, The ruin of the poor is their poverty.
ylt.10:16: The wage of the righteous is for life, The increase of the wicked for sin.
ylt.10:17: A traveller to life is he who is keeping instruction, And whoso is forsaking rebuke is erring.
ylt.10:18: Whoso is covering hatred with lying lips, And whoso is bringing out an evil report is a fool.
ylt.10:19: In the abundance of words transgression ceaseth not, And whoso is restraining his lips is wise.
ylt.10:20: The tongue of the righteous is chosen silver, The heart of the wicked--as a little thing.
ylt.10:21: The lips of the righteous delight many, And fools for lack of heart die.
ylt.10:22: The blessing of Jehovah--it maketh rich, And He addeth no grief with it.
ylt.10:23: To execute inventions is as play to a fool, And wisdom to a man of understanding.
ylt.10:24: The feared thing of the wicked it meeteth him, And the desire of the righteous is given.
ylt.10:25: As the passing by of a hurricane, So the wicked is not, And the righteous is a foundation age-during.
ylt.10:26: As vinegar to the teeth, And as smoke to the eyes, So is the slothful to those sending him.
ylt.10:27: The fear of Jehovah addeth days, And the years of the wicked are shortened.
ylt.10:28: The hope of the righteous is joyful, And the expectation of the wicked perisheth.
ylt.10:29: The way of Jehovah is strength to the perfect, And ruin to workers of iniquity.
ylt.10:30: The righteous to the age is not moved, And the wicked inhabit not the earth.
ylt.10:31: The mouth of the righteous uttereth wisdom, And the tongue of frowardness is cut out.
ylt.10:32: The lips of the righteous know a pleasing thing, And the mouth of the wicked perverseness!
ylt.11:1: Balances of deceit are an abomination to Jehovah, And a perfect weight is His delight.
ylt.11:2: Pride hath come, and shame cometh, And with the lowly is wisdom.
ylt.11:3: The integrity of the upright leadeth them, And the perverseness of the treacherous destroyeth them.
ylt.11:4: Wealth profiteth not in a day of wrath, And righteousness delivereth from death.
ylt.11:5: The righteousness of the perfect maketh right his way, And by his wickedness doth the wicked fall.
ylt.11:6: The righteousness of the upright delivereth them, And in mischief the treacherous are captured.
ylt.11:7: In the death of a wicked man, hope perisheth, And the expectation of the iniquitous hath been lost.
ylt.11:8: The righteous from distress is drawn out, And the wicked goeth in instead of him.
ylt.11:9: With the mouth a hypocrite corrupteth his friend, And by knowledge the righteous are drawn out.
ylt.11:10: In the good of the righteous a city exulteth, And in the destruction of the wicked is singing.
ylt.11:11: By the blessing of the upright is a city exalted, And by the mouth of the wicked thrown down.
ylt.11:12: Whoso is despising his neighbour lacketh heart, And a man of understanding keepeth silence.
ylt.11:13: A busybody is revealing secret counsel, And the faithful of spirit is covering the matter.
ylt.11:14: Without counsels do a people fall, And deliverance is in a multitude of counsellors.
ylt.11:15: Evil one suffereth when he hath been surety for a stranger, And whoso is hating suretyship is confident.
ylt.11:16: A gracious woman retaineth honour, And terrible men retain riches.
ylt.11:17: A kind man is rewarding his own soul, And the fierce is troubling his own flesh.
ylt.11:18: The wicked is getting a lying wage, And whoso is sowing righteousness--a true reward.
ylt.11:19: Rightly is righteousness for life, And whoso is pursuing evil--for his own death.
ylt.11:20: An abomination to Jehovah are the perverse of heart, And the perfect of the way are His delight.
ylt.11:21: Hand to hand, the wicked is not acquitted, And the seed of the righteous hath escaped.
ylt.11:22: A ring of gold in the nose of a sow--A fair woman and stubborn of behaviour.
ylt.11:23: The desire of the righteous is only good, The hope of the wicked is transgression.
ylt.11:24: There is who is scattering, and yet is increased, And who is keeping back from uprightness, only to want.
ylt.11:25: A liberal soul is made fat, And whoso is watering, he also is watered.
ylt.11:26: Whoso is withholding corn, the people execrate him, And a blessing is for the head of him who is selling.
ylt.11:27: Whoso is earnestly seeking good Seeketh a pleasing thing, And whoso is seeking evil--it meeteth him.
ylt.11:28: Whoso is confident in his wealth he falleth, And as a leaf, the righteous flourish.
ylt.11:29: Whoso is troubling his own house inheriteth wind, And a servant is the fool to the wise of heart.
ylt.11:30: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, And whoso is taking souls is wise.
ylt.11:31: Lo, the righteous in the earth is recompensed, Surely also the wicked and the sinner!
ylt.12:1: Whoso is loving instruction, is loving knowledge, And whoso is hating reproof is brutish.
ylt.12:2: The good bringeth forth favour from Jehovah, And the man of wicked devices He condemneth.
ylt.12:3: A man is not established by wickedness, And the root of the righteous is not moved.
ylt.12:4: A virtuous woman is a crown to her husband, And as rottenness in his bones is one causing shame.
ylt.12:5: The thoughts of the righteous are justice, The counsels of the wicked--deceit.
ylt.12:6: The words of the wicked are: `Lay wait for blood,' And the mouth of the upright delivereth them.
ylt.12:7: Overthrow the wicked, and they are not, And the house of the righteous standeth.
ylt.12:8: According to his wisdom is a man praised, And the perverted of heart becometh despised.
ylt.12:9: Better is the lightly esteemed who hath a servant, Than the self-honoured who lacketh bread.
ylt.12:10: The righteous knoweth the life of his beast, And the mercies of the wicked are cruel.
ylt.12:11: Whoso is tilling the ground is satisfied with bread, And whoso is pursuing vanities is lacking heart,
ylt.12:12: The wicked hath desired the net of evil doers, And the root of the righteous giveth.
ylt.12:13: In transgression of the lips is the snare of the wicked, And the righteous goeth out from distress.
ylt.12:14: From the fruit of the mouth is one satisfied with good, And the deed of man's hands returneth to him.
ylt.12:15: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, And whoso is hearkening to counsel is wise.
ylt.12:16: The fool--in a day is his anger known, And the prudent is covering shame.
ylt.12:17: Whoso uttereth faithfulness declareth righteousness, And a false witness--deceit.
ylt.12:18: A rash speaker is like piercings of a sword, And the tongue of the wise is healing.
ylt.12:19: The lip of truth is established for ever, And for a moment--a tongue of falsehood.
ylt.12:20: Deceit is in the heart of those devising evil, And to those counselling peace is joy.
ylt.12:21: No iniquity is desired by the righteous, And the wicked have been full of evil.
ylt.12:22: An abomination to Jehovah are lying lips, And stedfast doers are his delight.
ylt.12:23: A prudent man is concealing knowledge, And the heart of fools proclaimeth folly.
ylt.12:24: The hand of the diligent ruleth, And slothfulness becometh tributary.
ylt.12:25: Sorrow in the heart of a man boweth down, And a good word maketh him glad.
ylt.12:26: The righteous searcheth his companion, And the way of the wicked causeth them to err.
ylt.12:27: The slothful roasteth not his hunting, And the wealth of a diligent man is precious.
ylt.12:28: In the path of righteousness is life, And in the way of that path is no death!
ylt.13:1: A wise son--the instruction of a father, And a scorner--he hath not heard rebuke.
ylt.13:2: From the fruit of the mouth a man eateth good, And the soul of the treacherous--violence.
ylt.13:3: Whoso is keeping his mouth, is keeping his soul, Whoso is opening wide his lips--ruin to him!
ylt.13:4: The soul of the slothful is desiring, and hath not. And the soul of the diligent is made fat.
ylt.13:5: A false word the righteous hateth, And the wicked causeth abhorrence, and is confounded.
ylt.13:6: Righteousness keepeth him who is perfect in the way, And wickedness overthroweth a sin offering.
ylt.13:7: There is who is making himself rich, and hath nothing, Who is making himself poor, and wealth is abundant.
ylt.13:8: The ransom of a man's life are his riches, And the poor hath not heard rebuke.
ylt.13:9: The light of the righteous rejoiceth, And the lamp of the wicked is extinguished.
ylt.13:10: A vain man through pride causeth debate, And with the counselled is wisdom.
ylt.13:11: Wealth from vanity becometh little, And whoso is gathering by the hand becometh great.
ylt.13:12: Hope prolonged is making the heart sick, And a tree of life is the coming desire.
ylt.13:13: Whoso is despising the Word is destroyed for it, And whoso is fearing the Command is repayed.
ylt.13:14: The law of the wise is a fountain of life, To turn aside from snares of death.
ylt.13:15: Good understanding giveth grace, And the way of the treacherous is hard.
ylt.13:16: Every prudent one dealeth with knowledge, And a fool spreadeth out folly.
ylt.13:17: A wicked messenger falleth into evil, And a faithful ambassador is healing.
ylt.13:18: Whoso is refusing instruction--poverty and shame, And whoso is observing reproof is honoured.
ylt.13:19: A desire accomplished is sweet to the soul, And an abomination to fools is: Turn from evil.
ylt.13:20: Whoso is walking with wise men is wise, And a companion of fools suffereth evil.
ylt.13:21: Evil pursueth sinners, And good recompenseth the righteous.
ylt.13:22: A good man causeth sons' sons to inherit, And laid up for the righteous is the sinner's wealth.
ylt.13:23: Abundance of food--the tillage of the poor, And substance is consumed without judgment.
ylt.13:24: Whoso is sparing his rod is hating his son, And whoso is loving him hath hastened him chastisement.
ylt.13:25: The righteous is eating to the satiety of his soul, And the belly of the wicked lacketh!
ylt.14:1: Every wise woman hath builded her house, And the foolish with her hands breaketh it down.
ylt.14:2: Whoso is walking in his uprightness is fearing Jehovah, And the perverted in his ways is despising Him.
ylt.14:3: In the mouth of a fool is a rod of pride, And the lips of the wise preserve them.
ylt.14:4: Without oxen a stall is clean, And great is the increase by the power of the ox.
ylt.14:5: A faithful witness lieth not, And a false witness breatheth out lies.
ylt.14:6: A scorner hath sought wisdom, and it is not, And knowledge to the intelligent is easy.
ylt.14:7: Go from before a foolish man, Or thou hast not known the lips of knowledge.
ylt.14:8: The wisdom of the prudent is to understand his way, And the folly of fools is deceit.
ylt.14:9: Fools mock at a guilt-offering, And among the upright--a pleasing thing.
ylt.14:10: The heart knoweth its own bitterness, And with its joy a stranger doth not intermeddle.
ylt.14:11: The house of the wicked is destroyed, And the tent of the upright flourisheth.
ylt.14:12: There is a way--right before a man, And its latter end are ways of death.
ylt.14:13: Even in laughter is the heart pained, And the latter end of joy is affliction.
ylt.14:14: From his ways is the backslider in heart filled, And a good man--from his fruits.
ylt.14:15: The simple giveth credence to everything, And the prudent attendeth to his step.
ylt.14:16: The wise is fearing and turning from evil, And a fool is transgressing and is confident.
ylt.14:17: Whoso is short of temper doth folly, And a man of wicked devices is hated.
ylt.14:18: The simple have inherited folly, And the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
ylt.14:19: The evil have bowed down before the good, And the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
ylt.14:20: Even of his neighbour is the poor hated, And those loving the rich are many.
ylt.14:21: Whoso is despising his neighbour sinneth, Whoso is favouring the humble, O his happiness.
ylt.14:22: Do not they err who are devising evil? And kindness and truth are to those devising good,
ylt.14:23: In all labour there is advantage, And a thing of the lips is only to want.
ylt.14:24: The crown of the wise is their wealth, The folly of fools is folly.
ylt.14:25: A true witness is delivering souls, And a deceitful one breatheth out lies.
ylt.14:26: In the fear of Jehovah is strong confidence, And to His sons there is a refuge.
ylt.14:27: The fear of Jehovah is a fountain of life, To turn aside from snares of death.
ylt.14:28: In the multitude of a people is the honour of a king, And in lack of people the ruin of a prince.
ylt.14:29: Whoso is slow to anger is of great understanding, And whoso is short in temper is exalting folly.
ylt.14:30: A healed heart is life to the flesh, And rottenness to the bones is envy.
ylt.14:31: An oppressor of the poor reproacheth his Maker, And whoso is honouring Him Is favouring the needy.
ylt.14:32: In his wickedness is the wicked driven away, And trustful in his death is the righteous.
ylt.14:33: In the heart of the intelligent wisdom doth rest. And in the midst of fools it is known.
ylt.14:34: Righteousness exalteth a nation, And the goodliness of peoples is a sin-offering.
ylt.14:35: The favour of a king is to a wise servant, And an object of his wrath is one causing shame!
ylt.15:1: A soft answer turneth back fury, And a grievous word raiseth up anger.
ylt.15:2: The tongue of the wise maketh knowledge good, And the mouth of fools uttereth folly.
ylt.15:3: In every place are the eyes of Jehovah, Watching the evil and the good.
ylt.15:4: A healed tongue is a tree of life, And perverseness in it--a breach in the spirit.
ylt.15:5: A fool despiseth the instruction of his father, And whoso is regarding reproof is prudent.
ylt.15:6: In the house of the righteous is abundant strength, And in the increase of the wicked--trouble.
ylt.15:7: The lips of the wise scatter knowledge, And the heart of fools is not right.
ylt.15:8: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to Jehovah, And the prayer of the upright is His delight.
ylt.15:9: An abomination to Jehovah is the way of the wicked, And whoso is pursuing righteousness He loveth.
ylt.15:10: Chastisement is grievous to him who is forsaking the path, Whoso is hating reproof dieth.
ylt.15:11: Sheol and destruction are before Jehovah, Surely also the hearts of the sons of men.
ylt.15:12: A scorner loveth not his reprover, Unto the wise he goeth not.
ylt.15:13: A joyful heart maketh glad the face, And by grief of heart is the spirit smitten.
ylt.15:14: The heart of the intelligent seeketh knowledge, And the mouth of fools enjoyeth folly.
ylt.15:15: All the days of the afflicted are evil, And gladness of heart is a perpetual banquet.
ylt.15:16: Better is a little with the fear of Jehovah, Than much treasure, and tumult with it.
ylt.15:17: Better is an allowance of green herbs and love there, Than a fatted ox, and hatred with it.
ylt.15:18: A man of fury stirreth up contention, And the slow to anger appeaseth strife.
ylt.15:19: The way of the slothful is as a hedge of briers, And the path of the upright is raised up.
ylt.15:20: A wise son rejoiceth a father. And a foolish man is despising his mother.
ylt.15:21: Folly is joy to one lacking heart, And a man of intelligence directeth his going.
ylt.15:22: Without counsel is the making void of purposes, And in a multitude of counsellors it is established.
ylt.15:23: Joy is to a man in the answer of his mouth, And a word in its season--how good!
ylt.15:24: A path of life is on high for the wise, To turn aside from Sheol beneath.
ylt.15:25: The house of the proud Jehovah pulleth down, And He setteth up the border of the widow.
ylt.15:26: An abomination to Jehovah are thoughts of wickedness, And pure are sayings of pleasantness.
ylt.15:27: A dishonest gainer is troubling his house, And whoso is hating gifts liveth.
ylt.15:28: The heart of the righteous meditateth to answer, And the mouth of the wicked uttereth evil things.
ylt.15:29: Far is Jehovah from the wicked, And the prayer of the righteous He heareth.
ylt.15:30: The light of the eyes rejoiceth the heart, A good report maketh fat the bone.
ylt.15:31: An ear that is hearing the reproof of life Doth lodge among the wise.
ylt.15:32: Whoso is refusing instruction is despising his soul, And whoso is hearing reproof Is getting understanding.
ylt.15:33: The fear of Jehovah is the instruction of wisdom, And before honour is humility!
ylt.16:1: Of man are arrangements of the heart, And from Jehovah an answer of the tongue.
ylt.16:2: All the ways of a man are pure in his own eyes, And Jehovah is pondering the spirits.
ylt.16:3: Roll unto Jehovah thy works, And established are thy purposes,
ylt.16:4: All things hath Jehovah wrought for Himself, And also the wicked worketh for a day of evil.
ylt.16:5: An abomination to Jehovah is every proud one of heart, Hand to hand he is not acquitted.
ylt.16:6: In kindness and truth pardoned is iniquity, And in the fear of Jehovah Turn thou aside from evil.
ylt.16:7: When a man's ways please Jehovah, even his enemies, He causeth to be at peace with him.
ylt.16:8: Better is a little with righteousness, Than abundance of increase without justice.
ylt.16:9: The heart of man deviseth his way, And Jehovah establisheth his step.
ylt.16:10: An oath is on the lips of a king, In judgment his mouth trespasseth not.
ylt.16:11: A just beam and balances are Jehovah's, His work are all the stones of the bag.
ylt.16:12: An abomination to kings is doing wickedness, For by righteousness is a throne established.
ylt.16:13: The delight of kings are righteous lips, And whoso is speaking uprightly he loveth,
ylt.16:14: The fury of a king is messengers of death, And a wise man pacifieth it.
ylt.16:15: In the light of a king's face is life, And his good-will is as a cloud of the latter rain.
ylt.16:16: To get wisdom--how much better than gold, And to get understanding to be chosen than silver!
ylt.16:17: A highway of the upright is, `Turn from evil,' Whoso is preserving his soul is watching his way.
ylt.16:18: Before destruction is pride, And before stumbling--a haughty spirit.'
ylt.16:19: Better is humility of spirit with the poor, Than to apportion spoil with the proud.
ylt.16:20: The wise in any matter findeth good, And whoso is trusting in Jehovah, O his happiness.
ylt.16:21: To the wise in heart is called, `Intelligent,' And sweetness of lips increaseth learning.
ylt.16:22: A fountain of life is understanding to its possessors, The instruction of fools is folly.
ylt.16:23: The heart of the wise causeth his mouth to act wisely, And by his lips he increaseth learning,
ylt.16:24: Sayings of pleasantness are a honeycomb, Sweet to the soul, and healing to the bone.
ylt.16:25: There is a way right before a man, And its latter end--ways of death.
ylt.16:26: A labouring man hath laboured for himself, For his mouth hath caused him to bend over it.
ylt.16:27: A worthless man is preparing evil, And on his lips--as a burning fire.
ylt.16:28: A froward man sendeth forth contention, A tale-bearer is separating a familiar friend.
ylt.16:29: A violent man enticeth his neighbour, And hath causeth him to go in a way not good.
ylt.16:30: Consulting his eyes to devise froward things, Moving his lips he hath accomplished evil.
ylt.16:31: A crown of beauty are grey hairs, In the way of righteousness it is found.
ylt.16:32: Better is the slow to anger than the mighty, And the ruler over his spirit than he who is taking a city.
ylt.16:33: Into the centre is the lot cast, And from Jehovah is all its judgment!
ylt.17:1: Better is a dry morsel, and rest with it, Than a house full of the sacrifices of strife.
ylt.17:2: A wise servant ruleth over a son causing shame, And in the midst of brethren He apportioneth an inheritance.
ylt.17:3: A refining pot is for silver, and a furnace for gold, And the trier of hearts is Jehovah.
ylt.17:4: An evil doer is attentive to lips of vanity, Falsehood is giving ear to a mischievous tongue.
ylt.17:5: Whoso is mocking at the poor Hath reproached his Maker, Whoso is rejoicing at calamity is not acquitted.
ylt.17:6: Sons' sons are the crown of old men, And the glory of sons are their fathers.
ylt.17:7: Not comely for a fool is a lip of excellency, Much less for a noble a lip of falsehood.
ylt.17:8: A stone of grace is the bribe in the eyes of its possessors, Whithersoever it turneth, it prospereth.
ylt.17:9: Whoso is covering transgression is seeking love, And whoso is repeating a matter Is separating a familiar friend.
ylt.17:10: Rebuke cometh down on the intelligent More than a hundred stripes on a fool.
ylt.17:11: An evil man seeketh only rebellion, And a fierce messenger is sent against him.
ylt.17:12: The meeting of a bereaved bear by a man, And--not a fool in his folly.
ylt.17:13: Whoso is returning evil for good, Evil moveth not from his house.
ylt.17:14: The beginning of contention is a letting out of waters, And before it is meddled with leave the strife.
ylt.17:15: Whoso is justifying the wicked, And condemning the righteous, Even both of these are an abomination to Jehovah.
ylt.17:16: Why is this--a price in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom, And a heart there is none?
ylt.17:17: At all times is the friend loving, And a brother for adversity is born.
ylt.17:18: A man lacking heart is striking hands, A surety he becometh before his friend.
ylt.17:19: Whoso is loving transgression is loving debate, Whoso is making high his entrance is seeking destruction.
ylt.17:20: The perverse of heart findeth not good, And the turned in his tongue falleth into evil.
ylt.17:21: Whoso is begetting a fool hath affliction for it, Yea, the father of a fool rejoiceth not.
ylt.17:22: A rejoicing heart doth good to the body, And a smitten spirit drieth the bone.
ylt.17:23: A bribe from the bosom the wicked taketh, To turn aside the paths of judgment.
ylt.17:24: The face of the intelligent is to wisdom, And the eyes of a fool--at the end of the earth.
ylt.17:25: A provocation to his father is a foolish son, And bitterness to her that bare him.
ylt.17:26: Also, to fine the righteous is not good, To smite nobles for uprightness.
ylt.17:27: One acquainted with knowledge is sparing his words, And the cool of temper is a man of understanding.
ylt.17:28: Even a fool keeping silence is reckoned wise, He who is shutting his lips intelligent!
ylt.18:1: For an object of desire he who is separated doth seek, With all wisdom he intermeddleth.
ylt.18:2: A fool delighteth not in understanding, But--in uncovering his heart.
ylt.18:3: With the coming of the wicked come also hath contempt, And with shame--reproach.
ylt.18:4: Deep waters are the words of a man's mouth, The fountain of wisdom is a flowing brook.
ylt.18:5: Acceptance of the face of the wicked is not good, To turn aside the righteous in judgment.
ylt.18:6: The lips of a fool enter into strife, And his mouth for stripes calleth.
ylt.18:7: The mouth of a fool is ruin to him, And his lips are the snare of his soul.
ylt.18:8: The words of a tale-bearer are as self-inflicted wounds, And they have gone down to the inner parts of the heart.
ylt.18:9: He also that is remiss in his work, A brother he is to a destroyer.
ylt.18:10: A tower of strength is the name of Jehovah, Into it the righteous runneth, and is set on high.
ylt.18:11: The wealth of the rich is the city of his strength, And as a wall set on high in his own imagination.
ylt.18:12: Before destruction the heart of man is high, And before honour is humility.
ylt.18:13: Whoso is answering a matter before he heareth, Folly it is to him and shame.
ylt.18:14: The spirit of a man sustaineth his sickness, And a smitten spirit who doth bear?
ylt.18:15: The heart of the intelligent getteth knowledge, And the ear of the wise seeketh knowledge.
ylt.18:16: The gift of a man maketh room for him, And before the great it leadeth him.
ylt.18:17: Righteous is the first in his own cause, His neighbour cometh and hath searched him.
ylt.18:18: The lot causeth contentions to cease, And between the mighty it separateth.
ylt.18:19: A brother transgressed against is as a strong city, And contentions as the bar of a palace.
ylt.18:20: From the fruit of a man's mouth is his belly satisfied, From the increase of his lips he is satisfied.
ylt.18:21: Death and life are in the power of the tongue, And those loving it eat its fruit.
ylt.18:22: Whoso hath found a wife hath found good, And bringeth out good-will from Jehovah.
ylt.18:23: With supplications doth the poor speak, And the rich answereth fierce things.
ylt.18:24: A man with friends is to show himself friendly, And there is a lover adhering more than a brother!
ylt.19:1: Better is the poor walking in his integrity, Than the perverse in his lips, who is a fool.
ylt.19:2: Also, without knowledge the soul is not good, And the hasty in feet is sinning.
ylt.19:3: The folly of man perverteth his way, And against Jehovah is his heart wroth.
ylt.19:4: Wealth addeth many friends, And the poor from his neighbour is separated.
ylt.19:5: A false witness is not acquitted, Whoso breatheth out lies is not delivered.
ylt.19:6: Many entreat the face of the noble, And all have made friendship to a man of gifts.
ylt.19:7: All the brethren of the poor have hated him, Surely also his friends have been far from him, He is pursuing words--they are not!
ylt.19:8: Whoso is getting heart is loving his soul, He is keeping understanding to find good.
ylt.19:9: A false witness is not acquitted, And whoso breatheth out lies perisheth.
ylt.19:10: Luxury is not comely for a fool, Much less for a servant to rule among princes.
ylt.19:11: The wisdom of a man hath deferred his anger, And his glory is to pass over transgression.
ylt.19:12: The wrath of a king is a growl as of a young lion, And as dew on the herb his good-will.
ylt.19:13: A calamity to his father is a foolish son, And the contentions of a wife are a continual dropping.
ylt.19:14: House and wealth are the inheritance of fathers, And from Jehovah is an understanding wife.
ylt.19:15: Sloth causeth deep sleep to fall, And an indolent soul doth hunger.
ylt.19:16: Whoso is keeping the command is keeping his soul, Whoso is despising His ways dieth.
ylt.19:17: Whoso is lending to Jehovah is favouring the poor, And his deed He repayeth to him.
ylt.19:18: Chastise thy son, for there is hope, And to put him to death lift not up thy soul.
ylt.19:19: A man of great wrath is bearing punishment, For, if thou dost deliver, yet again thou dost add.
ylt.19:20: Hear counsel and receive instruction, So that thou art wise in thy latter end.
ylt.19:21: Many are the purposes in a man's heart, And the counsel of Jehovah it standeth.
ylt.19:22: The desirableness of a man is his kindness, And better is the poor than a liar.
ylt.19:23: The fear of Jehovah is to life, And satisfied he remaineth--he is not charged with evil.
ylt.19:24: The slothful hath hidden his hand in a dish, Even unto his mouth he bringeth it not back.
ylt.19:25: A scorner smite, and the simple acts prudently, And give reproof to the intelligent, He understandeth knowledge.
ylt.19:26: Whoso is spoiling a father causeth a mother to flee, A son causing shame, and bringing confusion.
ylt.19:27: Cease, my son, to hear instruction--To err from sayings of knowledge.
ylt.19:28: A worthless witness scorneth judgment, And the mouth of the wicked swalloweth iniquity.
ylt.19:29: Judgments have been prepared for scorners, And stripes for the back of fools!
ylt.20:1: Wine is a scorner--strong drink is noisy, And any going astray in it is not wise.
ylt.20:2: The fear of a king is a growl as of a young lion, He who is causing him to be wroth is wronging his soul.
ylt.20:3: An honour to a man is cessation from strife, And every fool intermeddleth.
ylt.20:4: Because of winter the slothful plougheth not, He asketh in harvest, and there is nothing.
ylt.20:5: Counsel in the heart of a man is deep water, And a man of understanding draweth it up.
ylt.20:6: A multitude of men proclaim each his kindness, And a man of stedfastness who doth find?
ylt.20:7: The righteous is walking habitually in his integrity, O the happiness of his sons after him!
ylt.20:8: A king sitting on a throne of judgment, Is scattering with his eyes all evil,
ylt.20:9: Who saith, `I have purified my heart, I have been cleansed from my sin?'
ylt.20:10: A stone and a stone, an ephah and an ephah, Even both of them are an abomination to Jehovah.
ylt.20:11: Even by his actions a youth maketh himself known, Whether his work be pure or upright.
ylt.20:12: A hearing ear, and a seeing eye, Jehovah hath made even both of them.
ylt.20:13: Love not sleep, lest thou become poor, Open thine eyes--be satisfied with bread.
ylt.20:14: `Bad, bad,' saith the buyer, And going his way then he boasteth himself.
ylt.20:15: Substance, gold, and a multitude of rubies, Yea, a precious vessel, are lips of knowledge.
ylt.20:16: Take his garment when a stranger hath been surety, And for strangers pledge it.
ylt.20:17: Sweet to a man is the bread of falsehood, And afterwards is his mouth filled with gravel.
ylt.20:18: Purposes by counsel thou dost establish, And with plans make thou war.
ylt.20:19: A revealer of secret counsels is the busybody, And for a deceiver with his lips make not thyself surety.
ylt.20:20: Whoso is vilifying his father and his mother, Extinguished is his lamp in blackness of darkness.
ylt.20:21: An inheritance gotten wrongly at first, Even its latter end is not blessed.
ylt.20:22: Do not say, `I recompense evil,' Wait for Jehovah, and He delivereth thee.
ylt.20:23: An abomination to Jehovah are a stone and a stone, And balances of deceit are not good.
ylt.20:24: From Jehovah are the steps of a man, And man--how understandeth he his way?
