ylt.20:25: A snare to a man is he hath swallowed a holy thing, And after vows to make inquiry.
ylt.20:26: A wise king is scattering the wicked, And turneth back on them the wheel.
ylt.20:27: The breath of man is a lamp of Jehovah, Searching all the inner parts of the heart.
ylt.20:28: Kindness and truth keep a king, And he hath supported by kindness his throne.
ylt.20:29: The beauty of young men is their strength, And the honour of old men is grey hairs.
ylt.20:30: The bandages of a wound thou removest with the evil, Also the plagues of the inner parts of the heart!
ylt.21:1: Rivulets of waters is the heart of a king in the hand of Jehovah, Wherever He pleaseth He inclineth it.
ylt.21:2: Every way of a man is right in his own eyes, And Jehovah is pondering hearts.
ylt.21:3: To do righteousness and judgment, Is chosen of Jehovah rather than sacrifice.
ylt.21:4: Loftiness of eyes, and breadth of heart, Tillage of the wicked is sin.
ylt.21:5: The purposes of the diligent are only to advantage, And of every hasty one, only to want.
ylt.21:6: The making of treasures by a lying tongue, Is a vanity driven away of those seeking death.
ylt.21:7: The spoil of the wicked catcheth them, Because they have refused to do judgment.
ylt.21:8: Froward is the way of a man who is vile, And the pure--upright is his work.
ylt.21:9: Better to sit on a corner of the roof, Than with a woman of contentions and a house of company.
ylt.21:10: The soul of the wicked hath desired evil, Not gracious in his eyes is his neighbour.
ylt.21:11: When the scorner is punished, the simple becometh wise, And in giving understanding to the wise He receiveth knowledge.
ylt.21:12: The Righteous One is acting wisely Towards the house of the wicked, He is overthrowing the wicked for wickedness.
ylt.21:13: Whoso is shutting his ear from the cry of the poor, He also doth cry, and is not answered.
ylt.21:14: A gift in secret pacifieth anger, And a bribe in the bosom strong fury.
ylt.21:15: To do justice is joy to the righteous, But ruin to workers of iniquity.
ylt.21:16: A man who is wandering from the way of understanding, In an assembly of Rephaim resteth.
ylt.21:17: Whoso is loving mirth is a poor man, Whoso is loving wine and oil maketh no wealth.
ylt.21:18: The wicked is an atonement for the righteous, And for the upright the treacherous dealer.
ylt.21:19: Better to dwell in a wilderness land, Than with a woman of contentions and anger.
ylt.21:20: A treasure to be desired, and oil, Is in the habitation of the wise, And a foolish man swalloweth it up.
ylt.21:21: Whoso is pursuing righteousness and kindness, Findeth life, righteousness, and honour.
ylt.21:22: A city of the mighty hath the wise gone up, And bringeth down the strength of its confidence.
ylt.21:23: Whoso is keeping his mouth and his tongue, Is keeping from adversities his soul.
ylt.21:24: Proud, haughty, scorner is his name, Who is working in the wrath of pride.
ylt.21:25: The desire of the slothful slayeth him, For his hands have refused to work.
ylt.21:26: All the day desiring he hath desired, And the righteous giveth and withholdeth not.
ylt.21:27: The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination, Much more when in wickedness he bringeth it.
ylt.21:28: A false witness doth perish, And an attentive man for ever speaketh.
ylt.21:29: A wicked man hath hardened by his face, And the upright--he prepareth his way.
ylt.21:30: There is no wisdom, nor understanding, Nor counsel, over-against Jehovah.
ylt.21:31: A horse is prepared for a day of battle, And the deliverance is of Jehovah!
ylt.22:1: A name is chosen rather than much wealth, Than silver and than gold--good grace.
ylt.22:2: Rich and poor have met together, The Maker of them all is Jehovah.
ylt.22:3: The prudent hath seen the evil, and is hidden, And the simple have passed on, and are punished.
ylt.22:4: The end of humility is the fear of Jehovah, Riches, and honour, and life.
ylt.22:5: Thorns--snares are in the way of the perverse, Whoso is keeping his soul is far from them.
ylt.22:6: Give instruction to a youth about his way, Even when he is old he turneth not from it.
ylt.22:7: The rich over the poor ruleth, And a servant is the borrower to the lender.
ylt.22:8: Whoso is sowing perverseness reapeth sorrow, And the rod of his anger weareth out.
ylt.22:9: The good of eye--he is blessed, For he hath given of his bread to the poor.
ylt.22:10: Cast out a scorner--and contention goeth out, And strife and shame cease.
ylt.22:11: Whoso is loving cleanness of heart, Grace are his lips, a king is his friend.
ylt.22:12: The eyes of Jehovah have kept knowledge, And He overthroweth the words of the treacherous.
ylt.22:13: The slothful hath said, `A lion is without, In the midst of the broad places I am slain.'
ylt.22:14: A deep pit is the mouth of strange women, The abhorred of Jehovah falleth there.
ylt.22:15: Folly is bound up in the heart of a youth, The rod of chastisement putteth it far from him.
ylt.22:16: He is oppressing the poor to multiply to him, He is giving to the rich--only to want.
ylt.22:17: Incline thine ear, and hear words of the wise, And thy heart set to my knowledge,
ylt.22:18: For they are pleasant when thou dost keep them in thy heart, They are prepared together for thy lips.
ylt.22:19: That thy trust may be in Jehovah, I caused thee to know to-day, even thou.
ylt.22:20: Have I not written to thee three times With counsels and knowledge?
ylt.22:21: To cause thee to know the certainty of sayings of truth, To return sayings of truth to those sending thee.
ylt.22:22: Rob not the poor because he is poor, And bruise not the afflicted in the gate.
ylt.22:23: For Jehovah pleadeth their cause, And hath spoiled the soul of their spoilers.
ylt.22:24: Shew not thyself friendly with an angry man, And with a man of fury go not in,
ylt.22:25: Lest thou learn his paths, And have received a snare to thy soul.
ylt.22:26: Be not thou among those striking hands, Among sureties for burdens.
ylt.22:27: If thou hast nothing to pay, Why doth he take thy bed from under thee?
ylt.22:28: Remove not a border of olden times, That thy fathers have made.
ylt.22:29: Hast thou seen a man speedy in his business? Before kings he doth station himself, He stations not himself before obscure men!
ylt.23:1: When thou sittest to eat with a ruler, Thou considerest diligently that which is before thee,
ylt.23:2: And thou hast put a knife to thy throat, If thou art a man of appetite.
ylt.23:3: Have no desire to his dainties, seeing it is lying food.
ylt.23:4: Labour not to make wealth, From thine own understanding cease, Dost thou cause thine eyes to fly upon it? Then it is not.
ylt.23:5: For wealth maketh to itself wings, As an eagle it flieth to the heavens.
ylt.23:6: Eat not the bread of an evil eye, And have no desire to his dainties,
ylt.23:7: For as he hath thought in his soul, so is he, `Eat and drink,' saith he to thee, And his heart is not with thee.
ylt.23:8: Thy morsel thou hast eaten thou dost vomit up, And hast marred thy words that are sweet.
ylt.23:9: In the ears of a fool speak not, For he treadeth on the wisdom of thy words.
ylt.23:10: Remove not a border of olden times, And into fields of the fatherless enter not,
ylt.23:11: For their Redeemer is strong, He doth plead their cause with thee.
ylt.23:12: Bring in to instruction thy heart, And thine ear to sayings of knowledge.
ylt.23:13: Withhold not from a youth chastisement, When thou smitest him with a rod he dieth not.
ylt.23:14: Thou with a rod smitest him, And his soul from Sheol thou deliverest.
ylt.23:15: My son, if thy heart hath been wise, My heart rejoiceth, even mine,
ylt.23:16: And my reins exult when thy lips speak uprightly.
ylt.23:17: Let not thy heart be envious at sinners, But--in the fear of Jehovah all the day.
ylt.23:18: For, is there a posterity? Then thy hope is not cut off.
ylt.23:19: Hear thou, my son, and be wise, And make happy in the way thy heart,
ylt.23:20: Be not thou among quaffers of wine, Among gluttonous ones of flesh,
ylt.23:21: For the quaffer and glutton become poor, And drowsiness clotheth with rags.
ylt.23:22: Hearken to thy father, who begat thee, And despise not thy mother when she hath become old.
ylt.23:23: Truth buy, and sell not, Wisdom, and instruction, and understanding,
ylt.23:24: The father of the righteous rejoiceth greatly, The begetter of the wise rejoiceth in him.
ylt.23:25: Rejoice doth thy father and thy mother, Yea, she that bare thee is joyful.
ylt.23:26: Give, my son, thy heart to me, And let thine eyes watch my ways.
ylt.23:27: For a harlot is a deep ditch, And a strange woman is a strait pit.
ylt.23:28: She also, as catching prey, lieth in wait, And the treacherous among men she increaseth.
ylt.23:29: Who hath woe? who hath sorrow? Who hath contentions? who hath plaint? Who hath wounds without cause? Who hath redness of eyes?
ylt.23:30: Those tarrying by the wine, Those going in to search out mixed wine.
ylt.23:31: See not wine when it showeth itself red, When it giveth in the cup its colour, It goeth up and down through the upright.
ylt.23:32: Its latter end--as a serpent it biteth, And as a basilisk it stingeth.
ylt.23:33: Thine eyes see strange women, And thy heart speaketh perverse things.
ylt.23:34: And thou hast been as one lying down in the heart of the sea, And as one lying down on the top of a mast.
ylt.23:35: `They smote me, I have not been sick, They beat me, I have not known. When I awake--I seek it yet again!'
ylt.24:1: Be not envious of evil men, And desire not to be with them.
ylt.24:2: For destruction doth their heart meditate, And perverseness do their lips speak.
ylt.24:3: By wisdom is a house builded, And by understanding it establisheth itself.
ylt.24:4: And by knowledge the inner parts are filled, With all precious and pleasant wealth.
ylt.24:5: Mighty is the wise in strength, And a man of knowledge is strengthening power,
ylt.24:6: For by plans thou makest for thyself war, And deliverance is in a multitude of counsellors.
ylt.24:7: Wisdom is high for a fool, In the gate he openeth not his mouth.
ylt.24:8: Whoso is devising to do evil, Him they call a master of wicked thoughts.
ylt.24:9: The thought of folly is sin, And an abomination to man is a scorner.
ylt.24:10: Thou hast shewed thyself weak in a day of adversity, Straitened is thy power,
ylt.24:11: If from delivering those taken to death, And those slipping to the slaughter--thou keepest back.
ylt.24:12: When thou sayest, `Lo, we knew not this.' Is not the Ponderer of hearts He who understandeth? And the Keeper of thy soul He who knoweth? And He hath rendered to man according to his work.
ylt.24:13: Eat my son, honey that is good, And the honeycomb--sweet to thy palate.
ylt.24:14: So is the knowledge of wisdom to thy soul, If thou hast found that there is a posterity And thy hope is not cut off.
ylt.24:15: Lay not wait, O wicked one, At the habitation of the righteous. Do not spoil his resting-place.
ylt.24:16: For seven times doth the righteous fall and rise, And the wicked stumble in evil.
ylt.24:17: In the falling of thine enemy rejoice not, And in his stumbling let not thy heart be joyful,
ylt.24:18: Lest Jehovah see, and it be evil in His eyes, And He hath turned from off him His anger.
ylt.24:19: Fret not thyself at evil doers, Be not envious at the wicked,
ylt.24:20: For there is not a posterity to the evil, The lamp of the wicked is extinguished.
ylt.24:21: Fear Jehovah, my son, and the king, With changers mix not up thyself,
ylt.24:22: For suddenly doth their calamity rise, And the ruin of them both--who knoweth!
ylt.24:23: These also are for the wise: --To discern faces in judgment is not good.
ylt.24:24: Whoso is saying to the wicked, `Thou art righteous,' Peoples execrate him--nations abhor him.
ylt.24:25: And to those reproving it is pleasant, And on them cometh a good blessing.
ylt.24:26: Lips he kisseth who is returning straightforward words.
ylt.24:27: Prepare in an out-place thy work, And make it ready in the field--go afterwards, Then thou hast built thy house.
ylt.24:28: Be not a witness for nought against thy neighbour, Or thou hast enticed with thy lips.
ylt.24:29: Say not, `As he did to me, so I do to him, I render to each according to his work.'
ylt.24:30: Near the field of a slothful man I passed by, And near the vineyard of a man lacking heart.
ylt.24:31: And lo, it hath gone up--all of it--thorns! Covered its face have nettles, And its stone wall hath been broken down.
ylt.24:32: And I see--I--I do set my heart, I have seen--I have received instruction,
ylt.24:33: A little sleep--a little slumber--A little folding of the hands to lie down.
ylt.24:34: And thy poverty hath come as a traveller, And thy want as an armed man!
ylt.25:1: Also these are Proverbs of Solomon, that men of Hezekiah king of Judah transcribed: --
ylt.25:2: The honour of God is to hide a thing, And the honour of kings to search out a matter.
ylt.25:3: The heavens for height, and the earth for depth, And the heart of kings-- are unsearchable.
ylt.25:4: Take away dross from silver, And a vessel for the refiner goeth forth,
ylt.25:5: Take away the wicked before a king, And established in righteousness is his throne.
ylt.25:6: Honour not thyself before a king, And in the place of the great stand not.
ylt.25:7: For better that he hath said to thee, `Come thou up hither,' Than that he humble thee before a noble, Whom thine eyes have seen.
ylt.25:8: Go not forth to strive, haste, turn, What dost thou in its latter end, When thy neighbour causeth thee to blush?
ylt.25:9: Thy cause plead with thy neighbour, And the secret counsel of another reveal not,
ylt.25:10: Lest the hearer put thee to shame, And thine evil report turn not back.
ylt.25:11: Apples of gold in imagery of silver, Is the word spoken at its fit times.
ylt.25:12: A ring of gold, and an ornament of pure gold, Is the wise reprover to an attentive ear.
ylt.25:13: As a vessel of snow in a day of harvest, So is a faithful ambassador to those sending him, And the soul of his masters he refresheth.
ylt.25:14: Clouds and wind, and rain there is none, Is a man boasting himself in a false gift.
ylt.25:15: By long-suffering is a ruler persuaded, And a soft tongue breaketh a bone.
ylt.25:16: Honey thou hast found--eat thy sufficiency, Lest thou be satiated with it, and hast vomited it.
ylt.25:17: Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbour's house, Lest he be satiated with thee, and have hated thee.
ylt.25:18: A maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow, Is the man testifying against his neighbour a false testimony.
ylt.25:19: A bad tooth, and a tottering foot, Is the confidence of the treacherous in a day of adversity.
ylt.25:20: Whoso is taking away a garment in a cold day, Is as vinegar on nitre, And a singer of songs on a sad heart.
ylt.25:21: If he who is hating thee doth hunger, cause him to eat bread, And if he thirst, cause him to drink water.
ylt.25:22: For coals thou art putting on his head, And Jehovah giveth recompense to thee.
ylt.25:23: A north wind bringeth forth rain, And a secret tongue--indignant faces.
ylt.25:24: Better to sit on a corner of a roof, Than with a woman of contentions, and a house of company.
ylt.25:25: As cold waters for a weary soul, So is a good report from a far country.
ylt.25:26: A spring troubled, and a fountain corrupt, Is the righteous falling before the wicked.
ylt.25:27: The eating of much honey is not good, Nor a searching out of one's own honour--honour.
ylt.25:28: A city broken down without walls, Is a man without restraint over his spirit!
ylt.26:1: As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, So honour is not comely for a fool.
ylt.26:2: As a bird by wandering, as a swallow by flying, So reviling without cause doth not come.
ylt.26:3: A whip is for a horse, a bridle for an ass, And a rod for the back of fools.
ylt.26:4: Answer not a fool according to his folly, Lest thou be like to him--even thou.
ylt.26:5: Answer a fool according to his folly, Lest he be wise in his own eyes.
ylt.26:6: He is cutting off feet, he is drinking injury, Who is sending things by the hand of a fool.
ylt.26:7: Weak have been the two legs of the lame, And a parable in the mouth of fools.
ylt.26:8: As one who is binding a stone in a sling, So is he who is giving honour to a fool.
ylt.26:9: A thorn hath gone up into the hand of a drunkard, And a parable in the mouth of fools.
ylt.26:10: Great is the Former of all, And He is rewarding a fool, And is rewarding transgressors.
ylt.26:11: As a dog hath returned to its vomit, A fool is repeating his folly.
ylt.26:12: Thou hast seen a man wise in his own eyes, More hope of a fool than of him!
ylt.26:13: The slothful hath said, `A lion is in the way, A lion is in the broad places.'
ylt.26:14: The door turneth round on its hinge, And the slothful on his bed.
ylt.26:15: The slothful hath hid his hand in a dish, He is weary of bringing it back to his mouth.
ylt.26:16: Wiser is the slothful in his own eyes, Than seven men returning a reason.
ylt.26:17: Laying hold on the ears of a dog, Is a passer-by making himself wrath for strife not his own.
ylt.26:18: As one pretending to be feeble, Who is casting sparks, arrows, and death,
ylt.26:19: So hath a man deceived his neighbour, And hath said, `Am not I playing?'
ylt.26:20: Without wood is fire going out, And without a tale-bearer, contention ceaseth,
ylt.26:21: Coal to burning coals, and wood to fire, And a man of contentions to kindle strife.
ylt.26:22: The words of a tale-bearer are as self-inflicted wounds, And they have gone down to the inner parts of the heart.
ylt.26:23: Silver of dross spread over potsherd, Are burning lips and an evil heart.
ylt.26:24: By his lips doth a hater dissemble, And in his heart he placeth deceit,
ylt.26:25: When his voice is gracious trust not in him, For seven abominations are in his heart.
ylt.26:26: Hatred is covered by deceit, Revealed is its wickedness in an assembly.
ylt.26:27: Whoso is digging a pit falleth into it, And the roller of a stone, to him it turneth.
ylt.26:28: A lying tongue hateth its bruised ones, And a flattering mouth worketh an overthrow!
ylt.27:1: Boast not thyself of to-morrow, For thou knowest not what a day bringeth forth.
ylt.27:2: Let another praise thee, and not thine own mouth, A stranger, and not thine own lips.
ylt.27:3: A stone is heavy, and the sand is heavy, And the anger of a fool Is heavier than they both.
ylt.27:4: Fury is fierce, and anger is overflowing, And who standeth before jealousy?
ylt.27:5: Better is open reproof than hidden love.
ylt.27:6: Faithful are the wounds of a lover, And abundant the kisses of an enemy.
ylt.27:7: A satiated soul treadeth down a honeycomb, And to a hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.
ylt.27:8: As a bird wandering from her nest, So is a man wandering from his place.
ylt.27:9: Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart, And the sweetness of one's friend--from counsel of the soul.
ylt.27:10: Thine own friend, and the friend of thy father, forsake not, And the house of thy brother enter not In a day of thy calamity, Better is a near neighbour than a brother afar off.
ylt.27:11: Be wise, my son, and rejoice my heart. And I return my reproacher a word.
ylt.27:12: The prudent hath seen the evil, he is hidden, The simple have passed on, they are punished.
ylt.27:13: Take his garment, when a stranger hath been surety, And for a strange woman pledge it.
ylt.27:14: Whoso is saluting his friend with a loud voice, In the morning rising early, A light thing it is reckoned to him.
ylt.27:15: A continual dropping in a day of rain, And a woman of contentions are alike,
ylt.27:16: Whoso is hiding her hath hidden the wind, And the ointment of his right hand calleth out.
ylt.27:17: Iron by iron is sharpened, And a man sharpens the face of his friend.
ylt.27:18: The keeper of a fig-tree eateth its fruit, And the preserver of his master is honoured.
ylt.27:19: As in water the face is to face, So the heart of man to man.
ylt.27:20: Sheol and destruction are not satisfied, And the eyes of man are not satisfied.
ylt.27:21: A refining pot is for silver, and a furnace for gold, And a man according to his praise.
ylt.27:22: If thou dost beat the foolish in a mortar, Among washed things--with a pestle, His folly turneth not aside from off him.
ylt.27:23: Know well the face of thy flock, Set thy heart to the droves,
ylt.27:24: For riches are not to the age, Nor a crown to generation and generation.
ylt.27:25: Revealed was the hay, and seen the tender grass, And gathered the herbs of mountains.
ylt.27:26: Lambs are for thy clothing, And the price of the field are he-goats,
ylt.27:27: And a sufficiency of goats' milk is for thy bread, For bread to thy house, and life to thy damsels!
ylt.28:1: The wicked have fled and there is no pursuer. And the righteous as a young lion is confident.
ylt.28:2: By the transgression of a land many are its heads. And by an intelligent man, Who knoweth right--it is prolonged.
ylt.28:3: A man--poor and oppressing the weak, Is a sweeping rain, and there is no bread.
ylt.28:4: Those forsaking the law praise the wicked, Those keeping the law plead against them.
ylt.28:5: Evil men understand not judgment, And those seeking Jehovah understand all.
ylt.28:6: Better is the poor walking in his integrity, Than the perverse of ways who is rich.
ylt.28:7: Whoso is keeping the law is an intelligent son, And a friend of gluttons, Doth cause his father to blush.
ylt.28:8: Whoso is multiplying his wealth by biting and usury, For one favouring the poor doth gather it.
ylt.28:9: Whoso is turning his ear from hearing the law, Even his prayer is an abomination.
ylt.28:10: Whoso is causing the upright to err in an evil way, Into his own pit he doth fall, And the perfect do inherit good.
ylt.28:11: A rich man is wise in his own eyes, And the intelligent poor searcheth him.
ylt.28:12: In the exulting of the righteous the glory is abundant, And in the rising of the wicked man is apprehensive.
ylt.28:13: Whoso is covering his transgressions prospereth not, And he who is confessing and forsaking hath mercy.
ylt.28:14: O the happiness of a man fearing continually, And whoso is hardening his heart falleth into evil.
ylt.28:15: A growling lion, and a ranging bear, Is the wicked ruler over a poor people.
ylt.28:16: A leader lacking understanding multiplieth oppressions, Whoso is hating dishonest gain prolongeth days.
ylt.28:17: A man oppressed with the blood of a soul, Unto the pit fleeth, none taketh hold on him.
ylt.28:18: Whoso is walking uprightly is saved, And the perverted of ways falleth at once.
ylt.28:19: Whoso is tilling his ground is satisfied with bread, And whoso is pursuing vanity, Is filled with poverty.
ylt.28:20: A stedfast man hath multiplied blessings, And whoso is hasting to be rich is not acquitted.
ylt.28:21: To discern faces is not good, And for a piece of bread doth a man transgress.
ylt.28:22: Troubled for wealth is the man with an evil eye, And he knoweth not that want doth meet him.
ylt.28:23: Whoso is reproving a man afterwards findeth grace, More than a flatterer with the tongue.
ylt.28:24: Whoso is robbing his father, or his mother, And is saying, `It is not transgression,' A companion he is to a destroyer.
ylt.28:25: Whoso is proud in soul stirreth up contention, And whoso is trusting on Jehovah is made fat.
ylt.28:26: Whoso is trusting in his heart is a fool, And whoso is walking in wisdom is delivered.
ylt.28:27: Whoso is giving to the poor hath no lack, And whoso is hiding his eyes multiplied curses.
ylt.28:28: In the rising of the wicked a man is hidden, And in their destruction the righteous multiply!
ylt.29:1: A man often reproved, hardening the neck, Is suddenly broken, and there is no healing.
ylt.29:2: In the multiplying of the righteous the people rejoice, And in the ruling of the wicked the people sigh.
ylt.29:3: A man loving wisdom rejoiceth his father, And a friend of harlots destroyeth wealth.
ylt.29:4: A king by judgment establisheth a land, And one receiving gifts throweth it down.
ylt.29:5: A man taking a portion above his neighbour, Spreadeth a net for his own steps.
ylt.29:6: In the transgression of the evil is a snare, And the righteous doth sing and rejoice.
ylt.29:7: The righteous knoweth the plea of the poor, The wicked understandeth not knowledge.
ylt.29:8: Men of scorning ensnare a city, And the wise turn back anger.
ylt.29:9: A wise man is judged by the foolish man, And he hath been angry, And he hath laughed, and there is no rest.
ylt.29:10: Men of blood hate the perfect, And the upright seek his soul.
ylt.29:11: A fool bringeth out all his mind, And the wise till afterwards restraineth it.
ylt.29:12: A ruler who is attending to lying words, All his ministers are wicked.
ylt.29:13: The poor and the man of frauds have met together, Jehovah is enlightening the eyes of them both.
ylt.29:14: a king that is judging truly the poor, His throne for ever is established.
ylt.29:15: A rod and reproof give wisdom, And a youth let away is shaming his mother.
ylt.29:16: In the multiplying of the wicked transgression multiplieth, And the righteous on their fall do look.
ylt.29:17: Chastise thy son, and he giveth thee comfort, Yea, he giveth delights to thy soul.
ylt.29:18: Without a Vision is a people made naked, And whoso is keeping the law, O his happiness!
ylt.29:19: By words a servant is not instructed though he understand, And there is nothing answering.
ylt.29:20: Thou hast seen a man hasty in his words! More hope of a fool than of him.
ylt.29:21: Whoso is bringing up his servant delicately, from youth, At his latter end also he is continuator.
ylt.29:22: An angry man stirreth up contention, And a furious man is multiplying transgression.
ylt.29:23: The pride of man humbleth him, And humility of spirit upholdeth honour.
ylt.29:24: Whoso is sharing with a thief is hating his own soul, Execration he heareth, and telleth not.
ylt.29:25: Fear of man causeth a snare, And the confident in Jehovah is set on high.
ylt.29:26: Many are seeking the face of a ruler, And from Jehovah is the judgment of each.
ylt.29:27: An abomination to the righteous is the perverse man, And an abomination to the wicked is the upright in the way!
ylt.30:1: Words of a Gatherer, son of an obedient one, the declaration, an affirmation of the man: --I have wearied myself for God, I have wearied myself for God, and am consumed.
ylt.30:2: For I am more brutish than any one, And have not the understanding of a man.
ylt.30:3: Nor have I learned wisdom, Yet the knowledge of Holy Ones I know.
ylt.30:4: Who went up to heaven, and cometh down? Who hath gathered the wind in his fists? Who hath bound waters in a garment? Who established all ends of the earth? What is His name? and what His son's name? Surely thou knowest!
ylt.30:5: Every saying of God is tried, A shield He is to those trusting in Him.
ylt.30:6: Add not to His words, lest He reason with thee, And thou hast been found false.
ylt.30:7: Two things I have asked from Thee, Withhold not from me before I die.
ylt.30:8: Vanity and a lying word put far from me, Poverty or wealth give not to me, Cause me to eat the bread of my portion,
ylt.30:9: Lest I become satiated, and have denied, And have said, `Who is Jehovah?' And lest I be poor, and have stolen, And have laid hold of the name of my God.
ylt.30:10: Accuse not a servant unto his lord, Lest he disesteem thee, and thou be found guilty.
ylt.30:11: A generation is, that lightly esteemeth their father, And their mother doth not bless.
ylt.30:12: A generation--pure in their own eyes, But from their own filth not washed.
ylt.30:13: A generation--how high are their eyes, Yea, their eyelids are lifted up.
ylt.30:14: A generation--swords are their teeth, And knives--their jaw-teeth, To consume the poor from earth, And the needy from among men.
ylt.30:15: To the leech are two daughters, `Give, give, Lo, three things are not satisfied, Four have not said `Sufficiency;'
ylt.30:16: Sheol, and a restrained womb, Earth--it is not satisfied with water, And fire--it hath not said, `Sufficiency,'
ylt.30:17: An eye that mocketh at a father, And despiseth to obey a mother, Dig it out do ravens of the valley, And eat it do young eagles.
ylt.30:18: Three things have been too wonderful for me, Yea, four that I have not known:
ylt.30:19: The way of the eagle in the heavens, The way of a serpent on a rock, The way of a ship in the heart of the sea, And the way of a man in youth.
ylt.30:20: So--the way of an adulterous woman, She hath eaten and hath wiped her mouth, And hath said, `I have not done iniquity.'
ylt.30:21: For three things hath earth been troubled, And for four--it is not able to bear:
ylt.30:22: For a servant when he reigneth, And a fool when he is satisfied with bread,
ylt.30:23: For a hated one when she ruleth, And a maid-servant when she succeedeth her mistress.
ylt.30:24: Four are little ones of earth, And they are made wiser than the wise:
ylt.30:25: The ants are a people not strong, And they prepare in summer their food,
ylt.30:26: Conies are a people not strong, And they place in a rock their house,
ylt.30:27: A king there is not to the locust, And it goeth out--each one shouting,
ylt.30:28: A spider with two hands taketh hold, And is in the palaces of a king.
ylt.30:29: Three there are going well, Yea, four are good in going:
ylt.30:30: An old lion--mighty among beasts, That turneth not back from the face of any,
ylt.30:31: A girt one of the loins, or a he-goat, And a king--no rising up with him.
ylt.30:32: If thou hast been foolish in lifting up thyself, And if thou hast devised evil--hand to mouth!
ylt.30:33: For the churning of milk bringeth out butter, And the wringing of the nose bringeth out blood, And the forcing of anger bringeth out strife!
ylt.31:1: Words of Lemuel a king, a declaration that his mother taught him:
ylt.31:2: `What, my son? and what, son of my womb? And what, son of my vows?
ylt.31:3: Give not to women thy strength, And thy ways to wiping away of kings.
ylt.31:4: Not for kings, O Lemuel, Not for kings, to drink wine, And for princes a desire of strong drink.
ylt.31:5: Lest he drink, and forget the decree, And change the judgment of any of the sons of affliction.
ylt.31:6: Give strong drink to the perishing, And wine to the bitter in soul,
ylt.31:7: He drinketh, and forgetteth his poverty, And his misery he remembereth not again.
ylt.31:8: Open thy mouth for the dumb, For the right of all sons of change.
ylt.31:9: Open thy mouth, judge righteously, Both the cause of the poor and needy!'
ylt.31:10: A woman of worth who doth find? Yea, far above rubies is her price.
ylt.31:11: The heart of her husband hath trusted in her, And spoil he lacketh not.
ylt.31:12: She hath done him good, and not evil, All days of her life.
ylt.31:13: She hath sought wool and flax, And with delight she worketh with her hands.
ylt.31:14: She hath been as ships of the merchant, From afar she bringeth in her bread.
ylt.31:15: Yea, she riseth while yet night, And giveth food to her household, And a portion to her damsels.
ylt.31:16: She hath considered a field, and taketh it, From the fruit of her hands she hath planted a vineyard.
ylt.31:17: She hath girded with might her loins, And doth strengthen her arms.
ylt.31:18: She hath perceived when her merchandise is good, Her lamp is not extinguished in the night.
ylt.31:19: Her hands she hath sent forth on a spindle, And her hands have held a distaff.
ylt.31:20: Her hand she hath spread forth to the poor, Yea, her hands she sent forth to the needy.
ylt.31:21: She is not afraid of her household from snow, For all her household are clothed with scarlet.
ylt.31:22: Ornamental coverings she hath made for herself, Silk and purple are her clothing.
ylt.31:23: Known in the gates is her husband, In his sitting with elders of the land.
ylt.31:24: Linen garments she hath made, and selleth, And a girdle she hath given to the merchant.
ylt.31:25: Strength and honour are her clothing, And she rejoiceth at a latter day.
ylt.31:26: Her mouth she hath opened in wisdom, And the law of kindness is on her tongue.
ylt.31:27: She is watching the ways of her household, And bread of sloth she eateth not.
ylt.31:28: Her sons have risen up, and pronounce her happy, Her husband, and he praiseth her,
ylt.31:29: `Many are the daughters who have done worthily, Thou hast gone up above them all.'
ylt.31:30: The grace is false, and the beauty is vain, A woman fearing Jehovah, she may boast herself.
ylt.31:31: Give ye to her of the fruit of her hands, And her works do praise her in the gates!

web.1:1: The proverbs of Solomon, the son of David, king of Israel:
web.1:2: to know wisdom and instruction; to discern the words of understanding;
web.1:3: to receive instruction in wise dealing, in righteousness, justice, and equity;
web.1:4: to give prudence to the simple, knowledge and discretion to the young man:
web.1:5: that the wise man may hear, and increase in learning; that the man of understanding may attain to sound counsel:
web.1:6: to understand a proverb, and parables, the words and riddles of the wise.
web.1:7: The fear of Yahweh is the beginning of knowledge; but the foolish despise wisdom and instruction.
web.1:8: My son, listen to your father’s instruction, and don’t forsake your mother’s teaching:
web.1:9: for they will be a garland to grace your head, and chains around your neck.
web.1:10: My son, if sinners entice you, don’t consent.
web.1:11: If they say, “Come with us. Let’s lay in wait for blood. Let’s lurk secretly for the innocent without cause.
web.1:12: Let’s swallow them up alive like Sheol, and whole, like those who go down into the pit.
web.1:13: We’ll find all valuable wealth. We’ll fill our houses with plunder.
web.1:14: You shall cast your lot among us. We’ll all have one purse.”
web.1:15: My son, don’t walk on the path with them. Keep your foot from their path,
web.1:16: for their feet run to evil. They hurry to shed blood.
web.1:17: For the net is spread in vain in the sight of any bird;
web.1:18: but these lay in wait for their own blood. They lurk secretly for their own lives.
web.1:19: So are the ways of everyone who is greedy for gain. It takes away the life of its owners.
web.1:20: Wisdom calls aloud in the street. She utters her voice in the public squares.
web.1:21: She calls at the head of noisy places. At the entrance of the city gates, she utters her words:
web.1:22: “How long, you simple ones, will you love simplicity? How long will mockers delight themselves in mockery, and fools hate knowledge?
web.1:23: Turn at my reproof. Behold, I will pour out my spirit on you. I will make known my words to you.
web.1:24: Because I have called, and you have refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no one has paid attention;
web.1:25: but you have ignored all my counsel, and wanted none of my reproof;
web.1:26: I also will laugh at your disaster. I will mock when calamity overtakes you,
web.1:27: when calamity overtakes you like a storm, when your disaster comes on like a whirlwind, when distress and anguish come on you.
web.1:28: Then they will call on me, but I will not answer. They will seek me diligently, but they will not find me;
web.1:29: because they hated knowledge, and didn’t choose the fear of Yahweh.
web.1:30: They wanted none of my counsel. They despised all my reproof.
web.1:31: Therefore they will eat of the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own schemes.
web.1:32: For the backsliding of the simple will kill them. The careless ease of fools will destroy them.
web.1:33: But whoever listens to me will dwell securely, and will be at ease, without fear of harm.”
web.2:1: My son, if you will receive my words, and store up my commandments within you,
web.2:2: so as to turn your ear to wisdom, and apply your heart to understanding;
web.2:3: yes, if you call out for discernment, and lift up your voice for understanding;
web.2:4: if you seek her as silver, and search for her as for hidden treasures:
web.2:5: then you will understand the fear of Yahweh, and find the knowledge of God.
web.2:6: For Yahweh gives wisdom. Out of his mouth comes knowledge and understanding.
web.2:7: He lays up sound wisdom for the upright. He is a shield to those who walk in integrity,
web.2:8: that he may guard the paths of justice, and preserve the way of his saints.
web.2:9: Then you will understand righteousness and justice, equity and every good path.
web.2:10: For wisdom will enter into your heart. Knowledge will be pleasant to your soul.
web.2:11: Discretion will watch over you. Understanding will keep you,
web.2:12: to deliver you from the way of evil, from the men who speak perverse things,
web.2:13: who forsake the paths of uprightness, to walk in the ways of darkness,
web.2:14: who rejoice to do evil, and delight in the perverseness of evil,
web.2:15: who are crooked in their ways, and wayward in their paths,
web.2:16: to deliver you from the strange woman, even from the foreigner who flatters with her words,
web.2:17: who forsakes the friend of her youth, and forgets the covenant of her God;
web.2:18: for her house leads down to death, her paths to the departed spirits.
web.2:19: None who go to her return again, neither do they attain to the paths of life.
web.2:20: So you may walk in the way of good men, and keep the paths of the righteous.
web.2:21: For the upright will dwell in the land. The perfect will remain in it.
web.2:22: But the wicked will be cut off from the land. The treacherous will be rooted out of it.
web.3:1: My son, don’t forget my teaching; but let your heart keep my commandments:
web.3:2: for they will add to you length of days, years of life, and peace.
web.3:3: Don’t let kindness and truth forsake you. Bind them around your neck. Write them on the tablet of your heart.
web.3:4: So you will find favor, and good understanding in the sight of God and man.
web.3:5: Trust in Yahweh with all your heart, and don’t lean on your own understanding.
web.3:6: In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.
web.3:7: Don’t be wise in your own eyes. Fear Yahweh, and depart from evil.
web.3:8: It will be health to your body, and nourishment to your bones.
web.3:9: Honor Yahweh with your substance, with the first fruits of all your increase:
web.3:10: so your barns will be filled with plenty, and your vats will overflow with new wine.
web.3:11: My son, don’t despise Yahweh’s discipline, neither be weary of his correction;
web.3:12: for whom Yahweh loves, he corrects, even as a father reproves the son in whom he delights.
web.3:13: Happy is the man who finds wisdom, the man who gets understanding.
web.3:14: For her good profit is better than getting silver, and her return is better than fine gold.
web.3:15: She is more precious than rubies. None of the things you can desire are to be compared to her.
web.3:16: Length of days is in her right hand. In her left hand are riches and honor.
web.3:17: Her ways are ways of pleasantness. All her paths are peace.
web.3:18: She is a tree of life to those who lay hold of her. Happy is everyone who retains her.
web.3:19: By wisdom Yahweh founded the earth. By understanding, he established the heavens.
web.3:20: By his knowledge, the depths were broken up, and the skies drop down the dew.
web.3:21: My son, let them not depart from your eyes. Keep sound wisdom and discretion:
web.3:22: so they will be life to your soul, and grace for your neck.
web.3:23: Then you shall walk in your way securely. Your foot won’t stumble.
web.3:24: When you lie down, you will not be afraid. Yes, you will lie down, and your sleep will be sweet.
web.3:25: Don’t be afraid of sudden fear, neither of the desolation of the wicked, when it comes;
web.3:26: for Yahweh will be your confidence, and will keep your foot from being taken.
web.3:27: Don’t withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in the power of your hand to do it.
web.3:28: Don’t say to your neighbor, “Go, and come again; tomorrow I will give it to you,” when you have it by you.
web.3:29: Don’t devise evil against your neighbor, since he dwells securely by you.
web.3:30: Don’t strive with a man without cause, if he has done you no harm.
web.3:31: Don’t envy the man of violence. Choose none of his ways.
web.3:32: For the perverse is an abomination to Yahweh, but his friendship is with the upright.
web.3:33: Yahweh’s curse is in the house of the wicked, but he blesses the habitation of the righteous.
web.3:34: Surely he mocks the mockers, but he gives grace to the humble.
web.3:35: The wise will inherit glory, but shame will be the promotion of fools.
web.4:1: Listen, sons, to a father’s instruction. Pay attention and know understanding;
web.4:2: for I give you sound learning. Don’t forsake my law.
web.4:3: For I was a son to my father, tender and an only child in the sight of my mother.
web.4:4: He taught me, and said to me: “Let your heart retain my words. Keep my commandments, and live.
web.4:5: Get wisdom. Get understanding. Don’t forget, and don’t deviate from the words of my mouth.
web.4:6: Don’t forsake her, and she will preserve you. Love her, and she will keep you.
web.4:7: Wisdom is supreme. Get wisdom. Yes, though it costs all your possessions, get understanding.
web.4:8: Esteem her, and she will exalt you. She will bring you to honor when you embrace her.
web.4:9: She will give to your head a garland of grace. She will deliver a crown of splendor to you.”
web.4:10: Listen, my son, and receive my sayings. The years of your life will be many.
web.4:11: I have taught you in the way of wisdom. I have led you in straight paths.
web.4:12: When you go, your steps will not be hampered. When you run, you will not stumble.
web.4:13: Take firm hold of instruction. Don’t let her go. Keep her, for she is your life.
web.4:14: Don’t enter into the path of the wicked. Don’t walk in the way of evil men.
web.4:15: Avoid it, and don’t pass by it. Turn from it, and pass on.
web.4:16: For they don’t sleep unless they do evil. Their sleep is taken away, unless they make someone fall.
web.4:17: For they eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence.
web.4:18: But the path of the righteous is like the dawning light that shines more and more until the perfect day.
web.4:19: The way of the wicked is like darkness. They don’t know what they stumble over.
web.4:20: My son, attend to my words. Turn your ear to my sayings.
web.4:21: Let them not depart from your eyes. Keep them in the center of your heart.
web.4:22: For they are life to those who find them, and health to their whole body.
web.4:23: Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.
web.4:24: Put away from yourself a perverse mouth. Put corrupt lips far from you.
web.4:25: Let your eyes look straight ahead. Fix your gaze directly before you.
web.4:26: Make the path of your feet level. Let all of your ways be established.
web.4:27: Don’t turn to the right hand nor to the left. Remove your foot from evil.
web.5:1: My son, pay attention to my wisdom. Turn your ear to my understanding,
web.5:2: that you may maintain discretion, that your lips may preserve knowledge.
web.5:3: For the lips of an adulteress drip honey. Her mouth is smoother than oil,
web.5:4: but in the end she is as bitter as wormwood, and as sharp as a two-edged sword.
web.5:5: Her feet go down to death. Her steps lead straight to Sheol.
web.5:6: She gives no thought to the way of life. Her ways are crooked, and she doesn’t know it.
web.5:7: Now therefore, my sons, listen to me. Don’t depart from the words of my mouth.
web.5:8: Remove your way far from her. Don’t come near the door of her house,
web.5:9: lest you give your honor to others, and your years to the cruel one;
web.5:10: lest strangers feast on your wealth, and your labors enrich another man’s house.
web.5:11: You will groan at your latter end, when your flesh and your body are consumed,
web.5:12: and say, “How I have hated instruction, and my heart despised reproof;
web.5:13: neither have I obeyed the voice of my teachers, nor turned my ear to those who instructed me!
web.5:14: I have come to the brink of utter ruin, among the gathered assembly.”
web.5:15: Drink water out of your own cistern, running water out of your own well.
web.5:16: Should your springs overflow in the streets, streams of water in the public squares?
web.5:17: Let them be for yourself alone, not for strangers with you.
web.5:18: Let your spring be blessed. Rejoice in the wife of your youth.
web.5:19: A loving doe and a graceful deer— let her breasts satisfy you at all times. Be captivated always with her love.
web.5:20: For why should you, my son, be captivated with an adulteress? Why embrace the bosom of another?
web.5:21: For the ways of man are before Yahweh’s eyes. He examines all his paths.
web.5:22: The evil deeds of the wicked ensnare him. The cords of his sin hold him firmly.
web.5:23: He will die for lack of instruction. In the greatness of his folly, he will go astray.
web.6:1: My son, if you have become collateral for your neighbor, if you have struck your hands in pledge for a stranger,
web.6:2: you are trapped by the words of your mouth; you are ensnared with the words of your mouth.
web.6:3: Do this now, my son, and deliver yourself, since you have come into the hand of your neighbor. Go, humble yourself. Press your plea with your neighbor.
web.6:4: Give no sleep to your eyes, nor slumber to your eyelids.
web.6:5: Free yourself, like a gazelle from the hand of the hunter, like a bird from the snare of the fowler.
web.6:6: Go to the ant, you sluggard. Consider her ways, and be wise;
web.6:7: which having no chief, overseer, or ruler,
web.6:8: provides her bread in the summer, and gathers her food in the harvest.
web.6:9: How long will you sleep, sluggard? When will you arise out of your sleep?
web.6:10: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep:
web.6:11: so your poverty will come as a robber, and your scarcity as an armed man.
web.6:12: A worthless person, a man of iniquity, is he who walks with a perverse mouth,
web.6:13: who winks with his eyes, who signals with his feet, who motions with his fingers,
web.6:14: in whose heart is perverseness, who devises evil continually, who always sows discord.
web.6:15: Therefore his calamity will come suddenly. He will be broken suddenly, and that without remedy.
web.6:16: There are six things which Yahweh hates; yes, seven which are an abomination to him:
web.6:17: arrogant eyes, a lying tongue, hands that shed innocent blood,
web.6:18: a heart that devises wicked schemes, feet that are swift in running to mischief,
web.6:19: a false witness who utters lies, and he who sows discord among brothers.
web.6:20: My son, keep your father’s commandment, and don’t forsake your mother’s teaching.
web.6:21: Bind them continually on your heart. Tie them around your neck.
web.6:22: When you walk, it will lead you. When you sleep, it will watch over you. When you awake, it will talk with you.
web.6:23: For the commandment is a lamp, and the law is light. Reproofs of instruction are the way of life,
web.6:24: to keep you from the immoral woman, from the flattery of the wayward wife’s tongue.
web.6:25: Don’t lust after her beauty in your heart, neither let her captivate you with her eyelids.
web.6:26: For a prostitute reduces you to a piece of bread. The adulteress hunts for your precious life.
web.6:27: Can a man scoop fire into his lap, and his clothes not be burned?
web.6:28: Or can one walk on hot coals, and his feet not be scorched?
web.6:29: So is he who goes in to his neighbor’s wife. Whoever touches her will not be unpunished.
web.6:30: Men don’t despise a thief if he steals to satisfy himself when he is hungry;
web.6:31: but if he is found, he shall restore seven times. He shall give all the wealth of his house.
web.6:32: He who commits adultery with a woman is void of understanding. He who does it destroys his own soul.
web.6:33: He will get wounds and dishonor. His reproach will not be wiped away.
web.6:34: For jealousy arouses the fury of the husband. He won’t spare in the day of vengeance.
web.6:35: He won’t regard any ransom, neither will he rest content, though you give many gifts.
web.7:1: My son, keep my words. Lay up my commandments within you.
web.7:2: Keep my commandments and live! Guard my teaching as the apple of your eye.
web.7:3: Bind them on your fingers. Write them on the tablet of your heart.
web.7:4: Tell wisdom, “You are my sister.” Call understanding your relative,
web.7:5: that they may keep you from the strange woman, from the foreigner who flatters with her words.
web.7:6: For at the window of my house, I looked out through my lattice.
web.7:7: I saw among the simple ones. I discerned among the youths a young man void of understanding,
web.7:8: passing through the street near her corner, he went the way to her house,
web.7:9: in the twilight, in the evening of the day, in the middle of the night and in the darkness.
web.7:10: Behold, there a woman met him with the attire of a prostitute, and with crafty intent.
web.7:11: She is loud and defiant. Her feet don’t stay in her house.
web.7:12: Now she is in the streets, now in the squares, and lurking at every corner.
web.7:13: So she caught him, and kissed him. With an impudent face she said to him:
web.7:14: “Sacrifices of peace offerings are with me. Today I have paid my vows.
web.7:15: Therefore I came out to meet you, to diligently seek your face, and I have found you.
web.7:16: I have spread my couch with carpets of tapestry, with striped cloths of the yarn of Egypt.
web.7:17: I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.
web.7:18: Come, let’s take our fill of loving until the morning. Let’s solace ourselves with loving.
web.7:19: For my husband isn’t at home. He has gone on a long journey.
web.7:20: He has taken a bag of money with him. He will come home at the full moon.”
web.7:21: With persuasive words, she led him astray. With the flattering of her lips, she seduced him.
web.7:22: He followed her immediately, as an ox goes to the slaughter, as a fool stepping into a noose.
web.7:23: Until an arrow strikes through his liver, as a bird hurries to the snare, and doesn’t know that it will cost his life.
web.7:24: Now therefore, sons, listen to me. Pay attention to the words of my mouth.
web.7:25: Don’t let your heart turn to her ways. Don’t go astray in her paths,
web.7:26: for she has thrown down many wounded. Yes, all her slain are a mighty army.
web.7:27: Her house is the way to Sheol, going down to the rooms of death.
web.8:1: Doesn’t wisdom cry out? Doesn’t understanding raise her voice?
web.8:2: On the top of high places by the way, where the paths meet, she stands.
web.8:3: Beside the gates, at the entry of the city, at the entry doors, she cries aloud:
web.8:4: “I call to you men! I send my voice to the sons of mankind.
web.8:5: You simple, understand prudence! You fools, be of an understanding heart!
web.8:6: Hear, for I will speak excellent things. The opening of my lips is for right things.
web.8:7: For my mouth speaks truth. Wickedness is an abomination to my lips.
web.8:8: All the words of my mouth are in righteousness. There is nothing crooked or perverse in them.
web.8:9: They are all plain to him who understands, right to those who find knowledge.
web.8:10: Receive my instruction rather than silver, knowledge rather than choice gold.
web.8:11: For wisdom is better than rubies. All the things that may be desired can’t be compared to it.
web.8:12: “I, wisdom, have made prudence my dwelling. Find out knowledge and discretion.
web.8:13: The fear of Yahweh is to hate evil. I hate pride, arrogance, the evil way, and the perverse mouth.
web.8:14: Counsel and sound knowledge are mine. I have understanding and power.
web.8:15: By me kings reign, and princes decree justice.
web.8:16: By me princes rule, nobles, and all the righteous rulers of the earth.
web.8:17: I love those who love me. Those who seek me diligently will find me.
web.8:18: With me are riches, honor, enduring wealth, and prosperity.
web.8:19: My fruit is better than gold, yes, than fine gold, my yield than choice silver.
web.8:20: I walk in the way of righteousness, in the middle of the paths of justice,
web.8:21: that I may give wealth to those who love me. I fill their treasuries.
web.8:22: “Yahweh possessed me in the beginning of his work, before his deeds of old.
web.8:23: I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, before the earth existed.
web.8:24: When there were no depths, I was born, when there were no springs abounding with water.
web.8:25: Before the mountains were settled in place, before the hills, I was born;
web.8:26: while as yet he had not made the earth, nor the fields, nor the beginning of the dust of the world.
web.8:27: When he established the heavens, I was there. When he set a circle on the surface of the deep,
web.8:28: when he established the clouds above, when the springs of the deep became strong,
web.8:29: when he gave to the sea its boundary, that the waters should not violate his commandment, when he marked out the foundations of the earth,
web.8:30: then I was the craftsman by his side. I was a delight day by day, always rejoicing before him,
web.8:31: rejoicing in his whole world. My delight was with the sons of men.
web.8:32: “Now therefore, my sons, listen to me, for blessed are those who keep my ways.
web.8:33: Hear instruction, and be wise. Don’t refuse it.
web.8:34: Blessed is the man who hears me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at my door posts.
web.8:35: For whoever finds me, finds life, and will obtain favor from Yahweh.
web.8:36: But he who sins against me wrongs his own soul. All those who hate me love death.”
web.9:1: Wisdom has built her house. She has carved out her seven pillars.
web.9:2: She has prepared her meat. She has mixed her wine. She has also set her table.
web.9:3: She has sent out her maidens. She cries from the highest places of the city:
web.9:4: “Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!” As for him who is void of understanding, she says to him,
web.9:5: “Come, eat some of my bread, Drink some of the wine which I have mixed!
web.9:6: Leave your simple ways, and live. Walk in the way of understanding.”
web.9:7: One who corrects a mocker invites insult. One who reproves a wicked man invites abuse.
web.9:8: Don’t reprove a scoffer, lest he hate you. Reprove a wise person, and he will love you.
web.9:9: Instruct a wise person, and he will be still wiser. Teach a righteous person, and he will increase in learning.
web.9:10: The fear of Yahweh is the beginning of wisdom. The knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.
web.9:11: For by me your days will be multiplied. The years of your life will be increased.
web.9:12: If you are wise, you are wise for yourself. If you mock, you alone will bear it.
web.9:13: The foolish woman is loud, undisciplined, and knows nothing.
web.9:14: She sits at the door of her house, on a seat in the high places of the city,
web.9:15: to call to those who pass by, who go straight on their ways,
web.9:16: “Whoever is simple, let him turn in here.” as for him who is void of understanding, she says to him,
web.9:17: “Stolen water is sweet. Food eaten in secret is pleasant.”
web.9:18: But he doesn’t know that the departed spirits are there, that her guests are in the depths of Sheol.
web.10:1: The proverbs of Solomon. A wise son makes a glad father; but a foolish son brings grief to his mother.
web.10:2: Treasures of wickedness profit nothing, but righteousness delivers from death.
web.10:3: Yahweh will not allow the soul of the righteous to go hungry, but he thrusts away the desire of the wicked.
web.10:4: He becomes poor who works with a lazy hand, but the hand of the diligent brings wealth.
web.10:5: He who gathers in summer is a wise son, but he who sleeps during the harvest is a son who causes shame.
web.10:6: Blessings are on the head of the righteous, but violence covers the mouth of the wicked.
web.10:7: The memory of the righteous is blessed, but the name of the wicked will rot.
web.10:8: The wise in heart accept commandments, but a chattering fool will fall.
web.10:9: He who walks blamelessly walks surely, but he who perverts his ways will be found out.
web.10:10: One winking with the eye causes sorrow, but a chattering fool will fall.
web.10:11: The mouth of the righteous is a spring of life, but violence covers the mouth of the wicked.
web.10:12: Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all wrongs.
web.10:13: Wisdom is found on the lips of him who has discernment, but a rod is for the back of him who is void of understanding.
web.10:14: Wise men lay up knowledge, but the mouth of the foolish is near ruin.
web.10:15: The rich man’s wealth is his strong city. The destruction of the poor is their poverty.
web.10:16: The labor of the righteous leads to life. The increase of the wicked leads to sin.
web.10:17: He is in the way of life who heeds correction, but he who forsakes reproof leads others astray.
web.10:18: He who hides hatred has lying lips. He who utters a slander is a fool.
web.10:19: In the multitude of words there is no lack of disobedience, but he who restrains his lips does wisely.
web.10:20: The tongue of the righteous is like choice silver. The heart of the wicked is of little worth.
web.10:21: The lips of the righteous feed many, but the foolish die for lack of understanding.
web.10:22: Yahweh’s blessing brings wealth, and he adds no trouble to it.
web.10:23: It is a fool’s pleasure to do wickedness, but wisdom is a man of understanding’s pleasure.
web.10:24: What the wicked fear, will overtake them, but the desire of the righteous will be granted.
web.10:25: When the whirlwind passes, the wicked is no more; but the righteous stand firm forever.
web.10:26: As vinegar to the teeth, and as smoke to the eyes, so is the sluggard to those who send him.
web.10:27: The fear of Yahweh prolongs days, but the years of the wicked shall be shortened.
web.10:28: The prospect of the righteous is joy, but the hope of the wicked will perish.
web.10:29: The way of Yahweh is a stronghold to the upright, but it is a destruction to the workers of iniquity.
web.10:30: The righteous will never be removed, but the wicked will not dwell in the land.
web.10:31: The mouth of the righteous produces wisdom, but the perverse tongue will be cut off.
web.10:32: The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable, but the mouth of the wicked is perverse.
web.11:1: A false balance is an abomination to Yahweh, but accurate weights are his delight.
web.11:2: When pride comes, then comes shame, but with humility comes wisdom.
web.11:3: The integrity of the upright shall guide them, but the perverseness of the treacherous shall destroy them.
web.11:4: Riches don’t profit in the day of wrath, but righteousness delivers from death.
web.11:5: The righteousness of the blameless will direct his way, but the wicked shall fall by his own wickedness.
web.11:6: The righteousness of the upright shall deliver them, but the unfaithful will be trapped by evil desires.
web.11:7: When a wicked man dies, hope perishes, and expectation of power comes to nothing.
web.11:8: A righteous person is delivered out of trouble, and the wicked takes his place.
web.11:9: With his mouth the godless man destroys his neighbor, but the righteous will be delivered through knowledge.
web.11:10: When it goes well with the righteous, the city rejoices. When the wicked perish, there is shouting.
web.11:11: By the blessing of the upright, the city is exalted, but it is overthrown by the mouth of the wicked.
web.11:12: One who despises his neighbor is void of wisdom, but a man of understanding holds his peace.
web.11:13: One who brings gossip betrays a confidence, but one who is of a trustworthy spirit is one who keeps a secret.
web.11:14: Where there is no wise guidance, the nation falls, but in the multitude of counselors there is victory.
web.11:15: He who is collateral for a stranger will suffer for it, but he who refuses pledges of collateral is secure.
web.11:16: A gracious woman obtains honor, but violent men obtain riches.
web.11:17: The merciful man does good to his own soul, but he who is cruel troubles his own flesh.
web.11:18: Wicked people earn deceitful wages, but one who sows righteousness reaps a sure reward.
web.11:19: He who is truly righteous gets life. He who pursues evil gets death.
web.11:20: Those who are perverse in heart are an abomination to Yahweh, but those whose ways are blameless are his delight.
web.11:21: Most certainly, the evil man will not be unpunished, but the offspring of the righteous will be delivered.
web.11:22: Like a gold ring in a pig’s snout, is a beautiful woman who lacks discretion.
web.11:23: The desire of the righteous is only good. The expectation of the wicked is wrath.
web.11:24: There is one who scatters, and increases yet more. There is one who withholds more than is appropriate, but gains poverty.
web.11:25: The liberal soul shall be made fat. He who waters shall be watered also himself.
web.11:26: People curse someone who withholds grain, but blessing will be on the head of him who sells it.
web.11:27: He who diligently seeks good seeks favor, but he who searches after evil, it shall come to him.
web.11:28: He who trusts in his riches will fall, but the righteous shall flourish as the green leaf.
web.11:29: He who troubles his own house shall inherit the wind. The foolish shall be servant to the wise of heart.
web.11:30: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life. He who is wise wins souls.
web.11:31: Behold, the righteous shall be repaid in the earth, how much more the wicked and the sinner!
web.12:1: Whoever loves correction loves knowledge, but he who hates reproof is stupid.
web.12:2: A good man shall obtain favor from Yahweh, but he will condemn a man of wicked plans.
web.12:3: A man shall not be established by wickedness, but the root of the righteous shall not be moved.
web.12:4: A worthy woman is the crown of her husband, but a disgraceful wife is as rottenness in his bones.
web.12:5: The thoughts of the righteous are just, but the advice of the wicked is deceitful.
web.12:6: The words of the wicked are about lying in wait for blood, but the speech of the upright rescues them.
web.12:7: The wicked are overthrown, and are no more, but the house of the righteous shall stand.
web.12:8: A man shall be commended according to his wisdom, but he who has a warped mind shall be despised.
web.12:9: Better is he who is little known, and has a servant, than he who honors himself, and lacks bread.
web.12:10: A righteous man respects the life of his animal, but the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel.
web.12:11: He who tills his land shall have plenty of bread, but he who chases fantasies is void of understanding.
web.12:12: The wicked desires the plunder of evil men, but the root of the righteous flourishes.
web.12:13: An evil man is trapped by sinfulness of lips, but the righteous shall come out of trouble.
web.12:14: A man shall be satisfied with good by the fruit of his mouth. The work of a man’s hands shall be rewarded to him.
web.12:15: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but he who is wise listens to counsel.
web.12:16: A fool shows his annoyance the same day, but one who overlooks an insult is prudent.
web.12:17: He who is truthful testifies honestly, but a false witness lies.
web.12:18: There is one who speaks rashly like the piercing of a sword, but the tongue of the wise heals.
web.12:19: Truth’s lips will be established forever, but a lying tongue is only momentary.
web.12:20: Deceit is in the heart of those who plot evil, but joy comes to the promoters of peace.
web.12:21: No mischief shall happen to the righteous, but the wicked shall be filled with evil.
web.12:22: Lying lips are an abomination to Yahweh, but those who do the truth are his delight.
web.12:23: A prudent man keeps his knowledge, but the hearts of fools proclaim foolishness.
web.12:24: The hands of the diligent ones shall rule, but laziness ends in slave labor.
web.12:25: Anxiety in a man’s heart weighs it down, but a kind word makes it glad.
web.12:26: A righteous person is cautious in friendship, but the way of the wicked leads them astray.
web.12:27: The slothful man doesn’t roast his game, but the possessions of diligent men are prized.
web.12:28: In the way of righteousness is life; in its path there is no death.
web.13:1: A wise son listens to his father’s instruction, but a scoffer doesn’t listen to rebuke.
web.13:2: By the fruit of his lips, a man enjoys good things, but the unfaithful crave violence.
web.13:3: He who guards his mouth guards his soul. One who opens wide his lips comes to ruin.
web.13:4: The soul of the sluggard desires, and has nothing, but the desire of the diligent shall be fully satisfied.
web.13:5: A righteous man hates lies, but a wicked man brings shame and disgrace.
web.13:6: Righteousness guards the way of integrity, but wickedness overthrows the sinner.
web.13:7: There are some who pretend to be rich, yet have nothing. There are some who pretend to be poor, yet have great wealth.
web.13:8: The ransom of a man’s life is his riches, but the poor hear no threats.
web.13:9: The light of the righteous shines brightly, but the lamp of the wicked is snuffed out.
web.13:10: Pride only breeds quarrels, but wisdom is with people who take advice.
web.13:11: Wealth gained dishonestly dwindles away, but he who gathers by hand makes it grow.
web.13:12: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but when longing is fulfilled, it is a tree of life.
web.13:13: Whoever despises instruction will pay for it, but he who respects a command will be rewarded.
web.13:14: The teaching of the wise is a spring of life, to turn from the snares of death.
web.13:15: Good understanding wins favor, but the way of the unfaithful is hard.
web.13:16: Every prudent man acts from knowledge, but a fool exposes folly.
web.13:17: A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a trustworthy envoy gains healing.
web.13:18: Poverty and shame come to him who refuses discipline, but he who heeds correction shall be honored.
web.13:19: Longing fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but fools detest turning from evil.
web.13:20: One who walks with wise men grows wise, but a companion of fools suffers harm.
web.13:21: Misfortune pursues sinners, but prosperity rewards the righteous.
web.13:22: A good man leaves an inheritance to his children’s children, but the wealth of the sinner is stored for the righteous.
web.13:23: An abundance of food is in poor people’s fields, but injustice sweeps it away.
web.13:24: One who spares the rod hates his son, but one who loves him is careful to discipline him.
web.13:25: The righteous one eats to the satisfying of his soul, but the belly of the wicked goes hungry.
web.14:1: Every wise woman builds her house, but the foolish one tears it down with her own hands.
web.14:2: He who walks in his uprightness fears Yahweh, but he who is perverse in his ways despises him.
web.14:3: The fool’s talk brings a rod to his back, but the lips of the wise protect them.
web.14:4: Where no oxen are, the crib is clean, but much increase is by the strength of the ox.
web.14:5: A truthful witness will not lie, but a false witness pours out lies.
web.14:6: A scoffer seeks wisdom, and doesn’t find it, but knowledge comes easily to a discerning person.
web.14:7: Stay away from a foolish man, for you won’t find knowledge on his lips.
web.14:8: The wisdom of the prudent is to think about his way, but the folly of fools is deceit.
web.14:9: Fools mock at making atonement for sins, but among the upright there is good will.
web.14:10: The heart knows its own bitterness and joy; he will not share these with a stranger.
web.14:11: The house of the wicked will be overthrown, but the tent of the upright will flourish.
web.14:12: There is a way which seems right to a man, but in the end it leads to death.
web.14:13: Even in laughter the heart may be sorrowful, and mirth may end in heaviness.
web.14:14: The unfaithful will be repaid for his own ways; likewise a good man will be rewarded for his ways.
web.14:15: A simple man believes everything, but the prudent man carefully considers his ways.
web.14:16: A wise man fears and shuns evil, but the fool is hot headed and reckless.
web.14:17: He who is quick to become angry will commit folly, and a crafty man is hated.
web.14:18: The simple inherit folly, but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
web.14:19: The evil bow down before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
web.14:20: The poor person is shunned even by his own neighbor, but the rich person has many friends.
web.14:21: He who despises his neighbor sins, but he who has pity on the poor is blessed.
web.14:22: Don’t they go astray who plot evil? But love and faithfulness belong to those who plan good.
web.14:23: In all hard work there is profit, but the talk of the lips leads only to poverty.
web.14:24: The crown of the wise is their riches, but the folly of fools crowns them with folly.
web.14:25: A truthful witness saves souls, but a false witness is deceitful.
web.14:26: In the fear of Yahweh is a secure fortress, and he will be a refuge for his children.
web.14:27: The fear of Yahweh is a fountain of life, turning people from the snares of death.
web.14:28: In the multitude of people is the king’s glory, but in the lack of people is the destruction of the prince.
web.14:29: He who is slow to anger has great understanding, but he who has a quick temper displays folly.
web.14:30: The life of the body is a heart at peace, but envy rots the bones.
web.14:31: He who oppresses the poor shows contempt for his Maker, but he who is kind to the needy honors him.
web.14:32: The wicked is brought down in his calamity, but in death, the righteous has a refuge.
web.14:33: Wisdom rests in the heart of one who has understanding, and is even made known in the inward part of fools.
web.14:34: Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a disgrace to any people.
web.14:35: The king’s favor is toward a servant who deals wisely, but his wrath is toward one who causes shame.
web.15:1: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
web.15:2: The tongue of the wise commends knowledge, but the mouth of fools gush out folly.
web.15:3: Yahweh’s eyes are everywhere, keeping watch on the evil and the good.
web.15:4: A gentle tongue is a tree of life, but deceit in it crushes the spirit.
web.15:5: A fool despises his father’s correction, but he who heeds reproof shows prudence.
web.15:6: In the house of the righteous is much treasure, but the income of the wicked brings trouble.
web.15:7: The lips of the wise spread knowledge; not so with the heart of fools.
web.15:8: The sacrifice made by the wicked is an abomination to Yahweh, but the prayer of the upright is his delight.
web.15:9: The way of the wicked is an abomination to Yahweh, but he loves him who follows after righteousness.
web.15:10: There is stern discipline for one who forsakes the way: whoever hates reproof shall die.
web.15:11: Sheol and Abaddon are before Yahweh— how much more then the hearts of the children of men!
web.15:12: A scoffer doesn’t love to be reproved; he will not go to the wise.
web.15:13: A glad heart makes a cheerful face, but an aching heart breaks the spirit.
web.15:14: The heart of one who has understanding seeks knowledge, but the mouths of fools feed on folly.
web.15:15: All the days of the afflicted are wretched, but one who has a cheerful heart enjoys a continual feast.
web.15:16: Better is little, with the fear of Yahweh, than great treasure with trouble.
web.15:17: Better is a dinner of herbs, where love is, than a fattened calf with hatred.
web.15:18: A wrathful man stirs up contention, but one who is slow to anger appeases strife.
web.15:19: The way of the sluggard is like a thorn patch, but the path of the upright is a highway.
web.15:20: A wise son makes a father glad, but a foolish man despises his mother.
web.15:21: Folly is joy to one who is void of wisdom, but a man of understanding keeps his way straight.
web.15:22: Where there is no counsel, plans fail; but in a multitude of counselors they are established.
web.15:23: Joy comes to a man with the reply of his mouth. How good is a word at the right time!
web.15:24: The path of life leads upward for the wise, to keep him from going downward to Sheol.
web.15:25: Yahweh will uproot the house of the proud, but he will keep the widow’s borders intact.
web.15:26: Yahweh detests the thoughts of the wicked, but the thoughts of the pure are pleasing.
web.15:27: He who is greedy for gain troubles his own house, but he who hates bribes will live.
web.15:28: The heart of the righteous weighs answers, but the mouth of the wicked gushes out evil.
web.15:29: Yahweh is far from the wicked, but he hears the prayer of the righteous.
web.15:30: The light of the eyes rejoices the heart. Good news gives health to the bones.
web.15:31: The ear that listens to reproof lives, and will be at home among the wise.
web.15:32: He who refuses correction despises his own soul, but he who listens to reproof gets understanding.
web.15:33: The fear of Yahweh teaches wisdom. Before honor is humility.
web.16:1: The plans of the heart belong to man, but the answer of the tongue is from Yahweh.
web.16:2: All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes; but Yahweh weighs the motives.
web.16:3: Commit your deeds to Yahweh, and your plans shall succeed.
web.16:4: Yahweh has made everything for its own end— yes, even the wicked for the day of evil.
web.16:5: Everyone who is proud in heart is an abomination to Yahweh: they shall certainly not be unpunished.
web.16:6: By mercy and truth iniquity is atoned for. By the fear of Yahweh men depart from evil.
web.16:7: When a man’s ways please Yahweh, he makes even his enemies to be at peace with him.
web.16:8: Better is a little with righteousness, than great revenues with injustice.
web.16:9: A man’s heart plans his course, but Yahweh directs his steps.
web.16:10: Inspired judgments are on the lips of the king. He shall not betray his mouth.
web.16:11: Honest balances and scales are Yahweh’s; all the weights in the bag are his work.
web.16:12: It is an abomination for kings to do wrong, for the throne is established by righteousness.
web.16:13: Righteous lips are the delight of kings. They value one who speaks the truth.
web.16:14: The king’s wrath is a messenger of death, but a wise man will pacify it.
web.16:15: In the light of the king’s face is life. His favor is like a cloud of the spring rain.
web.16:16: How much better it is to get wisdom than gold! Yes, to get understanding is to be chosen rather than silver.
web.16:17: The highway of the upright is to depart from evil. He who keeps his way preserves his soul.
web.16:18: Pride goes before destruction, and an arrogant spirit before a fall.
web.16:19: It is better to be of a lowly spirit with the poor, than to divide the plunder with the proud.
web.16:20: He who heeds the Word finds prosperity. Whoever trusts in Yahweh is blessed.
web.16:21: The wise in heart shall be called prudent. Pleasantness of the lips promotes instruction.
web.16:22: Understanding is a fountain of life to one who has it, but the punishment of fools is their folly.
web.16:23: The heart of the wise instructs his mouth, and adds learning to his lips.
web.16:24: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
web.16:25: There is a way which seems right to a man, but in the end it leads to death.
web.16:26: The appetite of the laboring man labors for him; for his mouth urges him on.
web.16:27: A worthless man devises mischief. His speech is like a scorching fire.
web.16:28: A perverse man stirs up strife. A whisperer separates close friends.
web.16:29: A man of violence entices his neighbor, and leads him in a way that is not good.
web.16:30: One who winks his eyes to plot perversities, one who compresses his lips, is bent on evil.
web.16:31: Gray hair is a crown of glory. It is attained by a life of righteousness.
web.16:32: One who is slow to anger is better than the mighty; one who rules his spirit, than he who takes a city.
web.16:33: The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from Yahweh.
web.17:1: Better is a dry morsel with quietness, than a house full of feasting with strife.
web.17:2: A servant who deals wisely will rule over a son who causes shame, and shall have a part in the inheritance among the brothers.
web.17:3: The refining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold, but Yahweh tests the hearts.
web.17:4: An evildoer heeds wicked lips. A liar gives ear to a mischievous tongue.
web.17:5: Whoever mocks the poor reproaches his Maker. He who is glad at calamity shall not be unpunished.
web.17:6: Children’s children are the crown of old men; the glory of children are their parents.
web.17:7: Arrogant speech isn’t fitting for a fool, much less do lying lips fit a prince.
web.17:8: A bribe is a precious stone in the eyes of him who gives it; wherever he turns, he prospers.
web.17:9: He who covers an offense promotes love; but he who repeats a matter separates best friends.
web.17:10: A rebuke enters deeper into one who has understanding than a hundred lashes into a fool.
web.17:11: An evil man seeks only rebellion; therefore a cruel messenger shall be sent against him.
web.17:12: Let a bear robbed of her cubs meet a man, rather than a fool in his folly.
web.17:13: Whoever rewards evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house.
web.17:14: The beginning of strife is like breaching a dam, therefore stop contention before quarreling breaks out.
web.17:15: He who justifies the wicked, and he who condemns the righteous, both of them alike are an abomination to Yahweh.
web.17:16: Why is there money in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom, since he has no understanding?
web.17:17: A friend loves at all times; and a brother is born for adversity.
web.17:18: A man void of understanding strikes hands, and becomes collateral in the presence of his neighbor.
web.17:19: He who loves disobedience loves strife. One who builds a high gate seeks destruction.
web.17:20: One who has a perverse heart doesn’t find prosperity, and one who has a deceitful tongue falls into trouble.
web.17:21: He who becomes the father of a fool grieves. The father of a fool has no joy.
web.17:22: A cheerful heart makes good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.
web.17:23: A wicked man receives a bribe in secret, to pervert the ways of justice.
web.17:24: Wisdom is before the face of one who has understanding, but the eyes of a fool wander to the ends of the earth.
web.17:25: A foolish son brings grief to his father, and bitterness to her who bore him.
web.17:26: Also to punish the righteous is not good, nor to flog officials for their integrity.
web.17:27: He who spares his words has knowledge. He who is even tempered is a man of understanding.
web.17:28: Even a fool, when he keeps silent, is counted wise. When he shuts his lips, he is thought to be discerning.
web.18:1: A man who isolates himself pursues selfishness, and defies all sound judgment.
web.18:2: A fool has no delight in understanding, but only in revealing his own opinion.
web.18:3: When wickedness comes, contempt also comes, and with shame comes disgrace.
web.18:4: The words of a man’s mouth are like deep waters. The fountain of wisdom is like a flowing brook.
web.18:5: To be partial to the faces of the wicked is not good, nor to deprive the innocent of justice.
web.18:6: A fool’s lips come into strife, and his mouth invites beatings.
web.18:7: A fool’s mouth is his destruction, and his lips are a snare to his soul.
